# Decision log

Every decision of the owner, and every change to how a calculation or a
format works, is recorded here with its date, newest first. The theory
pages, the user guide and the [data model](data-model.md) describe the
result; this page says *what was decided, when and why*. Nothing here is
approved as finished: everything is built and in active development
(not approved yet). Open questions are in the roadmap (the open points
of Parts A, B and C).

## 2026-11-25 (country server: one model per line, decided at the network's design; twins stay as they are)

**A line and its branches are one model; separate lines are separate
models, meeting at substations and on towers carrying another line's
circuits as twins** (roadmap O17, *One model per line*; owner,
2026-11-25). Nothing is built by this entry.

- **The rule**: a line branching (a Y or T connection, two or more routes
  sharing a tower) is one model, its shared towers one object each (phase
  8's towers shared by several routes). Only separate lines are separate
  models in the country server.
- **Where it is decided**: at the network's design, before the import;
  `ohl network import` stays one project file = one line. **Where it is
  corrected**: in OHL-Design, the application with the capability — a
  command joining another project file's routes into the open project is
  to be built (its twins offered to become shared towers, the user
  deciding, none ticked by default; the open project's tower kept and the
  other line's sections re-attached by point label, those without a match
  refused and listed; owner, 2026-11-25: "Ok with recommendations").
- **Twins unchanged**: listed by the import for an admin, never merged,
  taken as one tower by the scoped checks; they cover substation portals
  holding several lines' starts. The admin's command merging twins,
  planned under *Later*, is dropped.

## 2026-11-25 (country server: the usage of a shared tower on every line's loads; the electric field's cuts, volumes and jumpers with the other lines)

**Four "left" items of the server's follow-ups of 2026-11-24, and a
scoped check's result made independent of the machine's load** (ROADMAP
O17; owner, 2026-11-23: "go ahead with the server too"; built, in active
development, not approved yet).

1. **The usage of a shared tower on every line's loads** (the first
   follow-up's owner question 1, recommended "next, the usage check of a
   shared tower on the combined loads";
   [theory](../theory/scoped-checks.md#the-usage-of-a-shared-tower-on-every-lines-loads),
   [user guide](../user-guide/structure-loads-window.md#the-usage-of-a-shared-tower-on-every-lines-loads)).
   - **Before**: the Usage view said in red that the shared towers' usage
     was this line's loads alone (NOT ALL CHECKED); the network's check
     gave loads only.
   - **Now** each case of a shared tower (line \\( x \\)'s case, every
     line's loads on it as added there) is one load case of the working
     set's structure (`ohl_scope::loads::combine`) checked by **the same
     structure check as the line's own loads** (`ohl_loads::capacity`
     through `ohl_scope::loads::tower_usage`). OHL-Design's window checks
     with its own types and sections and lists these cases in the Usage
     view beside its own (*line L's case C, every line (shared towers)*):
     the governing usage is the larger of the two, per member too (the
     largest member of either). The network's check (server and
     `check_offline`) reads the line's structure libraries
     (`Neighbourhood::structure_checks`, new, default: left to the caller)
     and reports one finding per tower — its governing usage against
     100 % (a violation above) — and notes for what was not checked.
   - **Decided**: a broken wire in every span — every combination of one
     break per line a variant of its own for the finite-element and pole
     checks (at most 256, more said NOT ALL CHECKED), the lines' envelopes
     added for the allowable loads (conservative); allowable spans take
     this line's conductor positions (a shared point's summed vertical
     load: a larger weight span); twins turned more than 0.5° apart NOT
     ALL CHECKED (found: the loads were added in each twin's own axes and
     by point label, right only for one orientation; said for the Shared
     towers view's loads too); **the network's server runs no
     member-check plugin** (a library naming one: NOT ALL CHECKED there,
     checked in OHL-Design); with Use local conditions, NOT ON THE SAFE
     SIDE (said with what makes it safe).
2. **The electric field's cuts and volumes with the other lines**
   ([theory](../theory/electric-field.md#cuts-and-volumes-with-the-other-lines)):
   a cut as a profile (its own system where it crosses the axis, each
   point the larger of alone and together); a volume's box gets a second
   set of surfaces with every line solved together, drawn with the own
   ones (the union: the larger of the two), its run cut into stretches of
   53 m each with its own system (`ohl_scope::electric::JointAlong`,
   `ohl_electrical::joint::System`: a system solved once, its field taken
   at any point after — `joint::solve` unchanged, to the bit).
   `FieldVolume` gains an optional `label` (the [data model](data-model.md)).
3. **The jumpers in the joint system**: every line's jumpers as solved,
   each held at the voltage of the section ending where it starts, a
   bundle of that section's with the jumper's own conductor; a jumper at
   no section's end left out NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE, one not solved NOT ALL
   CHECKED.
4. **The Offline working set window's step 2 offers the electric field**
   (distance, limit in kV/m); its loads check is named *Loads and usage of
   shared towers*.
5. **Found and fixed first: a scoped check's result depended on the
   machine's load** (coordinator, 2026-11-25: the full check failed the
   offline window's test under a load average of ~115 — the network's
   electric field on the file 0.74, 1.45, 0.74 kV/m on three spans where
   the window gave 1.17, 2.03, 1.16; alone the test passed). The only
   clock in those checks was the wire solver's 120 s time limit on each
   section solve: under load a neighbour's section could stop on it and
   be left out (said NOT ALL CHECKED, yet a lower value). Now every
   section solve of a scoped check has the solver's iteration limit and
   no clock (`ohl_scope::solve_budget`), for clearances, fields and loads
   alike; the test compares the network's values only when its check is
   complete (else it fails naming why); a new test forces the slow path
   (a neighbour that cannot be solved: NOT ALL CHECKED, the line named).
   **Found on the way** (the full check under load again): the network's
   value was the same in every run (0.7428… kV/m on the first span) and
   the test's own "this line alone" (the window's solve, which keeps the
   120 s limit) was the one that moved — a section of its whole-line solve
   stopped on the clock, its wires left out (an earth wire missing raises
   the field); the test now solves that line clock-free too and requires
   every section solved. The Electric field window itself still says such
   a section "not solved in this case, left out" in its notes. Also
   found: the server's folder for the structure libraries
   (`work/checks-types`) was not made when its parent did not exist yet
   — every shared tower's usage NOT ALL CHECKED there; made now (tested),
   its errors without the server's paths.

- **Tested**: on the synthetic country (150 pylons, an invented type with
  allowable loads on every structure) 4 shared towers, 72 cases of every
  line's loads, the allowable loads' usage equal by hand to the summed
  points (largest 148 %), 36 of the line's own cases through the same path
  equal to its own check, to the bit; a volume stretch's values equal a
  profile's centred there, to the bit; a system solved once equals
  `joint::solve`, to the bit; 2 m under the synthetic line's jumper the
  joint system with it 7.8–9.3 kV/m against the line alone's 8.8–11.2
  (without it 2.5–4.6: 72 % below).
- **Measured** on the offline test's synthetic country (150 pylons, a shared machine): one span's volume (2 m steps, plane ground) 145 s alone → 155 s with the export's lines (6 systems of at most 739 pieces, 1.7 s of it the lines together); a cut in the same span 24 s alone, 22 s with them (the same within the machine's noise), the lines together adding up to 0.076 kV/m; the Structure loads window's 11 shared towers 27.5 s beside its own loads (6.1 s), their usage on every line's loads about 0.3 s of it (the synthetic towers have no type: nothing to check against).

## 2026-11-25 (joint checks: a weld's sides, one fillet or two, and their check, O44 J7b)

**A weld gets its sides — the number of fillets — and the check of each**
(roadmap O44 J7b; the owner's decision of 2026-11-19: *"a weld gets a
`sides` (fillet count) field and its check"*;
[theory](../theory/joint-plates.md#a-welds-sides-j7b)).

- **The field**: `[[plate.weld]] sides`, 1 (one fillet on one side of the
  plate) or 2 (a fillet on each side; a length given is both together,
  none each fillet the seam's); any other number refused; structure file
  version 28 (`WELD_SIDES_VERSION`), written only when a weld gives them,
  an older reader refuses it.
- **The default, not given**: the check takes **the worse of one fillet
  and two**. Today's check was the one fillet's (its throat bent across by
  a moment about the seam, one line of the whole length along it), so a
  file of before is never checked weaker than before; but where its weld
  is really two fillets with the length given both together, each fillet
  takes up to twice the moment along it that one line of the whole length
  does — today's check was not on the safe side there, and the default
  covers it. Usages of such welds with a moment along them may rise; none
  can fall.
- **The check** (SIA 263, the bundled plugin's new export; no rule of the
  standard for a fillet's moment about its own line, so engineering models,
  each conservative, marked so in the theory): one fillet — its root
  opened, taken by the throat (contact width) bent across elastically
  against (87) and (88), as before, with SIA 263 6.3.6.5's "avoid it"
  said; two fillets — the moment about the seam a couple across the
  thinner plate's thickness (the real lever arm is larger), the moment
  along them on both lines, each fillet by (87) and (88). The weld bent
  about its seam is no longer said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE where the bundled
  plugin checks it. ASCE 10-97: no weld rule, not checked, said, as before.
- **The plugin interface** (needed for this, additive and backwards
  compatible): a new optional export `joint-check-welds` (each weld with
  its sides and per case its force and moments, results as
  `joint-check-groups`'), in the `structure-code-plugin` world; both
  bundled plugins have it. A plugin without it gets its welds through
  `joint-check-moments` as before; OpenOHL adds "NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: the
  weld's sides not sent …" to such a weld's row where the sides change the
  check (a moment about the seam; a moment along a weld whose length is
  given and which is not said to be one fillet).
- **Where the sides come from**: the user (Joint details › welds, the
  *Sides* column); the automatic joint layout's welded plate in a member's
  own plane (step 4), welded from both sides by design: `sides = 2` (a weld
  given by hand there keeps the user's; files laid out before have none
  until laid out again, checked as the worse). Plates joined by
  `welded_to` alone have no weld data and stay not checked; no public
  importer writes welds.
- **Validation**: `joints-018` to `joints-021` (`structures.welds`) against
  the hand calculations in `reference_joint_capacities.py`, at 10⁻⁹.

## 2026-11-25 (joint layout: an outstanding leg into the flange, a half or quarter turn weighed, L25)

**The members left with an end whose outstanding leg points into the
flange are laid out turned by half a turn and by a quarter turn, each
weighed over every joint the member reaches** (roadmap O44 L25; the
owner, 2026-11-24: *"probably a half turn if possible then other
options"*, *"maybe a 90 degrees turn might be better so you could also
consider it"*; L25's two open questions taken as recommended: L25 now, the
quarter turn of an unequal angle allowed and said with the leg it bolts;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#an-outstanding-leg-pointing-into-the-flange-a-half-or-a-quarter-turn-weighed-l25)).

- **What**: after the run (and L19's weighing), every member with such an
  end — not a leg or chord, not one part with another, a single angle,
  every joint it reaches laid out by the run — is laid out turned by half a
  turn, by +90° and by −90° (three whole layouts); a turn passes where
  every joint the member reaches is laid out no worse and one better after
  writing; the best passing turn is the one laying out more member ends
  (one no joint elsewhere blames first; on a tie the half turn, then the
  fewer plates); the turns chosen are laid out together and weighed again
  with L19's guard past the turned members until all still pass (at most
  four rounds). `LayoutSettings::flange_half` and `flange_quarter`, on.
- **The quarter turn of an unequal angle** bolts its other leg (the plan
  takes that leg's bolts, gauges and edge distances), only where no leg
  is given (`connected_leg`, the end's `leg`): never changed silently. The
  member check is unchanged (the bundled plugin takes the short leg bolted
  without a leg given).
- **Applied or offered**: applied where the roll is the program's (an
  imported tower's, or values given by hand replaced), recorded in the
  layout record's new `flange_turns` rows (no version change; the [data
  model](data-model.md)); offered in Lay out joints where the roll is the
  designer's (applied when ticked). A member weighed is not weighed again
  while its row is its own; neither turn helping: left, said (a stand-off
  later).
- **Measured** (eight private towers, 6 852 joints, kept privately; the
  bundled ASCE 10-97 plugin built fresh and checked to load before each
  run; the base main before L25, the same setup): joints whole 4 218 →
  4 253, member ends 15 141 → 15 268, plates 8 047 → 8 196, 124 joints
  better and none worse; ends left with the outstanding leg into the flange
  460 → 335; of 326 members weighed, half a turn kept at 83, a quarter
  turn at 46, 23 passing alone but not together, neither helping at 174.
  Every member weighed there is an equal-leg angle (the unequal angle's
  quarter turn tested on an invented body only). Each turn alone on four
  of the towers: the half turn 23 joints better, the quarter turn 30, both
  weighed 38 (none worse in any): both kept, as the owner asked. The
  weighing lays each tower out four or five more times
  (once per tower). **Kept** (the rule met: no joint worse).

## 2026-11-25 (safety gaps of the "not on the safe side" audit closed)

The audit of 2026-11-24 (every NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE text says why) listed
places where a check leaves something out and **no input makes it
safe**. Each is turned into a check on the safe side where that needs no
owner's decision (built, in active development, not approved yet; the
owner busy: built on its own, reported):

- **The pole check takes a post insulator's moment**
  ([post insulators](../theory/post-insulators.md),
  [the pole check](../theory/structures-fe.md)). Before: a fixed post's
  moment about its base (its top's forces at their lever, its clamp's
  moment) was left out of the pole check — said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE in
  the line's checks and in OHL-Structure ("add it by hand"). Now: the
  moment at its point (`PoleLoad::moment`) bends every section below it,
  twists it (a design code's check takes the torsion) and is in the
  P-Delta model with the force — exactly the couple of forces it is,
  nothing assumed. The note now says it is taken. No file format or
  plugin interface changed (the pole check is the core's). Tested: the
  moment against the couple of forces (usage, ground moment, P-Delta
  ratio equal; a torsion by ASCE/SEI 48-19 the same), a moment that is
  not a number refused.
- **More than six forces a level plate may pass: exact for the bolts**
  ([joint bolt groups](../theory/joint-groups.md#the-force-a-level-plate-passes-between-its-two-holders-l21)).
  Before: beyond `PASSED_EACH` (six) the rest were taken together, none or
  all — a mix in between, which can load a bolt more, not tried (said NOT
  ON THE SAFE SIDE on the rows). Now: each bolt's shear in the plane at
  its exact largest over every share (the corners of a zonotope found by
  one direction in each arc between the generators' normals, at most 2 n
  of them — no 2ⁿ loadings), its pull out of the plane likewise (a
  number: each share where it adds); a plate's row, a member's own steel
  and a weld add each further force's size to the largest of the first
  six's (a bound, on the safe side). Up to six, as before, bit for bit:
  results change only at a place with more (rare: two holders and a few
  ends laid onto the other). Tested against every corner (2¹⁰ invented vectors; 2⁸
  corners of a three-bolt group's shear and pull).
- **ASCE 10-97: bolts beyond the leg's centre line**
  ([ASCE 10-97](../theory/asce10.md#bolts-beyond-the-legs-centre-line)).
  Before: a single angle bolted by one leg whose bolt pattern's centroid
  lies beyond the connected leg's centre line was checked by the curve for
  normal framing eccentricity (commentary C3.7.4 ties that to a centroid
  between the heel and the centre line) — said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE in the
  joint layout's theory only. Now, inside the asce10 plugin (its own code;
  the gauges it already received): the part beyond, Δe = ḡ − w/2, bends
  the angle by P·Δe about its principal axes, the stresses at both axes'
  farthest fibres added, amplified by 1/(1 − P/P_e) (C_m = 1, P_e at the
  member's governing KL/r), against F_y — added to the curve's P/P_a by
  Eq. 3.12-1's form; uniform along the member and whole (C3.7.4's "due
  consideration", on the safe side). What it still leaves out is said on
  the member (NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: the angle's lateral-torsional buckling
  under that moment — ASCE 10-97 3.14 has no rule for angles). Tension
  unchanged. SIA 263 already takes the real gauge in its N·e (5.4.1.2):
  unchanged. No plugin interface changed. Tested by hand (an invented
  L 80 × 8, 15 mm beyond).
- **An end bolted through a splice's outer cover: its offset taken; the
  packing an owner question**
  ([joint layout](../theory/joint-layout.md#bracing-bolted-through-the-outer-cover)).
  Before: the end lies the cover's thickness farther out of the leg — in
  neither the analysis nor the member's check — and the cover is a
  packing, the bolt's bending across it not checked; both said NOT ON THE
  SAFE SIDE in the theory only. Now: where the joint details are taken
  (level 4) the cover's thickness is an offset of unknown sign at that end
  (`eccentricities::cover_offsets`, the core's `free_offsets`, along its
  bolts' axis): never in the solve, its moment N·t whole and sign-free in
  the member's own check (on the safe side for the member; the others
  relieved of nothing), said in the run's notes. The packing: no rule in
  ASCE 10-97 or SIA 263, another standard's values not in the documents —
  **not built**, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE on the cover's row (before, in
  the theory only), the question with a recommendation in the roadmap
  (O19). At level 3 the joint details are not read: the offset is not
  analysed there, as an end's on a gusset plate (O45 D). Tested on the
  invented spliced leg (`leg_splices` tests: D through a 15 mm cover, its
  offset 15 mm along its bolts, its moment at least 50 kN × 15 mm; none
  without the joint details).
- **A bent plate's bend takes a frame member's end shear and moments**
  ([the bend in bending](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-bend-in-bending-2026-11-19)).
  Before: the bend's section took the members' axial forces only — said
  NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE in the theory. Now, where the case's end forces are
  known (OHL-Structure's runs): each member's shear (square to its axis)
  and moment, carried to its bolts' centroid and on to the bend's middle,
  the shear across the bend added to N, along it to V, square to the flat
  to V by size; the moment about the bend line to M by size, in the
  plate's plane to M_in, its twist to M by size (a thin plate's torsion
  stress 3T/(w t²) counted as a bending stress 6T/(w t²): on the safe
  side). The same four values reach the plugins' `joint-check-bends`,
  larger: no interface changed. Tested by hand (1 kN square to the flat
  at 0.2 m, 50 N m of twist, 30 N m in the plane). Results rise only at
  bends where frame members (end moments) meet.
- **Not built, an owner question: a plate in compression lying on a
  flange** (a short plate, a level plate on its holders). Its strut check
  (K = 2 to its edge) takes it as held where it lies on the flange — by
  contact on one side where it has no bolts of its own there; the fix
  (such a strut NOT CHECKED, never a usage) changes how many plates read
  "not checked", so it is asked with a recommendation in the roadmap
  (O19); the NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE text in the theory stays.

## 2026-11-25 (joint layout: a detailing practice as data, O44 L24)

**The owner's approval** (2026-11-24, the plan in roadmap O44 L24): make
the joint layout's detailing *rules* pluggable as data; keep the engine
that builds, checks and validates the layout in the program (thousands
of joints per tower; one source of truth with the joint details; safety
stays with the core — a plugin never certifies its own result). Step 1,
this entry: a "detailing practice" preset, as data, with the plugin
interface change it needs. Step 2 (a "propose a joint" hook for joints
left for a hand detail): later. **The plan's six design questions were
built as recommended, awaiting the owner's confirmation** (the owner
approved the plan "go with what you said"). Built
(`ohl_structure_link::practice`; built, in active development, not
approved yet; [theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-detailing-practice-l24),
[plugins](plugins.md#detailing-practice)).

- **(1) Where it lives**: a table `[layout_practice]` in the structure
  file (structure file version 27, `LAYOUT_PRACTICE_VERSION`, written at
  27 only when present; older files read as today's defaults) and the
  same table answered by a code plugin's optional export
  `layout-practice` (additive to interface 0.3: a plugin without it loads
  as before); the structure's own table wins over the plugin's **value by
  value** (`practice::merged`, `in_force`). A run records the plugin's
  answer in the layout record (`[generator.practice]`); an edit's follow
  and the estimated eccentricities lay the file's table over it.
- **(2) Which values**: only today's settings and constants, each with
  its present value as the default — the fabrication forms (bend, welded
  allowed or not), the face preferences (L10's pattern and other face,
  L11's both faces), the gap, pull-back and shift (the window's starting
  values), the flatness, the small bend's and the welded plate's axis
  offset's limits, the bend's inside radius, the least gap for a plate
  between angles, plates stopping short of the work point, the picked
  bolt's pattern. **An empty preset lays out exactly as today**: applying
  a practice only turns switches off and replaces the program's numbers
  by the same numbers (tested: the engine's settings equal, also with
  switches off; an invented K-brace laid out to the same plans, file and
  estimated eccentricities). Not measured on the private towers yet.
- **(3) The fabrication order**: an ordered list of the five forms
  (direct, plate, bend, bends, welded), each allowed or not; the weighing
  keeps its rule (more ends, or as many on fewer plates) and the order is
  used only on ties — today the one tie between forms, a plate bent by a
  few degrees against one welded in the member's own plane
  (`LayoutSettings::weld_before_bend`); "bends" is not built.
- **(4) Limits**: the core's checks are no values of a practice (the
  clash check, the code's distances, holes overlapping, the bend check,
  the NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE words); every value is range-checked and a
  value beyond what the core can check is refused with the reason, whose
  table, in Lay out joints and in the run's notes
  (`LayoutSettings::practice_refused`), the default then used. The
  safety-relevant ranges: the flatness never looser than the joint
  details' 2°; the shift at most 30 mm and the welded plate's axis offset
  at most 40 mm (the estimated eccentricities' upper bounds, until J5);
  the bend radius at least one thickness; no single bolt (J8); "direct"
  and "plate" always allowed.
- **(5) Per member class first**: `[layout_practice.classes.<class>]` for
  the connection presets' classes, with the picked bolt's pattern
  (`LayoutSettings::class_bolts`); other values per class refused (not
  built yet); per joint kind later if asked.
- **(6) Shown**: Lay out joints shows, below its preview, the practice in
  force, its source (the file, the plugin, the defaults), why one given
  is not used, and each value with where it comes from and its effect.
  **Not yet**: each value's effect *measured* on the private towers
  (next, with the bundled `asce10` built fresh, as L23 found necessary).
- **Not in the practice** (kept in code, listed in the roadmap with why):
  the search bounds and rounds, the geometric tolerances (the joint
  details', clash check's, planes' and groups' 2°, the 75° tilt, the
  in-line angles), the switches that make the plan agree with the check,
  the plate's thickness rule (as thick as the thickest leg on it; a least
  thickness and steps of thickness, in the plan's list, not yet), a
  plate grown along its holder, the plates' own holding bolts, the class
  order.
- **The bundled codes** give no practice (a practice is a shop's, not a
  code's); the example plugin gives an invented one for the tests.

## 2026-11-25 (joint layout: three steps measured, none kept, L23)

**L22's questions 2 and 3, L21's item 3 and L19's question 7b tried and
measured; none changes the program** (roadmap O44 L23; the owner busy:
built on its own, reported;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#a-plates-own-holding-bolts-tested-by-the-clash-check-after-writing-tried-not-kept-l23)).

- **A plate's own holding bolts tested by the clash check after writing**
  (L22's question 2; testing each candidate inside the plan would cost a
  joint's whole detail per candidate, so the run's own check after
  writing was used, the plan told what it found and planned again first):
  in four forms on four private towers no end more; the first changes no
  joint at a much longer run, the others leave one joint kind an end short
  on three towers. With the plate grown along its holder (L22's question
  3) again 15 joints worse. **Not kept** (no joint worse is the rule).
- **The members' turns weighed without the far-out welded plates** (L21's
  item 3, the joints L20 item 2 left worse): the half and quarter turns
  and L10's other faces chosen as if L20 item 2's plates did not exist
  (as L16 does for the plates between): 24 joints better, 28 worse, 30
  ends fewer — those plates gain mostly through turns. **Not kept**; next
  (an owner question): each turn they change weighed over every joint its
  member reaches, as L19 weighs the plane turns.
- **The joggle** (L19's question 7b): **not built** — a straight leg tilted
  over the flange lies a plate's thickness above it at its lowest point
  and rises along its slope to its bolts whatever the plate under it does;
  the welded plate is already within the seam's room of that bound (of 60
  such ends at most 15° off on eight private towers, 5 could come within a
  plate's thickness with no room at the seam at all).
- **The measuring setup** (found on the way): L21's, L22's and this

## 2026-11-24 (bolt distances: ASCE 10-97's force per bolt without an analysis capped by its bearing, O44 L16 question 4)

**The owner's answer** to O44 L16's question 4 (approved 2026-11-24, "go
ahead with recommendations"): the plugin's force basis without an
analysis is the smaller of the bolt's shear capacity and its bearing in
the part (a code plugin change, the source cited; the joint checks still
check the bearing), and the toe of a rolled angle is taken as a rolled
edge. **Built: the force basis** (`asce10` only, no core or interface
change; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/asce10.md#minimum-distances-of-bolts)). **Not built:
the rolled toe** — which edge is sheared is decided by OpenOHL's core
(`ohl_structures_fe::bolt_rules::basis`: sheared unless the connection
says `rolled_edge = true`, the owner's rule of 2026-11-03) and sent to
the plugin as `sheared-edge`; the plugin cannot tell an angle's toe from a
plate's edge, so taking the toe as rolled is a core change, asked first
(the rule that plugins stay independent of the core; roadmap O44 L16).

- **Before**: without an analysis the force per bolt in Eq. 4.5-1 was the
  bolt's design shear capacity (4.3.2) alone.
- **Now**: the smaller of that and its bearing cap in the part, 1.5 f_u d
  t (4.4, f_u the lower of the part's and the bolt's; `asce10::bearing_cap`,
  `asce10::force_without_analysis`); the basis said with the distances. A
  force above either is refused by the member and joint checks (which
  still check both), so Eq. 4.5-1's 1.2 P/(f_u t) needs not exceed 1.8 d;
  an M20 in a 5 mm leg (f_u 490 MPa, 94 kN shear capacity): 73.5 kN, end
  46 → 36 mm, sheared edge 41 → 32.2 mm (rolled 30.6 mm). Without a shear
  capacity the bearing cap alone (the force terms were left out before).
- **Validation**: `joints-015` to `joints-017` (a new calculation,
  `structures.bolt_distances`: one bolt's minimums by a code plugin as

## 2026-11-24 (every "not on the safe side" says why)

**The owner's rule** (verbatim): *"with the 'not on the safe side' please
always explain why it's written"*. Every NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE text says
**what** is left out or assumed, **why** that can make the result unsafe
(which quantity can be larger in reality, or the capacity smaller) and
**what makes it safe** (an input, a setting, or the planned step, named;
"not modelled yet: keep a margin" where there is none). The rule is in
`CONTRIBUTING.md` (Ground rules) and
[Staying on the safe side](safe-side.md).

- **Text only**: nothing computed changed; no mark was removed or
  weakened. The texts that lacked a part were rewritten — the results'
  notes, report lines, table cells, command-line lines, hover and (?)
  helps, the default weather and load case descriptions, and the theory
  and guide pages that quote them.
- **Helpers carry the why** where one mark is used in many places: the
  member's `[not on the safe side: …]` (the core's check and both code
  plugins' end it with "its usage can be higher than shown; give what is
  missing, or check it by hand"), "NOT CHECKED by <plugin>, NOT ON THE
  SAFE SIDE (a failure there would not be found)", the members without a
  plugin result, the rigid-structures note of the clearance checks.
- **Left as they were**: the decision log's older entries (a record of
  what was said then), code comments for developers, and the files
  another change was editing at the time (the joint layout and the
  electric field's neighbour files) — those follow when that work lands.
- **Second pass, the same day**: those files done too — the joint
  layout's theory and notes, the electric field's theory, its scoped and
  offline notes and their guide pages. The "wires beyond the field
  distance" note now has one wording for the magnetic and the electric
  field (`ohl_scope::fields::beyond_words`: their field is missing, so
  the real field can be higher; a larger field distance takes them in).

**Each holder of a level plate takes the force the plate may pass from
the other holder** (roadmap O44 L21, L20's question 2; the owner busy:
built on its own, reported; built, in active development, not approved
yet; [theory](../theory/joint-groups.md#the-force-a-level-plate-passes-between-its-two-holders-l21)).

  forces on the plate whole, neither holder's own force taken; said NOT ON
  THE SAFE SIDE on the rows: a force the plate passes between its two
  holders.

  safe bound, no load path worked out — each holder's holding group takes
  the other ends' forces whole or none, each with and without the other
  holder's force (and those of the ends laid onto that holder near its

  force through the plate; a force circulating round the joint from its
  own deformation is not counted (the joint one point in the analysis;

## 2026-11-24 (country server: the electric field with other lines, solved together)

**The electric field with other lines: the network's check and
OHL-Design's Electric field window on an offline file** (ROADMAP O17,
the second follow-up's "left" and its owner question 4, recommended
"solved together … the worst over the relative angles found without
sampling"; owner, 2026-11-23: "go ahead with the server too"; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/electric-field.md#other-lines-solved-together),
[checks on a working set](../theory/scoped-checks.md#electric-field),
[user guide](../user-guide/electric-field.md#other-lines-on-an-offline-working-sets-file)).

- **Before**: the network computed no electric field with other lines;
  the window named the export's lines within 500 m (NOT ALL CHECKED, NOT
  ON THE SAFE SIDE where they come near).
- **Why solved together**: a neighbour's conductors, held at their own
  voltages, and its earth wires, held at zero, change this line's
  charges; fields of lines computed apart and added by size are **not a
  proven bound** for the electric field (unlike the magnetic field, whose
  sources are the given currents). Not done.
- **The system** (`ohl_electrical::joint`, new): charge simulation
  (Singer, Steinbigler and Weiss 1974) — every line's wires and earth
  wires (a bundle as its equivalent wire) cut into straight pieces of
  uniform charge, graded with their distance from the profile's middle
  (4 m, growing at 0.15 of the distance, at most 60 m; the wires within
  the field distance of the middle), each piece's potential held at its
  wire's voltage at a point on its surface; the images in the ground
  plane fitted under each matching point and each field point (the
  electric field's quick ground model); \\( Pq = V \\) by faer's LU on all
  cores. The jumpers are left out of the system (this line alone keeps
  them).
- **The phase angles** (the owner question's recommendation): the system
  is linear, so it is solved **by parts** (one line's phases of one
  frequency, every other wire at zero; one LU, two right-hand sides per
  part), and the worst over the parts' unknown angles is
  \\( \sum_k|E_k|^2 + 2\sum_{k<l}|\langle E_k,E_l\rangle| \\) — **exact for two
  parts** (this line and one other line: closed form, no sampling),
  **an upper bound for three or more** (said "an upper bound" in every
  result), never above the parts added by size (Cauchy–Schwarz).
- **The result at a point**: the larger of this line alone in its own
  model and the lines together (decided here: neither model may lower the
  other; owner question 1).
- **The network's check**: a new scoped check `electric_field` (`case`,
  `distance`?, `limit_kv_m`?; the protocol's `check` message gains the
  kind, no schema change) → `ohl_scope::electric::electric_field`; the
  lines taken as the magnetic field takes them (the selection split out
  as `ohl_scope::fields::near_sections`, `other_lines` on it unchanged in
  what it computes); each result lists what the system took in and the
  method; `ohl network check-offline --check electric [--limit-kv-m E]`.
- **The window**: `ohl_app::offline_neighbours::ElectricNeighbours` →
  `ohl_server::offline_checks::electric_neighbours` (the file read as the
  server reads it, the working set's sections replaced by those of the
  spans computed) → the same `joint_lines` and `joint_at` at the window's
  profile points and given points (each given point its own system), with
  the window's voltages for this line's circuits. NOT ALL CHECKED (red)
  for the cuts and volumes (this line alone), a reach beyond the export,
  neighbours left out, a line or profile not solved; NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE
  for the wires beyond 500 m, a given point far from the spans, a line at
  its nominal voltage. The 2026-11-23 note "no check adds them yet — NOT
  ON THE SAFE SIDE" is gone where the lines are computed.
- **Tested**: two long parallel wires over level ground against the
  image method in 2D by hand (each part's field within 0.5 % at 21
  points); the worst over the angle against 3 600 sampled angles (none
  above, the best within a thousandth); three parts' bound above every
  sampled pair of angles and below the parts added by size; an earthed
  wire screening a phase (below 90 % of alone); on the synthetic country
  (300 pylons) every point at least this line alone, the method said;
  against a local network's server, the window's values per span the
  network check's on the same file, to the bit (this line and two other
  lines: three parts, the bound).
- **Measured** (a heavily shared machine): the network's check on the
  synthetic country 0.4–7.2 s per working set of four sections (one to
  three profiles, 586–1 068 pieces per system); on the offline test's
  country (300 pylons) the working set's spans 7.2–7.9 s for this line +
  6.5–6.7 s for the other lines solved together, the network's check on
  the file 13.4–14.9 s; the window (plane ground, every 5 m) 8.8 s alone,
  15.6 s with them (with another test suite on the machine, load ~96:
  47 s for the other lines, the window 89 s).

## 2026-11-24 (country server: the magnetic field with an offline file's lines near)

**OHL-Design's Magnetic field window adds the field of an offline
working set's other lines** (ROADMAP O17: the 2026-11-23 follow-up's
last "left" but one; its owner question 1 recommended "next, those two
computed with them in the windows themselves by the network's code";

  the wires of the **sections whose spans it computed** (profiles, cuts,

  synthetic country, the working set's spans, every circuit at 600 A):

  the bit equal to the network's on the same field, and per span the
  highest value equal **to the bit** to the network's check on the same
  file (150 and 300 pylons; the file's line holds no more of this line
  near the working set than the network's sections within 500 m).

  (since 2026-11-23); they are now red, an export's "may be stale"
  orange.

  added (their sections near), that they **may be stale**, then **NOT ALL
  CHECKED** (red) for a reach beyond the export (spans of the read-only
  parts around the working set reach farther than it holds), neighbours
  left out of the export, a neighbour not solved or not read, and **the
  volumes** (their surfaces are this line's field alone, decided: the
  owner's question below); **NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE** for the wires beyond
  500 m, a given point far from the spans computed, a circuit at 0 A.
- **The electric field** stays as on 2026-11-23 (the lines within 500 m
  named, NOT ALL CHECKED): the network computes no electric field with
  other lines — what it needs is in the roadmap (O17's follow-up of
  2026-11-24).
- **Measured** on the synthetic country (a heavily shared machine): the
  working set's spans as the network's check computes them (profiles
  every 5 m) 6.0–6.8 s for this line, + 3.7–7.7 s for the other lines
  (opening the file, solving them, adding them); the network's check on
  the same file 10.0–11.7 s. The window with its defaults (profiles every
  1 m, 144 spans of 300 pylons) 10.6–11.1 s alone → 17.0–20.0 s with
  the lines near (150 pylons: 11.9 → 19.7 s): the other lines' field is
  summed at five times more points.
- **The desktop format unchanged** (the current typed is not kept).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-24; the recommendation after the arrow)

## 2026-11-24 (structure analysis: the joint options' taking back where it failed, O19 stage 4.4 follow-up)

**The taking back of the end releases and the bolt slip reaches the cause of
a buckling mode** (roadmap O19 stage 4.4; the towers where the runs with
the options failed — 3, 6 and 10 of 72 private towers with releases, slip,
both — traced; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/structures-fe.md#end-releases-and-bolt-slip-from-the-joints-bolts-options)):

- **Traced**: with the slip, the buckling modes moved the top of the
  tower most (a sway) while their cause — bracing slipping inside its
  clearance — lay lower down; the taking back at the joints named and
  three rings around them took back the top and stopped there.
- **The members the mode strains most** (each member's change of length
  in the mode over its length; a tenth of the largest or more, at most 24;
  `FeError::Unstable`'s `straining`) are taken back where nothing is left
  within the rings — only then, so every run that solved before solves as
  before.
- **Each round's slip passes start where the last round's stopped** (its
  secant stiffnesses kept): the same settled point, fewer passes (one
  tower's case from 285 s to 28 s); the towers solved before with both
  options and taking back moved by up to 0.4 points.
- **Runs with the options no longer use the solves' memo of failed first
  iterations** (calculation level 4's speed-up): its key ignores the
  members' slip and releases, which the passes and the taking back change —
  a failure kept from one model would stand for the next. No run uses the
  options with the memo today (a latent fault, closed).
- **The share of the joints taken back is said** with the case ("N
  joint(s) of M (P %)"): where it is large the model is in large parts the
  one without the options, and a member kept rigid beside slipping ones
  draws force from them (on the safe side for that member; the larger of
  the two shows it).
- **Measured** (the private towers, one case, results kept privately): the
  slip solves on 70 of 72 towers (66 before), both on 68 (62), the
  releases on 69 (unchanged); the newly solved take the slip back at 7 %
  to 43 % of their joints, 11 s to 64 s a case; still failing: releases 3,
  slip 2, both 4 (2 of them P-Delta not converging) — joints held out of a
  face only by members in that face, which the model without the options
  carries only through the joints' stabilisation. Owner questions (5) and
  (6) in the roadmap.

## 2026-11-23 (structure analysis: end releases and bolt slip as options, O19 stage 4.4)

**End releases and bolt slip from the joints' bolts, options of the analysis
measured before any default** (roadmap O19 stage 4.4, queue item C8 of
2026-11-18; the owner's "Go ahead" on the queue, 2026-11-23 "go ahead … so
the work goes through the night"; built, in active development, not
approved yet; [theory](../theory/structures-fe.md#end-releases-and-bolt-slip-from-the-joints-bolts-options);
no file format change):

- **Both off by default, stored in no file**: OHL-Structure's Results ticks
  (for the session), `ohl structures fe --end-releases --bolt-slip`, the
  validation's `structures.fe` inputs. A file field (and its version) waits
  for the owner's answer below — a version bump now would also have met
  the joint layout's format work running at the same time.
- **End releases**: one bolt → both bending rotations of the end released
  (a member so at both ends is a bar); one row of bolts in one leg of an
  angle → the rotation about that leg's direction released; two rows, both
  legs, unknown → held. Read from each end's connection, else from the
  member's design data where the end is not in line with a member of the
  same section (taken as running on through the joint). Condensed out of
  the element's tangent (elastic and geometric together).
- **Bolt slip**: each bolted end slips by its hole clearance, no friction
  counted (the full slip — conservative for the deflections), 1 % of EA/L
  kept inside the clearance (without it the passes failed on 25 of 72 real
  towers instead of 6), solved by secant passes (first order, then
  P-Delta), tolerance 10⁻⁴.
- **Taken back where the solve fails**: a mechanism, buckling mode or
  implausible displacements with the options → the releases and slip of
  the members meeting the joints named taken back (rings around them where
  nothing is left there; first, at a buckling mode, every member compressed
  beyond its buckling load as released), said per case. Without this the
  releases failed on 12 of 72 real towers; with it on 3.
- **The effect of every run with an option**: each case also solved without
  it; the largest displacement, the forces changed, the largest usage, the
  usages up and down and both times in the case's notes.
- **Safe side**: neither option is on the safe side for every member (the
  releases share the forces differently; the slip relieves the members it
  lets slip and loads the legs) — said in the notes, never chosen silently.
- **Measured** (one vertical case, 72 private real towers, kept privately;
  two invented towers): releases — the top's displacement +0.1 %, a tower's
  largest usage +0.1 % (median; 0.92 to 2.37), 8.5 % of the member forces
  over 1 kN changed by more than 10 %, the solve 2.4 times slower; slip —
  the top's displacement 2.85 times, a tower's largest usage +15 % (0.78 to
  1.55), most bracing relieved, the solve 16 times slower (33 passes). The
  tower program's results match the model without the options (0.1 %).
