## 2026-11-23 (country server: a revision of main made by the server so any designer can export)

**Main's unrecorded changes recorded by the network's server itself
before an offline export** (ROADMAP O17: phase 12's "left"; the owner's
question 2 of phase 12, answered 2026-11-20 "go ahead with
recommendations": "yes for now; a revision of main made by the server
itself (audited) when someone exports, next — so any designer can
export"; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[the user guide](../user-guide/server.md#offline-working-sets-phase-12-in-active-development)).

- **Before**: an export's base must be a revision, so main's changes not
  yet recorded were recorded first **by the exporter** — by phase 11's
  rule for a commit (it records only what its user may edit): a
  designer of one route could not export while anyone had left an
  unrecorded change elsewhere on main ("ask whoever may edit them all to
  commit the main line").
- **Now** the network's server records them itself: a revision of main
  whose **author is `network:server`** (a name no user can have: users'
  names hold no ':'), message "Recorded by the network's server for an
  offline working set of USER", in its own unit of work, broadcast as
  any commit; **audited under the exporter's name** (*server revision*),
  after the export's own checks of rights (the working set seen whole,
  export on each of its objects, something editable on each route) —
  nothing is recorded for a user the export refuses. It records only
  what main holds already (each edit allowed by the rules when it was
  made); it moves nothing, gives the exporter nothing more (the file
  holds only what they may see), and is made **on a protected main too**
  (decided as recorded: the session's rule for a protected branch is for
  changes; this revision changes nothing — the owner's question 1
  below). The session sees the server's author as an admin of every
  model (`ModelRoles`), for this one act.
- **Tested** on PostgreSQL (`offline_working_sets_go_out_and_come_back`):
  the designer of one route exports while main has never been recorded
  (refused before): the export goes out, its base is main's new head, a
  revision by `network:server` naming her, in the audit under her name;
  her next export records nothing first.

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-23; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. The server's revision also on a protected main (it records what main
> holds; no review)? → yes: it changes nothing a review would look at.
> 2. Always the server's revision, even when the exporter could record
> every change themselves? → yes: one author for main's bookkeeping,
> the exporter named in the message and the audit.
> 3. Its author `network:server` (not a user)? → yes.

## 2026-11-23 (country server: the check windows with an offline file's neighbours)

**OHL-Design's check windows read an offline working set's neighbours**
(ROADMAP O17: phase 16's and phase 12's "left"; the owner, 2026-11-23:
"go ahead with the server too"; built, in active development, not
approved yet; [the user guide](../user-guide/offline-working-set.md#checks-with-the-exports-neighbours)).
Before, the Offline working set window ran the network's checks with
the neighbours an offline file holds, but the ordinary check windows ran
on the file alone (the rules to other lines skipped, "checked by `ohl
line --other-line`").

- **The Clearances window's rules to other lines** take the export's
  other lines: those whose sections' structures come within the rules'
  reach of the checked wires (the reach as the network's checks work it
  out — every voltage the neighbours have, at the highest point — plus
  30 m for the arms and the network's largest span margin: more
  candidates, never fewer), each solved in **every position checked**
  (each weather case and wind position, by the rules' calculation) with
  **its own line's settings and wire library** — the library built by
  the network's own code (`ohl_server::offline_checks::neighbour_wires`,
  as `check_offline` builds it: its wire files, else the shipped
  library). Their wires are named `LINE:SECTION`. **Tested**: on the same
  offline file (a synthetic country of 150 pylons with a tower shared by
  two lines, exported through OHL-Design's window from a local network's
  server), the rule to other lines finds **the same pairs at the same
  distances** (within 1e-6 m) as the network's own check on it.
- **Never silently**: the window's block *Offline working set:
  neighbours from its export* before Run (its (?) and User guide ↗), and
  the report's lines after it: the export's date (and its number when
  OHL-Design wrote the file), the lines read (their sections), those
  within the rules' reach, and **that they may be stale** (in the warning
  colour). **The stale export's logic re-used**: the Offline working set
  window keeps the server's answer (`stale`, `changed_meanwhile`) in the
  file it writes, as the application setting `app.offline_export` — not
  part of the line, not in its revisions, not in a bundle — and the
  check windows say *STALE already when exported: N object(s) …* or that
  nothing changed while it was written; a file written by `ohl network
  export-working-set` does not know (said).
- **NOT ALL CHECKED**, in red, for: neighbours left out of the export
  (the user may not see them), a rule reaching farther than the export's
  reach or outside its area, a neighbour line not solved, a neighbour's
  wire file not read, a rule to other lines across weather cases (case
  pairs: not in this window). **The verdict** then says *NOT ALL
  CHECKED — no violation among what was checked* instead of *Every rule
  met* — also for a network's working set joined (its "neighbours not
  pulled in" was a note under a ✔ before: found and fixed).
- **Decided as conservative** (the owner's questions below): **Structure
  loads, the fields and plugins name the neighbours instead of adding
  them** — the towers shared with another line of the export (the same
  type within 0.5 m, as the network finds twins), the lines within 500 m
  (the network's field distance), the lines within a plugin's declared
  reach — NOT ALL CHECKED for them, with where they are computed (the
  Offline working set window's *Loads on shared towers* and *Magnetic
  field*; for the electric field nothing yet: NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE where
  they come near). Nothing near: said, complete for neighbours. **Found**:
  the field windows on a network's working set joined said nothing of
  the neighbours not pulled in; they now say it (phase 10's note).
- **Measured** on the synthetic country of 300 pylons (two runs, a
  shared machine): a route's clearances (one weather case, its rules to
  other lines and between its wires) 3.5–3.9 s on the file alone,
  5.8–7.3 s with its 2 neighbour lines (in OHL-Design's window); the
  network's own check on the same file 5.2–5.6 s. The neighbours' wires
  taken as targets are those within the rules' reach of a checked wire
  in plan (as the network's checks take them).
- **The desktop format unchanged**: one application setting key added
  (the settings are free keys, documented in the data model).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-23; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. Structure loads, the fields and plugins name the export's
> neighbours (NOT ALL CHECKED) instead of adding them; the Offline
> working set window adds them for the loads on shared towers and the
> magnetic field? → yes for now; next, those two computed with them in
> the windows themselves by the network's code.
> 2. The server's answer on the export kept in the exported file as an
> application setting (not in the line, its revisions or a bundle)? →
> yes.
> 3. The neighbours solved in the weather case and wind position of this
> line's check (the same weather at the same place), each with its own
> settings and wires? → yes, as the network's checks.
> 4. Rules to other lines across weather cases still not in the window,
> NOT ALL CHECKED when the export's neighbours are there? → yes, until
> the network's checks take case pairs.
> 5. The verdict NOT ALL CHECKED whenever a reason holds, also on a
> network's working set joined? → yes.

## 2026-11-23 (joint layout: turns weighed over every joint they reach, L19)

**The turns Orient angles sets from the joints' planes are weighed by the
layout run: each kept only where every joint its members reach is laid
out no worse and one better, else taken back and offered** (roadmap O44
L19, L18's questions 1 and 2 and the owner's rule of 2026-11-22, "when
turning a member both sides should be reverified"; the owner busy: built
on its own, reported; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#turns-weighed-over-every-joint-they-reach-l19)).

- **Listed by Orient angles** (format: the layout record's `plane_turns`
  [[member, roll before, roll with, kind, run]] — written only when there
  are rows, no version change; an older OHL-Structure drops them and the
  turns stay as written, unweighed): each run it turns from the planes.
  A row counts only while the member's roll is the one written with the
  turn (changed since: the user's, never taken back); pieces confirmed one
  part (their rolls averaged) average the rolls before alike, so that
  taking the turns back leaves them one roll; runs written one part are
  weighed as one, a run one part with a piece not listed is left as
  written; Orient angles from the outline alone takes the rows of what it
  sets.
- **Weighed by the layout run** (`LayoutSettings::weigh_turns`, on;
  `ohl_structure_link::weighed_turns`): the base (every turn taken back),
  then stage by stage — legs and chords, then face members — each turn
  kept only where every joint its members reach lays out no worse than
  before the stage (no fewer ends, not as many on more plates, not whole
  lost) and one better (the run's guard, a joint's wholeness added), and
  where no joint
  elsewhere laid out worse meets a member the layout turned otherwise
  beside it (a bracing's one roll turned for its end at the turned member);
  laid out again with the turns kept until they all still help (at most
  four layouts more per stage). A turn only by a run laying out every joint
  it reaches. The rows go with the run (a run again lays out the same).
  Lay out joints weighs once per preview on the whole tower (the proposals'
  effects laid out from the file so settled, every joint a turn kept
  reaches laid out with it); the turns taken back are said in the notes
  and offered by the window beside the other proposals.
- **Measured** (the 78 private towers; L17 main and L18 main reproduced):
  L17 → L18 unweighed → weighed: joints whole 37 315 → 38 042 → 37 796,
  member ends 133 265 → 135 259 → 135 194, plates 69 295 → 69 840 →
  69 763, members left after the clash rounds 11 179 → 11 670 → 11 179,
  joints better / worse than L17 3 461 / 2 400 → 1 679 / 122 (44 of them
  worse than the weighing's base, where no turn reaches and no member
  turned otherwise meets; the rest the base's own: pieces confirmed one
  part after the turns). Both weighed (the leg-rotation check's turns too,
  every third tower, 26): whole 12 161 → 12 382 → 12 342 (weighed 12 304),
  ends 42 967 → 43 587 → 43 797, plates 22 232 → 22 409 → 22 314, 828 / 90
  (L18 1 083 / 768). A run again identical on 8 of 8 towers. The time per
  tower (six towers, twice, load 2.6–7.6): the layout after Orient angles
  median 45.0 / 70.9 s unweighed, 265.7 / 335.3 s weighed (about five and
  a half layouts), 426.7 / 433.9 s both weighed — once per imported tower.
  Owner questions in the roadmap.
- **The owner, 2026-11-23**: asked about plates with several bends and
  welded assemblies of several plates — "go ahead to improve" (roadmap O44
  L19, item 3). Measured first (an upper bound from the reasons the layout
  gives for the ends it leaves, the weighed column, 78 private towers):
  6 780 ends whose own-plane welded plate would have their outstanding leg
  stand on the flat plate (not freed by a flap in their plane), 5 674 whose
  axis that plate would put more than a plate's thickness out (a joggle:
  two bends), 7 266 on an inner face towards the other leg (a plate
  wrapping the leg) — up to 5 130 joints whole if all were laid out. The
  format carries a chain of bends (tested: read as one part, drawn,
  weighed and checked bend by bend) and welded assemblies of any number of
  plates. Nothing built: a flap in the member's plane does not free an
  outstanding leg pointing into the flange, and a joggle does not take out
  a tilt (most of the second kind are more than 15° off); the axis offset
  taken into the analysis recommended first (owner question in the
  roadmap).
- **Not built**: a level or bent plate across two horizontals (L17's
  question 5, the roadmap's item 2) — counted only: 6 793 plan and hip
  ends lie off their host's flange with no roll laying them flat, 5 092 of
  them at a joint where two other horizontal members (or one and a leg)
  meet (an upper bound of what it could take); 3 282 have their axis out
  of the host's face.

## 2026-11-23 (joint layout: lay out by planes first, rolls from the joints' planes, L18)

**The owner's decisions of 2026-11-22** (roadmap O44 L18; the owner: "the
axes of the incoming members into a joint define planes together and we
should have the parts rotated accordingly and then shifted and either
bolted to each other when possible and if not with a new plate, and if
there are multiple planes … then we should go from high to low"):

- **Lay out by planes first**: approved.
- **On imported towers** (no orientation data) the rolls from the joints'
  planes may be set **automatically**; on towers designed in OpenOHL (rolls
  given by the designer) they stay **proposals**, never applied silently.
  What the file records decides: a roll set by the program — Orient angles
  (the layout record's `oriented`) or the layout (`rolled`), or no roll at
  all — is automatic; a roll, reference or orientation in the file without
  such a mark is the designer's. Nothing new is recorded (no format change):
  an import carries no member orientation and is oriented by Orient angles
  first, which marks what it sets.
- **Side by side**: the turn from the joints' planes is offered beside the
  leg-rotation check's (L11) in Lay out joints' preview and in Solve the
  clashes, each with its own tick and its measured effect; on the 78
  private towers both measured.
- **"When turning a member both sides should be reverified"**: any turn,
  automatic or proposed, lays out and checks every joint the member reaches
  (both ends of each piece; every joint along a leg's or chord's run), and
  its effect counts them all — a turn is never judged on one joint.

**Built** (2026-11-23, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#lay-out-by-planes-first-rolls-from-the-joints-planes-l18);
no format change):

- **The planes of a joint** (`joint_planes`): each other end's axis and the
  host's span a plane through the host's axis; ends within 2° (the tool's
  value, the owner's flatness) one plane; listed high to low (the biggest
  member, then the force where given — the structure file stores none —,
  then the number of ends).
- **Orient angles v2** (`plane_rolls`, the default; the outline alone kept
  selectable): each leg's, then chord's, then face member's run in line
  turned as one (an angle has one roll along its length) so that the most
  ends at all its joints lie within 2° of its flanges' planes, centred in the
  turns that keep them so, at most 22.5° from the outline's (heel out); the
  residual of every end at every joint reported. Measured on the 78
  private towers (L17 main → v2 automatic): ends within 2° of their host's
  flange plane 79.2 → 81.0 %, joints whole 37 315 → 38 042, ends 133 265
  → 135 259, plates 69 295 → 69 840, 3 461 joints better and 2 400 worse;
  L11's proposals applied 38 046 whole (plates 68 392, 2 776 / 1 414);
  both 38 317 (4 450 / 2 593); v2 with each run's turn kept only where every
  joint it reaches is laid out better 37 882 (ends 135 444, 1 935 / 293) —
  owner questions in the roadmap.
- **Lay out joints' default tick** for a plane turn of a run whose roll is
  the program's: on only where every joint it reaches is laid out better
  with it (the run's guard), else proposed — the owner's "both sides
  reverified" for the automatic case.
- **Plane by plane, high to low** (step 3): the plan already lays a joint
  out plane by plane (directly where every bolt lands, else one plate per
  plane); a rank's planes taken from the biggest member down measured worse
  (fewer joints whole, more plates) — a setting, off. Not built: the special
  passes rewritten as one general procedure; forces in the order (no
  analysis forces in the structure file).
- **Offered side by side** (step 4) as decided above.

## 2026-11-23 (joint layout: one plate in one gap; a turn tried as before the plates between, L17)

**The ends across one gap between a built-up member's angles share one
plate between them; a turn refused after writing is first tried with its
joints planned without the plates between** (roadmap O44 L17, L16's
questions 2 and 3; the owner busy: built on its own, reported; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#one-plate-in-one-gap-a-turn-tried-as-before-the-plates-between-l17);
no format change).

- **One plate in one gap**: the plan's plane of an end across a gap (L15)
  is the gap's own — its normal turned one way, its first back along it —
  rather than the back the end lies on, so that ends across it from either
  side, and those on the pieces of a member one part through the joint,
  share one plate between, each on its own face. Found: two plates in one
  gap (each end its own) ran into each other after writing; the joint was
  taken back and fell back to plans laying out less.
- **A turn refused after writing** (its member laid out at none of its
  joints, L16's question 2): where a joint of its member was planned onto
  a plate between, that joint is planned without them first (the run's
  guard, planned with them again where that lays out less there), each
  member once; refused only if it still helps none.
- **Tried, not kept**: the half turn onto a plate between for an end on a
  built-up member's angle's inner face running towards its other leg,
  weighed with the plates between (more joints worse than better).
- **Measured** on the 78 private towers (L16 main → L17): joints whole
  37 100 → 37 315, member ends 133 075 → 133 265, plates 69 391 → 69 295,
  members left after the clash rounds 11 366 → 11 179, not fitting as
  given 48 → 48, a run again identical 78 of 78; joint by joint 273 better
  and 47 worse (owner question); against L14 main 1 761 better and 321
  worse.

## 2026-11-22 (joint layout: the newest step never leaving a joint worse; the plan's face as drawn, L16)

**The plates between a built-up member's angles (L15) no longer change a
member's roll nor leave a joint worse through the run's fallbacks; an end
is planned on the face the joint details draw it on** (roadmap O44 L16,
L15's questions 3 and 4 and its item 4; the owner busy: built on its own,
reported; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-newest-step-never-leaving-a-joint-worse-the-plans-face-as-drawn-l16);
no format change).

- **A base member holds no plate where an end left with no connection
  bolts onto it** (L15's item 4): L14's condition (no end left as it is
  bolted onto the base member directly) now also reads each end as the
  file written gives it — what it bolts onto there, else the joint's leg
  worked out for it (`Arrival::joint_leg`, new) — not only as planned (a
  name the run gave while planning is not written for an end left as it
  is). The step is applied after the joint's old automatic values are out.
- **The turns weighed without the plates between**: the half turns (an end
  on the inner face, L10's other faces) are weighed on plans without the
  plates between (as before L15), the plans then made with them. Found:
  184 of L15's 218 worse joints had a member turned otherwise.
- **The fallback** (L15's question 3): planned again without the plates
  between also where the joint lays out as many ends on more plates; the
  fallback's ends searched for other members to bolt onto as before L15
  (L1 d), those names written only when the joint falls back; where the
  fallback lays out less than the plan with the plates between, that plan
  is taken again and kept (the best plan already known). The guard's
  measures worked out again at every planning of a joint, and kept for the
  plans weighed for L10's turns.
- **The plan's face as drawn** (L15's question 4,
  `LayoutSettings::seat_as_drawn`, on): the face from `joints::seat_face`,
  the joint details' own seat rule, against the member the layout lays the
  end onto (before: the face it sat on what it bolted onto while planning,
  none for an end naming nothing that does not lie flat on the joint's
  leg — the outer face taken).
- **Traced, not changed** (L15's question 6): the 41 mm from a 60 mm leg's
  toe is the bundled code plugin's edge distance (ASCE 10-97 4.5.1 Eq.
  4.5-1 and 4.5.3 Eq. 4.5-7) with the force per bolt, without an analysis,
  the bolt's own design shear capacity (4.3.2); more conservative than the
  code needs where the bearing limit of 4.4 caps the force a bolt can pass
  into the thin part (owner question; a plugin's value, not changed).
- **Measured** on the 78 private towers (L15 main → items 1 and 2 → with
  the face as drawn): joints whole 37 059 → 37 031 → 37 100, member ends
  133 015 → 133 060 → 133 075, plates 69 226 → 69 197 → 69 391, members
  left after the clash rounds 11 670 → 11 744 → 11 366, not fitting as
  given 50 → 48 → 48, a run again identical 78 of 78; joint by joint
  against L14 main 218 worse → 81 (1 490 → 1 517 better); the face as
  drawn alone 227 better and 221 worse (owner question); the time per
  tower +2 % to +3 %.

## 2026-11-22 (joint checks: a member's own steel and its plate under the force followed through, L14's question 2)

**The owner's answers of 2026-11-22**: L13's questions 1 to 7 approved as
recommended ("for L13 go with recommendations"); L14's question 2 — **yes**
("you should check the impact on the bolt on the other member to make it
safe"); L14's other questions (1, 3 to 6) not answered explicitly: kept as
built and recommended.

**At a member's own end bolts that carry ends laid onto it, its own steel
there and a plate's own checks under those bolts now take the force followed
through** (built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-groups.md#the-force-through-a-members-own-end-bolts-l14)).
No format change; **no plugin interface changed** (the code plugins'
member capacities, read once per structure, and their joint checks as
before).

- **The member's own steel** (`joint_groups::EndSteel`, *Part* "its own
  steel at its end bolts with … laid onto it"): its tension capacity as the
  code's plugin gives it — the least over its ends of its net section, block
  shear and bolts — times the case's strength factor, against the larger of
  its own force alone and the resultant of its own and the riders' forces
  (each along its line, the same case). On the safe side: the least
  capacity, the resultant's whole size along the member. The member check
  itself is unchanged.
- **A plate's own checks under those bolts** (`plate_checks::bolted_force`):
  the larger of the member's own force and the resultant's size, along the
  member's line; where the resultant governs and turns more than 15° off
  that line (`RESULTANT_TURN`, the program's value) the plate's sections
  are taken across a line the force does not follow — said NOT ON THE SAFE
  SIDE on the row with the angle.
- **The NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE row** ("…'s own steel at its end bolts … is
  checked under its own force only") is gone where covered. **What remains,
  said**: no tension capacity from the code's plugin (or no plugin) — "NOT
  CHECKED, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: …'s own steel at its end bolts …"; the
  plate's sections under a resultant turned more than 15°; ends laid onto a
  member that bolts onto nothing or whose bolts are not placed (as before).
- **Measured** (the 72 private towers with loads, one vertical case, L14
  main's laid files): 414 NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE rows → 0, replaced by 414
  checked rows (usage median 0.12, the largest 0.47, none over 1); 28 plate
  rows' usages change, all up (the largest +0.104, 0.016 → 0.120), none
  newly failing; 10 of those said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for a resultant
  turned more than 15°.

## 2026-11-22 (joint layout: a plate between a built-up member's angles, L15)

**An end across the gap between a built-up member's angles goes onto a plate
between them, as thick as the gap** (roadmap O44 L15, L14's item 3 — J6's
rest; the owner busy: built on its own, reported; built, in active
development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#a-plate-between-a-built-up-members-angles-l15)).
**Format: structure file version 25**, a plate's `between` (it lies between
the angles of the built-up member it is `on`); older files read unchanged,
written at 25 only when a plate says so.

- **Which ends** (`LayoutSettings::between_plates`, on): onto a built-up
  member whose angles are known, the leg bolted flat (within 2°) on the
  back of one angle that faces another across a gap, the outstanding leg
  pointing across it (L13's seat by the plane puts plan members there).
- **The plate**: on that back, as thick as the gap (the section's), laid
  out only where the gap is at least half the thickest leg on it
  (`BETWEEN_LEAST`, the program's value — owner question); a plane of its
  own; the ends on its far face pulled back clear of the other angle (the
  member's own steel across the gap now in their way); never bolted
  directly in the gap.
- **Its own bolts** through the plate and both angles back to back (two
  shear planes in the joint checks, unless given; one in a star); the plate
  may grow along the member in the gap round them, the grown outline
  checked clear.
- **Weighed**: the plan without is taken where it lays out more ends, or as
  many on fewer plates; **on a tie the plate between** (concentric with the
  member, its bolts in double shear) — an approved order (the clear rule's
  tie to the plan without) changed, said.
- **Drawn and checked**: the joint details seat such a plate on the back of
  the angle its members look across, in that back's plane; the clash check
  tests it against the member it lies between (before, a plate and the
  member it lies on were never tested).
- **Found**: an end naming nothing it bolts onto was planned on the outer
  face of the angle the joint details seat it on by its inner face (the
  plate planned in the gap, drawn outside it); such ends across a gap now
  go onto the plate between.

- **Measured** on the 78 private towers (L14 main → with it): joints whole
  35 964 → 37 059, member ends 130 902 → 133 015, plates 67 928 → 69 226,
  members left after the clash rounds 12 260 → 11 670, joints that do not
  fit as given 50 → 50, a run again identical 78 of 78; joint by joint
  1 490 better and 218 worse (owner question); 3 327 plates between the
  angles; the joint checks of their members' bolts fail as often as the
  run's other plates' (5 % of rows against 6.9 %), checked as thick as
  they are.
- **Also**: the run's guard (L11's way) plans a joint again without the
  plates between where it was laid out with fewer ends after writing than
  its plan without them (`PlanCtx::no_between`), tried before the guard
  that plans it as before L1.

## 2026-11-22 (joint layout: the base member's end bolts as the gusset's holding bolts, L14)

**Where nothing runs through a joint, the base member's own end bolts are
bolted onto the gusset lying on its flange and hold it** (roadmap O44 L14,
the owner's answer of 2026-11-22 to L12's question 3, also L10's question
5; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-base-members-end-bolts-as-the-gussets-holding-bolts-l14)).
**Format: structure file version 24**, a plate's `held_by` (the member whose
own end bolts onto it hold it); older files read unchanged, written at 24
only when a plate names one.

- **The rule** (`LayoutSettings::base_holds`, on): a member left by hand only
  because its bolts join nothing, with a flat plate of the plan on its own
  flange, bolted by one leg, no end left as it is bolted onto it directly:
  its end bolted onto the plate (its bolts onto the flange the plate lies
  on, unless its leg is given as the other), the plate `held_by` it. The
  plate's own provisional bolts onto it (L5o), where planned, become its
  end bolts (one gauge line, an even pitch: bolts,
  gauge, pitch, end distance written, provisional); else its own bolts as
  drawn; the plate's own that cannot be so written: as before.
- **Applied as a plan is written**, after the plans are weighed — applied
  while planning, the end gained chose plans with more plates (16 joints
  worse on six towers); at writing none worse (an approved order changed,
  measured).
- **The joint checks** take that member as the plate's holder (its bolts the
  holding bolts, its flange's bearing under them); ends laid onto it are not
  followed through its bolts (it holds a plate). Drawn: the member not moved
  by the plate on its own flange.
- **Measured** on the 78 private towers (L13 main → with it): bolts joining
  nothing 3 303 → 2 833 ends, 121 plates held by their base member, joints
  whole 35 940 → 35 964, member ends 130 779 → 130 902, plates 67 917 →
  67 928, joint by joint 108 better and 11 worse, joints that do not fit as
  given 48 → 50, a run again identical 78 of 78; the
  members left after the clash rounds 11 875 → 12 260 (such ends whose bolts as
  drawn run into steel near the work point, put back, by hand as before).

## 2026-11-22 (joint checks: the force through a member's own end bolts, L14)

**Where an end is bolted onto a member that ends at the joint, that
member's own end bolts carry the end's force with its own** (roadmap O44
L14, the owner's answer of 2026-11-22 to L13's question 3; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-groups.md#the-force-through-a-members-own-end-bolts-l14)).
No format change; the code plugins' interface unchanged (`joint-check-groups`
takes the new group as any bearing group).

- **Which ends** (`joint_groups::riders`): every end bolted onto a member
  that ends at the joint — not a leg, not a member a plate's own bolts
  name, not running on as one part; pieces in line not said continuous
  end there (on the safe side, as before); a chain followed, each member
  once; two members lapped onto each other left out (their one
  connection).
- **The force**: the member's own end force at its bolts plus each such
  end's along its line through its own bolts' centroid, the same case,
  with their moment about the bolts' centroid, shared elastically — each
  bolt the **larger** of that and the member's own force alone (another's
  force relieving the bolts not counted on: on the safe side; a bolt's
  force can only grow). Followed through in the group of what the member
  bolts onto, a plate's holding bolts (the ends added to the plate's
  resultant) and a welded plate's welds (the ends on the member's side).
- **A group of its own** (`PlatePart::EndBolts`, "its end bolts with … laid
  onto it"): each bolt's shear, its bearing on the member and, onto a plate,
  on the plate, the distances along and square to its force; "does not
  fit" as the other groups say it.
- **Still NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE, said** (a row of the joint without a
  usage): the member's own steel at those bolts (net section, tearing out)
  and a plate's own checks under them take the member's own force only.
  Ends laid onto a member that bolts onto nothing at the joint, or whose
  bolts are not placed: NOT CHECKED, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE (before: silent).
  The layout run's note says what is left.
- **Measured** on the 72 private towers with loads (L13 main's laid-out
  files, one vertical case, the bundled plugin): 414 members' end bolts
  get their own group (usage median 15 %, the largest 78 %, none over
  100 %); of the rows before, 5 usages change (3 holding, 2 bearing), all
  up — the largest a plate's holding bolts 54 % → 137 % (now failing) —,
  200 rows that do not fit carry a larger force; 685 ends laid onto a
  member bolting onto nothing and 182 onto a member whose bolts are not
  placed now said not checked. The layout is unchanged (only the words
  of the run's note).

## 2026-11-22 (joint layout: leg and chord turns offered with a tick, L13)

**The leg and chord turns the joints ask for are offered in Lay out joints'
preview with a tick each, and the chord turns in Solve the clashes; the
disagreement of Orient angles' chord turn with the joints traced** (roadmap
O44 L13, the owner's answers to L12's questions 4 and 5; built, in active
development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#leg-and-chord-turns-offered-never-applied-silently),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md#leg-or-chord-turned-against-its-joints)).
No format change.

- **Lay out joints**: every leg piece (L11) and chord piece running on
  (L12) whose joints say it is turned, from the file as it is, with a tick,
  **off by default**; ticked, the preview is worked out with the turns (the
  pieces in line turned alike) and says the run with and without them
  (measured, the layout run both ways); Apply writes them with the layout,
  one undo step. The run's own chord turns (`chord_turns`) stay off.
- **Solve the clashes** offers a chord piece at the joint as it offers a
  leg piece, its solution worked out with the turn, ticked off.
- **Orient angles against the joints, traced** (78 private towers): every
  flagged chord piece Orient angles set (839) is flagged by exactly half
  its faces' difference from square — Orient puts the legs' bisector on the
  faces' bisector; the joints' estimate counts only the ends bolting onto
  the piece and asks for one flange in their face, the other then twice as
  far off. A rule tried (a flange in the face that alone has members ending
  on the chord) changed 2 of the 839: not a fix at no cost; left as built,
  the turn weighed per chord (the tick).

## 2026-11-22 (joint layout: an end on a built-up member seated by the plane its axis lies in, L13)

**The joint details choose an end's leg bolted on a built-up member by the
plane its axis lies in, and choose it against the member the layout plans
it onto where it names nothing** (roadmap O44 L13, the owner's answer to
L12's question 2; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#an-end-on-a-built-up-member-seated-by-the-plane-its-axis-lies-in)).
No format change; every file's joint details read it so.

- Onto a built-up member whose angles' flanges' planes hold the end's axis
  in one of them (within the owner's 2°): the leg lying in that plane.
- Bolting onto nothing named: its leg chosen against the member running
  through the joint (what the layout plans it onto) — before, its long leg,

## 2026-11-21: an older project's lines kept as differences upgraded on their whole state

**A project of before 2026-11-15 with project lines kept as differences
opens** (roadmap O17's follow-up; found by phase 14's second real line,
refused at import with "the project has no line"; built, in active
development, not approved yet; [data model](data-model.md#project-lines-kept-as-differences-schema-6)).
No format change.

- The objects' upgrades of an older project (routes and alignments,
  alignment points, the load case sets read into structure groups; done
  once, `ols_meta` `routes_alignments`, `alignment_points`,
  `structure_groups`) ran on each project line's rows. A line kept as
  differences (schema 6, `vc_ref.base`) holds only what it changed — no
  settings row `line` of its own — so its rows were taken for a line and
  refused: the whole project did not open, in the network's import and in
  OHL-Design alike (a bug of the session, not of the file or the importer
  plugin).
- Now a line with a base is upgraded **on its whole state** (its base
  revision's objects with its rows laid over them, as it is read), and
  what the upgrade changes is written **as its own rows**: an object
  changed becomes a row, one left out a tombstone when the base holds it
  (a row deleted otherwise) — the same rule as every command on such a
  line. Lines keeping all their objects are upgraded as before.
- The upgrades are **marked done once every line is upgraded** (before:
  with the lines keeping all their objects, before the others were read);
  an open failing between upgrades again, which changes nothing already
  upgraded.
- Tested on an invented project of the same shape (old load case sets
  committed on main, a line started from it with one move): refused with
  "the project has no line" before, open after, the line's groups those
  of main, its move kept, opened again nothing added twice. The real line
  refused in phase 14 now imports (measured locally only).

## 2026-11-21 (country server: the web viewer's sign-in, the Offline working set window, schema 8)

**The web viewer's "Sign in with your organisation", OHL-Design's
Offline working set window for a network, and network schema 8
deleting the branches' old rows of the spatial index** (ROADMAP O17:
phase 15's "left" and its owner questions 2 and 8, phase 12's "left";
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[the web viewer's sign-in](../user-guide/sign-in.md#in-the-web-viewer),
[the window](../user-guide/offline-working-set.md),
[what the provider must allow](../user-guide/server-deployment.md#sign-in-with-the-organisations-accounts-oidc),
[the security review](server-security-review.md#the-web-viewers-sign-in-2026-11-21)).

- **The web viewer's sign-in** (phase 15's question 8, recommended
  "build it next"): when the network's server takes OIDC sign-ins, the
  join page asks it (`sign_in_options`, on a WebSocket of its own) and
  offers **Sign in with your organisation ↗**: the authorization code
  flow with PKCE (S256) in the tab (`web/signin.js`), the page's own
  address `https://HOST:PORT/` the redirect; the provider's endpoints from
  its discovery document (its `issuer` the server's); the code exchanged
  at the token endpoint from the page; the ID token's issuer, audience
  and nonce looked at; then the join with the ID token (the protocol's
  `join` with `id_token`, as OHL-Design's), renewed with the refresh
  token after 50 minutes. **Tokens in the page's memory only**; only the
  one-time values of the sign-in under way (verifier, state, nonce, the
  token endpoint, the user name — no token) wait in the tab's session
  storage while it is on the provider's page, removed when it is back,
  and the code leaves the address bar at once. **The page's
  `connect-src`** gains the provider's origin — the scheme, host and port
  of the configured issuer (`web::provider_origin`: HTTPS, or plain HTTP
  to this computer; a plain host name), never the request's. **The
  provider must allow** the page's address as a redirect and its origin
  on the discovery document and the token endpoint (CORS); a provider
  whose token endpoint is on another origin than its issuer is not
  reached from the page (said; **accepted**, a narrower policy). Tested
  against the fake provider on the loopback (now also accepting a page's
  `https://127.0.0.1:PORT/` redirect and answering CORS for one allowed
  origin) with a network's server on a throwaway cluster: the policy
  (the request's `Origin` ignored), the page's question, CORS for the
  page only, **the page's own `signin.js` run in Node.js** when installed
  (else the same steps in Rust): the authorize address, a forged
  `state`, a code used twice, a sign-in older than 10 minutes, the
  renewal, what waits across the provider's page; the join over the
  page's WebSocket with the token, the same token under another user's
  name refused. The page's glue (`app.js`) is checked to parse; it was not
  driven in a browser here.
- **OHL-Design's Offline working set window** (phase 12's "left"):
  Versions › Offline copy gains four entries for a network's working set,
  each opening the window at its step — **1 Export for offline work**
  (joined: the server's `export_working_set` on this connection, the file
  written where the user says, never over a file), **2 Check offline**
  (the exported file open: `offline_checks::check_offline`, the server's
  code, on a thread of its own), **3 Make the bundle** (the file open:
  `Session::offline_bundle`, uncommitted changes refuse it), **4 Bring the
  work back** (joined: the server's `import_bundle`). **A stale export**
  is said first, in red, with the objects changed meanwhile (the
  server's `changed_meanwhile`), and what it means; bringing back says
  in red what changed on the server meanwhile (conflicts with main, the
  read-only neighbours changed since). The answers of the server come on
  the joined link and wait in the working set's state for the window (by
  their id); one that comes after its window stopped waiting is said in
  the status line (an export recorded then writes no file: export
  again). The tool windows' rules: a sentence, (?) and User guide ↗, every
  setting with its (?), one button row (the step's action first, Cancel
  last; Enter runs no step), Escape cancels, reports in boxes that
  scroll. To run the checks without the database, `ohl-server` has a new
  feature **`offline-checks`** (`ohl-scope`, `ohl-clearance`,
  `ohl-loads`; `network` includes it), which OHL-Design turns on — no
  PostgreSQL client in the desktop. Tested against a local network's
  server (a throwaway cluster, a synthetic country of 40 pylons, the
  invented user `tester`): exported, a stale report shown, Escape,
  checked offline, the bundle made after a commit, brought back onto
  `offline-tester-…`, the same bundle twice refused; the user guide's
  pictures made from it as `USER=tester`.
- **Network schema 8** (phase 15's question 2, recommended "a clean-up
  of the old rows with the next migration"): a migration deleting the
  rows of `spatial` whose branch is not `main` — since 2026-11-20 nothing
  reads or writes them. It goes through phase 13's guard like every
  migration: refused without a backup newer than
  `backup_max_age_hours`, or `--i-have-a-backup` (audited). Tested on a
  database of schema 7 holding branch rows of two models: refused,
  nothing changed; after a real backup brought to 8, the branch rows
  gone, the main lines' kept and answering, in the audit; the same with
  `--i-have-a-backup`.
- **A layout test made exact** (O44 L9's loosened assertion):
  `one_roll_for_the_whole_member_lets_both_its_ends_lie_flat` now asserts
  what each joint gives — at N2, where the layout writes G1's outline
  round H's bolts, H lies flat on its plate (0.047°, the outline written
  to 0.1 mm over 61 mm) and G1 takes the 0.8° to L2's flange (within
  0.1°); at N7, G2 written without an outline, H lies 0.8° off its plane
  (the members' axes', as before L9). This agrees with the comment L9
  wrote; no behaviour changed.

> transaction (no `VACUUM`: the database's administrators or autovacuum
> give the space back)? → yes, as built.

## 2026-11-21 (joint layout: a plate read in its own plane, plates planned as written, L9)

**A plate's plane read from its whole outline, an end on a plate seated
where the plate's member is drawn, a welded plate's flat plate planned as
written, holding bolts on plates stopping short of the work point, the
run faster** (roadmap O44 L9, L8's questions 4 to 6 in L8's recommended
order, the owner busy; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#a-plate-read-in-its-own-plane-plates-planned-as-written-short-plates-held-l9),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md),
[joint details](joint-details.md),
[performance](performance.md#automatic-joint-layout-the-run-made-faster-o44-l9-2026-11-21)).
No format change.

- **A plate's plane** (the joint details; every file): a plate's outline
  given in the file lies in the plane of all its corners (Newell's
  method). Before, the plane of its first three corners — in a line, or
  nearly, where the outline runs straight there (often in an outline the
  run writes to a tenth of a millimetre): the members on it drawn on their
  other leg, their bolts along the plate. This was nearly all of L8's heads
  and nuts against plates after writing (an end's own bolts against its
  own plate). A plate's bolts are measured from its edges in that plane
  too.
- **An end on a plate on a member drawn off its line** (the joint
  details; every file): the ends are seated again while a member moves
  (L7) — now also where the moved member is the one a plate some end is on
  lies on (before only where an end bolted onto it directly): the plate and
  its ends lie on that member where it is drawn.
- **A welded plate's flat plate as written** (`LayoutSettings::reach_clear`,
  on; L8's question 5): planned with its outline as the run writes it
  (round the work point, the seams and the flange under them, the flat
  ends' bolts, cut at the heel), clear of the fixed steel and what the
  planes before laid out; else stopping short of the work point (the seams
  and the flange under them, the flat ends' legs from the flange's toe)
  and cut straight short of what it still runs into, kept where it still
  lies on the flange over half a square of its width; else the ends in
  their own planes left for a hand detail, said. Before: not checked. Of
  L8's two ways (as written, or cut short), both, in that order.
- **After writing** (the run): a flat plate's clashes are also the members'
  on the plates welded to it in their own planes. Before, such a plate with
  nothing bolted on it was nobody's and its clashes were written unsaid —
  **not on the safe side before L9**; fixed.
- **Holding bolts on a plate stopping short of the work point**
  (`LayoutSettings::short_holds`, on; the owner's answer to L6's question
  2): given (as L5o's) where the plate's outline, grown round them as the
  joint details draw it, still runs into nothing and keeps each of them
  its distances (the largest its plane's ends keep, and the code's for the
  member it lies on) from the edge; else none, said. Measured alone on six private towers: holding groups checked 1 747 → 1 835, plates whose holding is not checked 1 624 → 1 558, for 3 fewer joints whole and 18 fewer ends.
- **Faster, every number the same** (performance): the least-cut search
  clips a footprint only where a line crosses it; the joint details' model
  takes the sections' properties without their plastic moduli
  (`ohl_sections::Section::elastic_properties`, new; the finite-element
  crate's `Section::from_library` uses it — it never read them); a
  connection with more than two fields is not looked up as empty. All 78
  private towers' written files compared byte for byte: the same.
- Measured on the 78 private real towers (with the bundled plugin), L8 →
  L9: joints laid out whole 53.3 % → 55.8 %, ends 70.1 % → 71.0 %, plates 70 722 →
  69 295, heads and nuts against plates after writing 1 754 → 795 ends,
  plates into steel after writing 2 326 → 1 517, joints not fitting as
  given 42 → 53 (said by the joint checks), a run again identical 78/78
  (of the ends fewer than with the plates as written alone, most were
  laid out with a clash of their flat plate written unsaid); the time per
  tower (six towers, back to back) median 45 → 33 s.

## 2026-11-21 (joint layout: a joint planned where its members are drawn, the partners' bolts kept, L8)

**A member the run named but does not lay out planned where the file
draws it, the bolts of a member left as it is kept on the end it bolts
onto, the bolts already there found wherever the structure lies**
(roadmap O44 L8, L7's proposals 3 to 6 in L7's recommended order, the
owner busy; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#a-joint-planned-where-its-members-are-drawn-the-partners-bolts-kept-l8),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md),
[joint details](joint-details.md)). No format change.

- **As drawn** (`LayoutSettings::as_drawn`, on; L7's proposal 3, which
  fixes L6's question 7): the run names what an end bolts onto in its
  planning copy but writes the name only for ends it lays out. A joint
  with an end so named and not laid out is planned once more with the
  name taken out (the member where the file will draw it) — only those
  joints worked out again —, kept where it then lays out more ends, or as
  many on no more plates, and leaves no member it laid out or left for a
  hand detail unsaid; else planned as before. A `face` given by hand keeps
  the name. At most two such passes (`AS_DRAWN_PASSES`, the program's
  bound). Each joint so planned is said in the run's notes.
- **The partners' bolts** (`LayoutSettings::partner_bolts`, on; L7's
  proposal 4): an end the plan lays out onto a member left as it is that
  itself bolts onto the end (the mutual-host guard's pair) takes a cut and
  move only where every hole of that member stays within its flange, past
  its cut by the end distance, its own bolts the minimum spacing from them
  (the code's, else the default minimums: assumed); else it is left for a
  hand detail in the plan, said, its place not kept free — before, laid
  out and then taken back after writing. A member left by the run's own
  rounds is not asked. Kept although it lays out slightly fewer ends in
  all (the owner's question in the roadmap); tried and not kept: a
  per-joint guard planning without it.
- **Found measuring, fixed**: the bolts already there on a face (of the
  members not laid out) were placed with the joint's position added once
  more and so missed unless the face passed near the structure's origin;
  now kept clear of as intended (on the safe side).
- **Tried and not kept**: L7's proposal 5 (the members left for a hand
  detail kept clear to an end's outstanding leg's height and behind it):
  no change on six towers. Traced: nearly all heads and nuts against
  plates after writing are the end's own bolts against another plate of
  the joint. **Traced, not fixed**: L7's proposal 6 (a plate into a run lapped
  on the same face, its outline after writing reaching over the run). L5o
  on short plates: not reached.
- Measured on the 78 private real towers (with the bundled plugin):
  joints laid out whole 52.5 % → 53.4 % (as drawn) → 53.3 % (with the
  partners' bolts), ends 69.4 % → 70.7 % → 70.1 % (of more asked), the
  bent flats' bolts off their flat 228 → 37 → 39 ends, members left as
  they are no longer fitting 1 734 → 1 379 → 152, plates 69 154 → 70 860
  → 70 722, joints not fitting as given 35 → 35 → 42 (one joint on seven
  towers of one type), a run again identical 78/78; the time per tower
  (six towers, back to back) median 30 → 41 → 45 s.

## 2026-11-20 (joint layout: an end seated where its member is drawn, L7)

**An end seated on its member where that member is drawn, a plate's own
bolts named on the right leg at a joint like another, the measured columns
traced** (roadmap O44 L7, the owner's answers to L6 of 2026-11-20; built,
in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#an-end-seated-where-its-member-is-drawn-the-measuring-traced-l7),
[joint details](joint-details.md)). No format change.

- **The joint details** (`joints::member_seat`, `joints::nest`): an end
  lapped onto an angle lies on the face of that angle **as drawn** — the
  angle's own offset (seat, shift, drawing offset) taken across the face;
  the ends placed again with the offsets of the pass before until no
  member some end bolts onto moves (at most four passes, the program's
  bound); two ends bolting onto each other do not follow each other.
  Before, the face was taken as if the angle lay on its work line: an end
  on a member seated on a third floated off it, in the drawings, the clash
  check and the joint checks, and the automatic layout (which plans on
  the member as drawn) found clashes after writing. It changes the details
  of every file with such ends (levels 3 and 4); on the safe side.
- **A joint laid out like another** (`joint_kinds::map_hold_legs`): a flat
  plate's own bolts name the leg the map carries the representative's leg
  onto (under a mirror an angle's leg along its y can be the matched
  member's leg along its z); before, the name was copied and the bolts
  drawn on the other leg.
- **The measuring**: L5's measured "after" column ran with the bundled code
  plugin's bolt minimums (found from the folder the sweep started in), its
  "before" column and L6's without — not a regression, not a merge effect.
  From now on the measurements run with the bundled plugin, as the program
  ships.
- **Tried and not kept**: writing what the run named an end onto in its
  planning copy for ends it does not lay out (so that the bent plates' flats
  on such members agree with their bolts): those members' assumed bolts
  then count as given (the decision of 2026-11-19 on what is given) and
  the joints not fitting as given triple on a sample, for no more ends.
- Measured on the 78 private real towers (with the bundled plugin): joints
  laid out whole 51.9 % → 52.5 %, ends 68.4 % → 69.4 %, plates into steel
  after writing 4 089 → 3 117 ends, nuts into plates 1 519 → 1 204, joints

## 2026-11-20 (country server: the rest of the exports' thread and the sign-in window)

**An index by place in the session, a bundle's branch made ready on the
exports' thread, and OHL-Design's Sign in to a network window** (ROADMAP
O17: phase 14's "not built yet" and phase 13's sign-in windows, within
the owner's approvals of phase 12's question 6 and phase 13; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-the-rest-of-the-exports-thread-2026-11-20),
[user guide](../user-guide/sign-in.md),
[the security review](server-security-review.md#the-sign-in-windows-side-2026-11-20)).

- **The place index** (`ohl_session::places`): for the line worked on,
  each structure's routes (the rules of shared towers' function) and the
  structures of each route, the structures by cell of a 1 km grid, an
  upper bound of the longest span. A working set's extent looks only at
  the candidates it gives — the objects through a structure of the
  route; the structures in the area's bounds and the sections through a
  structure within the bounds grown by the longest span — and tests each
  exactly as the whole scan did, so **the extent is the same** (tested
  against the whole scan, `Session::set_whole_scan`, on every route,
  station ranges and areas of the in-place tests' line and of a
  synthetic country, before and after hundreds of random commands and
  moves across cells). Kept up to date by the commands applied in place;
  dropped (made again when next needed) on a change of routes,
  alignments, their points or the settings, a line made whole, a unit of
  work put back. On the country as one model an export's decision went
  from 0.76–0.82 s to 0.30–0.36 s; what is left is proportional to the
  working set and its area.
- **A bundle brought back on the exports' thread**: decided on the
  authority (verified against the export's record, its base read along
  the main line's: about 0.1 s on the one model); **its branch's line
  made ready on the "ohl-exports" thread** (`LineSource::prepare`: the
  model read whole and validated, its spatial, reference and tree
  indexes — offered to the session's `create_line` from that revision,
  the same line either way, tested); **applied on the authority** (the
  final apply, the same function as without the thread). The final apply
  stays on the authority because it changes the model — a branch, one
  command, a revision, the stream's position — and is decided by the
  user's rights and the other lines as they are, which only the authority
  holds; it costs what the bundle changes (0.1–0.3 s on the one model).
  **Changes of main landing meanwhile** are main's when it is applied:
  listed as its conflicts, exactly as on the authority — the line made
  ready is the export's base revision's, which no change of main alters,
  so nothing is replayed and nothing goes stale. **A user whose rights
  changed meanwhile gets nothing applied** (the refusal audited: bring it
  back again); a client gone gets nothing; brought back meanwhile by
  another connection: refused. Long work overdue 2 s still starts (one
  client's work on the thread at a time, exports and bundles alike).
  Tested: the same report and the same branch on the thread as on the
  authority (protocol and command line), a move landing while it is made
  ready a conflict, rights changed meanwhile nothing applied.
- **A network's database keeps the spatial index of each model's main
  line only** (`Store::spatial_kept`; a project file every line's, as
  before). Writing a whole model's index (108 773 rows) for each new
  branch was most of bringing a bundle back on a big model; nothing reads
  a branch's rows there (every query of the database is on the main
  line), and the session keeps a branch's index in memory
  (`Session::objects_in` answers from it). Rows of branches written
  before are not read and go with their branch. Bundles on the one model:
  10.7–22.8 s on the authority → 2.4–3.0 s asked → answered, a move
  meanwhile p50 6.8 ms, at most 243–285 ms.
- **OHL-Design's Sign in to a network window** (File › Join a network
  starts there): the invitation (its end said at once: *valid until …*,
  *expired on …*), the user name, and **Sign in with your organisation**
  when the server offers it — asked before joining with the new message
  `sign_in_options` (the server answers `sign_in`: its provider's issuer
  and client id; a server of before closes unanswered: invitations only;
  protocol 3 unchanged). The sign-in is the **authorization code flow
  with PKCE (S256) and a loopback redirect** (`ohl_server::sign_in`:
  a port on 127.0.0.1 for each sign-in, `state` and `nonce` checked, the
  provider's endpoints from its discovery document, HTTPS only). **No
  password in OHL-Design; tokens in memory only** (no keychain is used in
  the code base): the join, opening a working set and joining again carry
  the ID token, renewed with the refresh token after 50 minutes. Refusals
  are explained (reissued, expired, an account not mapped, another
  user's), the server's words kept under; errors in boxes that scroll;
  Escape cancels (a sign-in in the browser too); the tool windows' shape.
  Tested against a fake provider on the loopback (`fake_provider`, the
  browser played by the test) with a network's server on a throwaway
  cluster: options asked, signed in, joined, renewed, a refusal, a
  forged answer, a cancel; OHL-Design's window against such a local
  server through to the Join a network window, and its picture made
  from it as `USER=tester`.
- **Personal invitations end after 90 days by default** (phase 13's
  question 4, as recommended "once OHL-Design shows an expired
  invitation", which it now does): `ohl network serve --invite-days`
  defaults to 90 (`DEFAULT_INVITE_DAYS`), `0` until reissued; invitations
  given before keep their terms.
- **The web client** answers the same question on its socket (tested),
  but its page does not offer the organisation's sign-in yet.
- **Formats**: no schema change; the protocol gains `sign_in_options` /
  `sign_in` (data model); `bench-offline --during-reach` also measures a
  move while a bundle is brought back.

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-20; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. An extent narrowed by an index by place, every candidate tested as
> before (the same extent, tested)? → yes, as built.
> 2. A network's database keeps only the main lines' spatial index (a
> branch's in memory; rows of branches written before ignored)? → yes,
> as built; a clean-up of the old rows with the next migration.
> 3. A bundle decided and applied on the authority, its branch's line
> made ready on the exports' thread; the final apply on the authority
> (it changes the model, decided by the rights and lines as they are)?
> → yes, as built.
> 4. A change of main landing while a bundle is made ready: one of its
> conflicts; rights changed meanwhile: nothing applied? → yes, as built.
> 5. Personal invitations 90 days by default (`--invite-days 0`: until
> reissued)? → yes, as built.
> 6. The organisation's sign-in in the user's browser (code flow with
> PKCE, a loopback redirect), tokens in memory only, renewed with the
> refresh token; signing in again after OHL-Design restarts? → yes; an
> OS keychain only if users ask for it.
> 7. The sign-in question answered without a new protocol number (a
> server of before answers nothing: invitations only)? → yes.
> 8. The web client's sign-in: the provider must accept the page's own
> address as a redirect and its token endpoint from the page (CORS), and
> the page's security policy must name the provider → build it next,
> with the provider's origin added to the page's `connect-src`.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 14)

**Scale validation, and the offline export on a thread of its own the
owner approved the same day** (ROADMAP O17 phase 14 and phase 12's
question 6; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-14-scale-validation-and-the-exports-thread-2026-11-20),
[commands](../user-guide/network-commands.md#measurements-each-but-bench-scoped-edits-the-network-use-a-database-made-for-it),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#offline-working-sets-phase-12-in-active-development)).

- **The exports' thread** (owner, 2026-11-20: phase 12's question 6, "a
  thread of its own"): an offline working set's export is **decided on
  the authority** — the reach checked, the working set seen whole and
  exportable by the user's rights, main's unrecorded changes recorded
  first (a revision, phase 11's rule) and the base taken, the line's and
  the other lines' neighbours within the reach chosen by the same rights,
  the replica's rows, the meta and the export's number taken — all in
  one moment between two commands; it is **written on a thread of its
  own** (the neighbours' structure types merged in, the project file
  with its export revision, a client's file read back); it is **recorded
  and audited on the authority** when it comes back, and answered. The
  same plan and the same writer serve the authority's way
  (`NetOptions::export_worker` off), so the two cannot drift; tested:
  the report and the file the same either way, for a user seeing
  everything and one seeing a route, through the protocol and the
  command line's way.
- **Changes landing while it is written: marked, not replayed.** The
  file stays the base revision's working set, which its record names.
  Replaying a change into it would make the file differ from the
  revision recorded as its base, and a bundle made from it would carry
  that change back as the user's own — applied twice, or conflicting with
  itself; refusing the export would starve it while others edit. So each
  change applied on a main line while it is written is kept and compared
  with what it holds (its objects, its lines, its area's tiles) when it
  comes back: the report's `changed_meanwhile` counts the objects and
  `stale` says the server is newer than the file — exactly as if they
  had landed just after an export on the authority; bringing the work
  back lists them as conflicts with main or as neighbours changed since
  (phase 12). Nothing is lost, nothing applied twice. Tested: a move
  before an export in it; a move while it is written not in it, the
  export stale, its base and record unchanged.
- **A user whose rights changed while the export was written gets
  nothing** (the file removed, nothing recorded, the refusal audited);
  a client gone gets nothing. The rights are read again before it is
  recorded.
- **One client's export at a time** on the thread; a check queued behind
  it starts meanwhile (and the other way round): the first long work in
  the queue that may start goes, no longer only the first.
- **Long work overdue starts anyway** (found by the scale bench): with
  forty users editing at once the authority's queue of commands was never
  empty, and on main's code no check or export started while they
  edited. Long work that may start and has waited 2 s now starts between
  two jobs, at most once every 2 s (`HEAVY_MAX_WAIT`). A check's or an
  export's start holds the commands only for its snapshot or decision; a
  bundle brought back still for its length (seconds at most). Tested on
  the authority's loop.
- **A large first revision** (found measuring): a model's first revision
  in one transaction checked each blob's references by reading the rows
  written so far (the planner's statistics of nearly empty tables): more
  than 7 minutes for the synthetic country as one model, stopped there.
  The store reads the version store's statistics again (`ANALYZE vc_blob,
  vc_blob_use`, its own rows counted) after 2 000 blobs, then each time
  their number doubled: 25 s. Only statistics change.
- **Measured** ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-14-scale-validation-and-the-exports-thread-2026-11-20);
  a shared machine, main's code and phase 14's in turn, the quietest
  rounds): **a move while a whole route is exported with 10 km on the
  country as one model: on the authority it waited the whole export,
  1.40 s; on the thread p50 6.7 ms, at most 714 ms** (the decision; 102
  moves meanwhile); on the 147 lines 274 ms → p50 3.9 ms, at most 112 ms.
  **End to end** (`bench-scale`): 80 clients joining at once p50 3.8 s to
  their whole first view; 40 editors moving without a pause p50 200 ms
  a move (the authority applies about 200 moves a second); checks and
  exports asked meanwhile started after 60 s (when the editing stopped)
  with main's code, after p50 6.0 s with phase 14's — clearances answered
  in 21–26 s instead of 78–83 s, exports in 5.6–7.1 s instead of 60 s
  (stale: 43 and 44 objects changed while written); memory 1.31 GB idle,
  2.29 GB with everyone working; the start 2.4–2.6 s; a backup 6.2–7.2 s,
  a restore with its drill 8.4–10.0 s. Moves, replicas, joining again
  and the start as with main's code.
- **A line's library import** (found measuring a real line locally, its
  numbers kept private): mapping each library entry onto the country
  library read every file of its kind from the database and parsed it
  again — for each entry, and for each file laid in — quadratic in the
  files of a kind: minutes for a line with hundreds of tower files. Each
  file's entry ids are now kept on the connection by its text's SHA-256
  (read in PostgreSQL), a file read and parsed again only when its text
  changed: about a sixth of the time, the same mappings and requests
  (the import's report compared).
- **The report's format**: `OfflineExported` gets `changed_meanwhile`
  and `stale` (serde defaults: 0 and false from a server of before); the
  protocol stays 3; no schema change.
- **Not yet**: the export's decision is still on the authority — on the
  country as one model 0.7 s for a whole route with 10 km (the working
  set's extent and its neighbours' extent worked out over the whole
  model, the known per-model cost of O17's extents); a bundle brought
  back runs on the authority; a real country's lines measured on a
  server of their own (the private import measured locally only).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-20; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. An export decided on the authority and written on a thread of its
> own; a change landing meanwhile marks it stale instead of being
> replayed into the file? → yes, as built (a replay would make the file
> differ from the base its record names).
> 2. A user whose rights change while their export is written gets
> nothing (asks again)? → yes, as built.
> 3. Long work that has waited 2 s behind commands that keep coming
> starts anyway, at most once every 2 s (a pause of up to its snapshot or
> decision for the editors)? → yes, as built; a setting of the server if
> 2 s proves wrong in use.
> 4. The version store's statistics read again during a large first
> revision (ANALYZE after 2 000 blobs, then each doubling)? → yes, as
> built; a store reading many blob hashes at once later.
> 5. The export's decision on the country as one model (0.7 s) and a
> bundle brought back there (10 s) still on the authority? → for now;
> next an index by place in the session (the extents) and the bundle on
> the exports' thread.
> 6. Forty editors moving without a pause is the saturation measured
> (about 200 moves a second); is that enough for the country? → yes for
> now (a working day's edits are far fewer); measure again with the real
> country's lines once they are imported on a server of their own.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 13)

**Security, deployment, backups: a security review of the network
server with its fixes, OIDC sign-in as an option, invitations reissued
and expiring, backups with a restore drill, migrations refused without
a recent backup, TLS to a database on another host, Compose files; and
the checks' worker thread the owner approved the same day** (ROADMAP O17
phase 13; the plan's answer of 2026-11-16: "Compose and OIDC, the owner's
IT deciding" — both built as options; built, in active development, not
approved yet;
[the review](server-security-review.md),
[deployment](../user-guide/server-deployment.md),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#security-sign-in-and-backups-phase-13-in-active-development),
[commands](../user-guide/network-commands.md#operations-phase-13),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-13-security-backups-and-the-checks-worker-2026-11-20)).

- **The security review** ([its page](server-security-review.md)): 15
  findings, each with its fix and test or "accepted" with the reason.
  The decisions in it: **long work** (checks, exports, bundles) waits in
  a queue and runs only when no other job waits — one per user waiting,
  four in all (`--max-heavy-queue`), more refused with a message; **a
  check reads at most 10 km** around its working set (a plugin's largest
  declared reach; beyond, nothing more is read and the check is refused),
  a field's distance at most 2 km, rules' text 256 KB, 10 000 structures;
  **new tiles** 64 a second per client (256 at once,
  `--tiles-per-second`), 1 024 being made at once, the rest not made
  then and said; **lists**: 4 096 routes, 256 picks, 200 saved working
  sets a user; **large messages** (over 1 MB) within one budget of 256 MB
  for the server, a browser's at most 8 MB after its join; **IPv6**
  counted by its /64 for the limits per address; temporary files named
  by the server only; options and connections printed without the
  connection string or password.
- **Invitations**: a user's personal invitation has a generation (schema
  7, `net_user.invitation`); `ohl network rights reissue-invitation`
  (network admins, audited) makes a new one, refuses every older one and
  lets the user go; `serve --invite-days N` gives invitations valid to the
  end of a day (UTC). Both are inside the code (`G.UNTIL.MAC`, the MAC
  over the name, generation and day — nothing changeable without the
  key); invitations given before stay valid until reissued (generation 0
  without an end is the code of before). A refused valid code says
  "reissued" or "expired" (in the audit); a wrong one only "wrong access
  code".
- **OIDC sign-in**, an option (`serve --oidc-issuer --oidc-audience`):
  an ID token in the join (`id_token`) instead of a code, checked off the
  authority — the signature with the provider's keys (asymmetric only:
  RS*, PS*, ES256, ES384, EdDSA; never HS* or `none`), the issuer, the
  audience, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat` within an hour, a minute of leeway; the
  keys from the provider's discovery document over HTTPS (its CA, or the
  Mozilla roots; no redirect; 1 MB, 10 s), kept an hour, fetched again
  for an unknown key at most every 30 s, or from a file. **The subject
  is mapped to a user by a network admin** (`ohl network rights
  map-identity`, schema 7 `net_identity`); unmapped: refused. **Crates**:
  `jsonwebtoken` 11 (its pure-Rust crypto) and `ureq` 3 (rustls with
  ring) — widely used and maintained. Personal invitations stay the
  default. Tested with a key pair and a fake provider on the loopback (no
  network).
- **Backups**: `ohl network backup` — `pg_dump` (custom format) in a
  snapshot its own connection exports, each model's and the network's
  own tables' hashes read in the same snapshot, a manifest (schema, time
  of the data, the dump's SHA-256); recorded in `net_meta` `last_backup`
  (every schema has it), `net_backup` and the audit. **Chosen over a
  base backup with WAL archiving** (the ADR's first idea): a logical
  dump is what an `ohl` command can make and check alone, beside a
  running server, and restore into another major version of PostgreSQL;
  base backups and WAL archiving stay PostgreSQL's, for the IT
  department, beside it. `ohl network restore`: into an empty database
  only, of this program's schema only (another: restore it with its own
  program, then migrate), the dump's hash checked, `pg_restore` in one
  transaction, then **the restore drill**: every model and the network's
  tables compared with the manifest (a difference fails, naming it).
- **Migrations** (a program connecting, the server's start,
  `ohl network migrate`) are refused unless a backup newer than the
  network's `backup_max_age_hours` (24; `ohl network setting`) is
  recorded, or `--i-have-a-backup` is given (audited with its user); an
  empty database is made without.
- **TLS to the database** (`ohl_store_pg::connect`): libpq's `sslmode`
  (`disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`) and `sslrootcert`
  read from the connection string or `OHL_DATABASE_SSLMODE` /
  `OHL_DATABASE_CA`, rustls with ring (`tokio-postgres-rustls`); **a
  host that is not this computer is refused without TLS** unless
  `sslmode=disable` is said (warned once); no system or bundled roots
  (the owner's CA). The password from the string or
  `OHL_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE`; the PostgreSQL tools get it in their
  environment.
- **Compose** (`deploy/compose/`): PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.5 (the
  network's database owned by a role `ohl` without superuser, PostGIS
  made once by the superuser, no published port), the server (QUIC
  published, its key and counters in a volume), a backup job (every 6
  hours, 28 kept), healthchecks, fake example secrets read as Compose
  secrets; read by a test (YAML), not run here (no Docker). Not needed
  for the desktop.
- **The checks' worker** (owner, 2026-11-20: phase 10's question 1): a
  scoped check runs on a thread of its own from **a snapshot** taken on
  the authority when it starts — its working set and rights decided
  there; the tile index within its 10 km and a copy of each model's line
  with something there, their library, weather and load case files, the
  network's largest span margin — through the same answers the authority
  gives (each part `line_part`, the session's `drawing_part` of the same
  line); its report written on the authority with the client's rights
  when it comes back (a client whose rights changed was let go); **the
  changes applied meanwhile are kept and checked against its watch**: a
  result they touch is marked stale at once. Tested: every check's report
  the same on the worker as on the authority (a user seeing everything,
  one seeing a route); a move landing during a check either in the
  result or marking it stale. `NetOptions::check_worker` (on by default)
  keeps the authority's way for the measurements. **The offline export
  on a thread of its own (phase 12's question 6) is not built yet**: it
  records main's changes first and writes the export's record, both on
  the authority; next.
- **Schema 7** (both stores where it matters: the desktop's project file
  is unchanged, no session table touched): `net_user.invitation`,
  `net_identity`, `net_backup`, `net_meta` `backup_max_age_hours`. The
  protocol stays 3 (`join` gets `id_token`).
- **Measured** ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-13-security-backups-and-the-checks-worker-2026-11-20)): main's code against phase 13's on fresh databases of the 147 lines (a shared machine, the quietest rounds): a move applied and broadcast p50 9.2 → 8.4 ms (a route's designer 9.5 → 8.9 ms), a replica loaded 0.076 / 0.130 → 0.074 / 0.120 s, joining again after 20 moves 358 → 355 ms, the start 3.0 → 2.8 s; a backup of the 147 lines 7.0–10.6 s (13.6 MB), a restore with its drill 13.8–14.1 s; **a move while a whole route's clearances run (12 s): on the authority the first waited 12.08 s, on the worker p50 9.6 ms, p95 27.8 ms (836 moves meanwhile)**.
- **Not yet**: OHL-Design's and the web client's sign-in windows (the
  protocol takes the token); the export on a thread of its own; a role
  per task in the database (migrations, the server, backups); WAL
  archiving driven by `ohl`; OHL-Server's Operations page (stage F).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-20; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. Long work queued behind the commands, one per user, four in all? →
> yes, as built; with the worker a check no longer holds the edits.
> 2. A check reads at most 10 km around its working set, a field 2 km? →
> yes, as built.
> 3. 64 new tiles a second per client, 1 024 being made at once? → yes,
> as built; settings of the server.
> 4. Invitations reissued per user and with an optional end; the old
> ones valid until reissued? → yes, as built; make `--invite-days`
> (e.g. 90) the default once OHL-Design shows an expired invitation.
> 5. OIDC with jsonwebtoken and ureq, subjects mapped by network admins
> (no automatic accounts)? → yes, as built; automatic accounts from a
> group claim later if wanted.
> 6. Backups by `pg_dump` with a restore drill, WAL archiving left to the
> IT department? → yes.
> 7. A migration refused without a backup newer than 24 h, the override
> audited? → yes, as built.
> 8. A remote database refused without TLS unless `sslmode=disable` is
> said? → yes, as built.
> 9. Compose with a role without superuser, the server's image on
> PostgreSQL's (for `pg_dump`)? → yes; a slimmer image later.
> 10. The checks' worker: a snapshot of the lines within 10 km, the
> report written on the authority? → yes, as built; the export next.
