## 2026-11-20 (joint layout: ends moved to bolt directly L5)

**O44, L5** (built 2026-11-20, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#ends-moved-to-bolt-directly-one-bolt-through-the-leg-looked-into-l5),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md), [joint details](joint-details.md);
no format change). From the owner's idea of the same day ("move the 2
diagonal a bit forward maybe to have one bolt on the main leg without them
touching each other. The second bolt needs the plate anyway but maybe
shorter"):

- **One bolt through the leg, the rest on a shorter plate — not built.**
  Between a bolt through the member, the plate and the leg (on the flange)
  and one through the member and the plate only (past the toe, its nut
  clear of the flange) the bolts must lie apart across the flange by the
  edge distance, the nut and the gap — about three bolt diameters, the
  default pitch: only for members nearly square to the flange. Measured on
  six private real towers: 3.7 % of the plate ends; 63 % of the plate ends
  have one bolt. It would need a format field (version 24) for a bolt
  through three plies, followed by the joint details, the clash check, the
  joint checks and the bill of materials. Asked.
- **An end moved to bolt directly — built, a switch** (`direct_moved`, on):
  on a face going onto a plate, each end whose bolts do not land pulled
  back further, else moved sideways by at most the plate's thickness,
  until its bolts land; where every end of the face then lands, no plate.
  The move is the end's `shift` (in the analysis at level 4 and with the
  estimated eccentricities; at level 3 without them NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE,
  as every shift). **The limit, the plate's thickness**, on the safe side
  relative to the plate it replaces (that plate's own offset out of the
  flange, not in the analysis, is as large). Moving only some ends of a
  face off its plate: measured, left out (fewer joints whole, more
  plates). Up to the shift limit (30 mm): measured, not chosen (moves of
  18 mm median on top of L5; asked).
- **The clear rule (a guard)**: the joint planned with and without the
  moves, the moves kept only where they lay out more ends, or as many on
  fewer plates.
- **The bend check under design cases** (L3's question 4): measured with
  the line's load case library (three temperatures, ice ×1.3, wind 300 Pa
  ×1.5 from four sides with the wind on the bodies; checking values, not a
  design code's).
- **A packing plate under the bent flap** (L3b's question 4): measured,
  not built — it puts the member a further plate's thickness out of the
  flange, an offset not in the analysis (NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE until O45 D).

Measured on the 78 private real towers (the theory page): joints laid out
whole 49.7 % → 50.4 %, ends 65.0 % → 65.3 %, plates 65 878 → 61 800
(−6.2 %), the moves median 3 mm (at most 8), joints not fitting as given
26 → 28, a run again identical 78 of 78, about a quarter more time per
tower. The bend check under the line's
checking cases: L3's bends 80 % → 57 % pass, J2b's 49 % → 24 % (against the
one vertical case). The packing plate: +1.0 point of the joints whole on a
sample. The owner's questions, and the proposals to lay out more joints
(L5a–L5o, with one way to weigh them per joint), are in the roadmap (O44
L5).

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 12)

**The offline working set: exported with read-only neighbours, checked
offline, back as a bundle onto a branch over the working set; and phase
11's two open items — the rules of shared towers on edits made directly
on a network's main line, a branch's base read along what differs**
(ROADMAP O17 phase 12; the plan's answer of 2026-11-16: offline working
sets without reservations at first; built, in active development, not
approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md#offline-working-sets),
[data model](data-model.md#an-offline-working-set-phase-12-2026-11-20),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#offline-working-sets-phase-12-in-active-development),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-12-the-offline-working-set-2026-11-20)).

**Phase 11's open items, first:**

- **Edits made directly on main** (a safety gap: the rules of shared
  towers applied on branches only): a command on a network's main line
  (do, undo, redo, rollback) is checked by phase 8's rules against **the
  routes that are its user's** — through the same code path as a branch
  over a working set (`Session::with_command_routes`, then the session's
  own check of every command): a broken connection refused, naming the
  other route; a move allowed, the other routes marked stale (the model's
  `stale_routes`) and their connected owners told (`notice`); a protected
  main refusing it pending its owners' review (even a line admin's, as
  phase 11 decided for merges). **Decided here**: a user's routes are
  those the rights let them edit something on (from the assignments when
  they name routes, parts of routes, the line or the network — a route
  list's cost; from every object's place when a grant is on a region or
  an object, or a deny touches the line), narrowed to the working set
  their connection follows on that model, if any; a user who may edit
  every route of the line and follows no working set has no rule (as a
  project without working sets — the owner's question 1). Tested on both
  stores (the store suite's `shared_towers_on_main`) and on the server
  (a route's designer refused deleting the tower another route uses,
  naming it; her move marking the other route stale, its designer told;
  a network admin following a working set of one route refused on a
  protected main, without one allowed).
- **Opening a model with branches** read each branch's base revision
  whole. A base kept as a split tree is now **read along what differs
  from the main line**: the main line's tree kept as a commit keeps it
  (each object hashed once — the same work the first commit after
  opening did, which then costs nothing more), only the nodes whose
  hashes differ and the objects in them that differ read from the store,
  the rest taken from the main line's objects (their JSON shared); a
  flat base is read whole as before. The same for a line made from a
  revision (a bundle's branch). Tested: the same objects (places,
  versions, JSON, library files) as the revision read whole, every line
  the same after opening again. Measured below.

**Phase 12:**

- **The export** (`ohl network export-working-set`, the server's
  `export_working_set`): the working set picked as a join picks it,
  written by the server as a project file of today's format — a part of
  the line (`part`: the working set, editable; the rest read-only, the
  session's part refusing edits to it), with:
  - its **context** as a replica's (what solving its sections alone
    reads, what it refers to, its routes' alignments, the line's
    settings and library files);
  - **the line's own neighbours** within the export's area (every
    section with a span in it and what solving each reads), read-only;
  - **other lines' neighbours** in the meta key `network.neighbours`:
    for each line with sections in the area, what solving them reads
    (`Session::drawing_part`, structure types resolved, as the server's
    checks take it) with its wire, weather and load case files.
  **Decided here: the area** is the working set's bounds grown by the
  reach and three times the network's largest span margin — a rectangle,
  because a scoped check asks for exactly that shape (its wires' bounds
  grown by its reach and twice the margin), so what the server reads the
  file holds; **the reach** is 500 m by default (the field distance, the
  largest of the shipped checks'; `--reach` up to 10 000 m, a plugin
  reach's bound).
- **Its rights** (the one function): everything it holds seen (refused
  as a join is when the working set reaches what its user may not see);
  **export on each object of the working set** and something editable
  on each of its routes (a branch over them is made when it comes back);
  its context and neighbours seen only, as a join's replica holds them
  (the owner's question 3). **What its user may not see is left out and
  counted, never written**: another line's section whose solve reads a
  hidden object (section by section), a neighbour line's library file it
  may not see, and — **decided as conservative** — the line's own
  neighbours all left out when one of them is hidden.
- **Its base** is the model's main revision; **the main line's changes
  not recorded in a revision are recorded first, by the exporter, by
  phase 11's rule for a branch over a working set** (a commit records
  only what its user may edit: otherwise refused, "ask whoever may edit
  them all to commit the main line" — the owner's question 2).
- **Recorded**: the file's first revision is the **export's revision**
  (by the exporter, its message naming the export's number and the base);
  the server keeps a row per export (`offline_export`, **network schema
  6**, with its migration tested on PostgreSQL): its model, user, base,
  export revision and that revision's tree text — each exported object by
  the hash of its JSON, no object copied —, the working set's objects,
  routes and picks, the reach, the bundles brought back. In the audit
  (`export working set`). **No reservation** (the plan's answer).
- **Written on the authority** between two commands (synchronously: the
  owner's question 6), into the requester's file (the command line) or
  sent in the answer (the protocol: base64, within a message's 64 MB).
- **Meta keys added** (the desktop's format unchanged): `network.offline`
  (the export's record: network, model, user, time, base, export, picks,
  routes, reach, area, the network's largest span margin, library pins,
  what was left out, the neighbours' counts), `network.neighbours`, and as
  a replica `network.name`, `network.line`, `network.position`,
  `network.working_set`, `network.library_pins`.
- **Checks offline** (`ohl network check-offline`,
  `ohl_server::offline_checks`): the scoped checks of phase 10 run on the
  file with the neighbours it holds, through **the server's own code**
  (the check's run and its report moved into one module both use:
  `scoped_report`; nothing of the computation changed) — the same report
  as the server's for a user who sees what the file holds (tested to the
  bit: clearances between wires and shared towers' loads on the
  synthetic country, the counts and every violation equal). **NOT ALL
  CHECKED** where the file cannot give the server's result: neighbours
  left out (computed on the server only), a check asking for an area
  beyond the export's (its working set moved or grown offline, a larger
  reach).
- **The bundle** (`ohl network offline-bundle`,
  `Session::offline_bundle`): the existing bundle format, holding the
  main line's revisions since the export's and only the blobs they need
  that the export does not hold (an object as exported stays behind) —
  never the exported state again. Uncommitted changes refuse it (they
  would not come back).
- **Bringing it back** (`ohl network import-bundle`, the server's
  `import_bundle`):
  - its base is the one revision its revisions come from; a base the
    network did not record is refused, as is another user's export;
  - verified as any bundle (every blob against its hash, every revision
    against its id, every parent the export or in the bundle, every tree
    whole: `ohl_session::offline::offline_changes`); what it changes is
    the difference between the export's revision and its head — objects
    put or deleted (a place among a kind changed alone is not a change);
  - **refused, nothing applied**: a library file changed (library files
    change on the network: requests); an object that was read-only in
    the file changed (its context, its neighbours, the line's settings);
    a bundle brought back already (its head recorded with the branch);
  - applied on **a new branch over the working set made from the
    export's base revision** (`CreateWorkingSetBranch`, whose `from` may
    now be a revision of the model: phase 11's rights, team and rules) —
    **never on main** — as **one command** (its puts and deletes, no
    cascade) decided by **the user's rights as they are now** and the
    rules of shared towers with the working set's routes, validated
    where it changes, then **committed** (its message naming the export
    and listing the offline revisions; the offline revisions themselves
    are not kept: they hold a part of the line). A refusal at any step
    takes the branch away again and is audited, naming nothing hidden;
  - **conflicts with main listed, never settled**: the objects it
    changes that changed on main since the export (named only when its
    user may see them; "an object you may not see" else) — merging the
    branch into main asks to settle them; and how many of the read-only
    neighbours changed since (checks made offline are out of date). In
    the audit (`import bundle`).
- **OHL-Design**: its Offline copy menu for a joined network is **not
  built** (the size of the work: the export, the file's transfer, the
  bundle's way back and the branch's window together); the command line
  and the server's messages do it. OHL-Design shows a note if such an
  answer comes.
- **Tests**: the session (a bundle holding only the changes; a bundle
  changed by hand, cut short, from another base, with nothing after the
  export: refused; the context read-only offline); the store
  (`schema_5_brought_to_6`: an export recorded, found, a bundle noted, the
  same export twice refused); the server: an export through the protocol
  and the command line's way (a user seeing everything: nothing left out;
  a route's designer: the other lines left out, counted, never written,
  her checks offline NOT ALL CHECKED); the checks offline equal to the
  server's; a bundle brought back onto a branch from the base, main
  unchanged; a conflict listed; refused, nothing applied, audited: a
  value changed by hand, an unknown base, another user's export, a
  read-only neighbour changed (the file's part opened by hand), the same
  bundle twice, an edit to an object the user may not see (a new object
  of a hidden id, refused without naming it), a bundle after the user's
  rights were taken away; **the property that no message holds a hidden
  id or place extended to exports**: each round's export asked (refused
  or written) and brought back, the file's objects, neighbours, record,
  users and working set scanned as the messages are, and a last round
  sure to export (a route's designer with hidden lines near).
- **Measured** ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-12-the-offline-working-set-2026-11-20)):
  the whole route of a line (145 structures, 1 576 objects) exported with 15 other lines' 3 222 sections near in 0.25 s (the first 0.93 s), a file of 7.7 MB; bundles of 20 and 500 changes made in 62 / 90 ms (0.32 / 4.9 MB) and brought back in 0.29 / 0.66 s; the country as one model opened with its two branches 20.8 s → 4.7 s; main's code against phase 12's on fresh databases of the 147 lines: a move applied and broadcast p50 9.1–9.3 → 8.5–8.6 ms (a route's designer 9.5–9.6 → 8.6–8.9 ms), a move with a working set followed 15.0 → 15.0 ms, a replica loaded 0.079 / 0.119 → 0.078 / 0.125 s, joining again after 20 moves 358 → 360 ms, the start 2.7–2.8 s both.
- **Not yet**: OHL-Design's Offline copy menu for a network; the export
  written on a thread of its own; OHL-Design's check windows using the
  neighbours a file holds (the command line's `check-offline` does);
  plugin checks offline with their neighbours; the line's own neighbours
  left out section by section (now: all when one is hidden); point
  clouds and terrain in an export; a server-made revision of main's
  changes so that any designer may export (now: whoever may record them).

> **Owner:** (answered 2026-11-20: as recommended — [the owner's entry](#2026-11-20-owner-country-server-phases-7-10-11-and-12--recommendations-approved); the recommendation after the arrow)

## 2026-11-20 (owner): country server phase 9's 10 recommendations approved

The owner, 2026-11-20: "go ahead with recommendations" — the ten
questions of [phase 9](#2026-11-20-country-server-phase-9) answered as
recommended:

1. A release changes no line; lines in design follow the latest by
   `update-pins --following` and are shown behind (explicit; a setting
   later if wanted).
2. Unlocking a kind by network admins only (maintainers may lock).
3. A request granted only by a maintainer other than its requester.
4. A pending draft "replaced" means taken out of the branch; a request
   withdrawn still blocks while its draft is in the branch.
5. A built line's pins moved by whoever may review the whole line; a
   library review flow with OHL-Server stage D.
6. Update library pins not undone by Undo (updated back to the release
   before).
7. A withdrawn entry stays in later releases and is never newly used;
   using routes marked "not on the safe side" when the app shows library
   notices (OHL-Server stage D).
8. The import adds new entries of kinds not locked, asks for the rest,
   the model keeping its own files until Update library pins.
9. A draft in the requester's own branch, and in a team's branch with
   phase 11 — built with [phase 11](#2026-11-20-country-server-phase-11).
10. A line's library file filtered per entry with OHL-Server stage D;
    until then a deny naming an entry denies the line's file holding it
    whole (built the same day in the rights' one function, tested).

The branches' use index, left by phase 9, was built with phase 11 too.
Phase 7's eight questions are not answered yet.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 11)

**Version control at scale: split trees, branches over working sets,
merges at shared towers; the owner's questions of phases 7 and 9 left
"with phase 11"** (ROADMAP O17 phase 11; built, in active development,
not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md#versions-at-the-scale-of-a-country),
[data model](data-model.md#server-database-postgresql),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#branches-over-a-working-set-phase-11-in-active-development),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-11-version-control-at-scale-2026-11-20)).

- **Split trees** (`ohl_session::trees`, tree version 2): a revision's
  tree is a trie of the objects keyed by the SHA-256 of each object's
  kind and id — a leaf holds at most 64 objects, a fuller node is split
  into up to 16 children by the next hexadecimal digit (16 digits at
  most) — and a root naming its top node and listing the library files.
  **Decided here (the unit)**: the object's key, not its route or tension
  section. A route or a section is worked out from the line (an object's
  routes change with edits, a tower stands on several routes, a structure
  near an alignment counts for its route): a trie by route would move
  objects between subtrees with edits, need the whole line to be made,
  and could differ between two programs reading the line differently. A
  trie by key depends on the objects only, so the server, a replica and
  an offline copy make the same tree and the same revision id. What a
  route's commit, diff or merge reads is what changed in it: the nodes
  whose hashes differ and the objects in them.
- **A commit costs what changed**: the session keeps per project line
  each object's value hash with the JSON it was taken from (shared, never
  copied) and the nodes' hashes; a commit compares the objects by their
  shared JSON (a pointer each), hashes the changed ones, makes the nodes
  on their paths again and writes only the nodes and objects not in the
  parent's tree (read along the paths that differ). The first commit of a
  line after opening hashes every object once. **A failed unit is safe**
  without copying anything: what is written is decided against the
  stored parent, never against what the memory thinks was written (a
  commit rolled back with its unit leaves nothing missing; tested).
- **Where** (decided here, the desktop's format unchanged): a store says
  whether it writes split trees — PostgreSQL does, a project file does
  not (flat trees, the same bytes as before). Both are read everywhere:
  a model's flat revisions of before (its import) stay its history, and
  "nothing to commit", the status and the differences are told object by
  object across the two kinds. An exported model keeps its split trees
  (its revision ids, so a bundle comes back); this build reads them, an
  older build of the desktop does not (a question below). Bundles carry
  the nodes; a bundle missing one is refused before anything is written.
- **Diffs, ahead/behind and merge bases**: `Session::diff_revisions` and
  the status read only the nodes that differ; ahead/behind and the merge
  bases stay exact (one read of the history's parents, as before).
- **Merges from what differs** (`MergePlan::local`): with split trees, the
  working state committed and no object kept twice, the objects that
  differ between the base and each side are read alone, merged as whole
  states merge (the others are equal on all three sides) and laid over
  the working state; the connection conflicts of shared towers are worked
  out as on whole states. The merged line is **validated as a command
  is**, where it changes (phase 3's local validation; the merge refused
  and nothing kept otherwise) — not whole first; notes are checked
  against the line only when the merge touches what they are on. **A
  merge changing library files takes the whole way** (their entry-by-entry
  merge and the structure types' check read whole states). Bring in
  likewise, from the two project lines in memory.
- **Branches over working sets** (`ohl_session::shared::BranchScope`,
  `ols_meta` key `branch_scopes`; the server's `CreateWorkingSetBranch`):
  a project line made from another over a set of routes, by its maker,
  shared with a team (users or groups). It holds only its changes (as
  every line since schema 6). The rules of shared towers (phase 8) apply
  to every command on it with its routes as the working set; **its stale
  marks are written when its changes reach main** (a merge, a review's
  merge), not on the branch. Changes brought into it from main are not
  checked again (they were on main).
- **Merges at shared towers**: a merge of such a branch is checked by
  its routes where it lands — a connection broken is a conflict, named
  (always said where branches over working sets exist); a move marks the
  other routes stale (the merge's log entry says it) and the server
  tells the connected users who may edit those routes (a notice in words
  they may see); **on a protected line the merge waits for a review** —
  a direct merge is refused, "it needs a review by its owners", a
  review's merge (approved) goes through. Reviews of the whole line are
  its owners' (deciding a review needs review on the whole line).
- **Rights** (the owner's questions of phase 7, through the one function
  `ohl_session::rights`): **a commit needs edit only on what it records**
  — the line's changes since its revision, each decided as create, edit
  or delete (a branch made from a line with uncommitted changes records
  them first: the same rule); **a branch over a working set** is made by
  whoever sees each of its routes and may edit something on it; its
  commands, commits, reviews and merges are its maker's and its team's,
  deleting, renaming or describing it its maker's; **merging it into
  main needs only what the merge changes there**; changes brought into it
  from main are main's. **Decided here (conservative)**: tags, branches
  of the whole line (`CreateLine`, `CreateBranch`), rollbacks, reverts
  and reviews' merges still need the line whole; a commit's objects are
  placed as the server keeps them (main's), an object gone or made only
  on the branch decided by its own place or none (only a scope of the
  whole line covers it). **A designer of a part of a route makes new
  objects inside it** (question 1): a new object refused by the rights as
  they were is decided again with the user's parts of routes worked out
  on the line as it is after the command.
- **Team branches** (question 9 of phase 9): a pending library draft may
  be used in a branch over a working set whose maker named the requester
  in its team (users; a group's members work on it, a draft's requester
  is named). The draft is still put and changed only by its requester,
  and still blocks the branch's review and merge into main until
  granted.
- **Branches' use index** (phase 9's left item): `lib_use` rows of a
  branch (the column existed) for the objects it changed, as it holds
  them — never a copy of main's rows; renamed and deleted with it; read
  through the rights with the branch named, an object placed as on main
  (one made only on the branch: seen by who sees the whole line).
- **No schema change**: the network schema stays 5 (the branches' scopes
  are a model's meta row, the use index had its branch column, nodes are
  blobs). The desktop's `.ohl` format is unchanged.
- **Tests**: split trees against flat ones on a random script (5 seeds,
  150 steps: edits, notes, commits, project lines, merges with conflicts
  chosen at random, bringing in — the same answers, states, statuses and
  differences at every step); a commit writes what changed; a commit
  rolled back with its unit; flat and split revisions mixed, bundles with
  nodes (one missing: refused); merges from what differs; branches over a
  working set in the session (rules on the branch, stale marks at the
  merge, a protected main waiting for a review, renamed and deleted) on
  both kinds of tree; on the server: a branch of the whole line refused
  to a route's designer, over her route made, its team and maker, a
  commit recording only what its user may edit (a hidden object's
  refusal naming nothing), a tag needing the line whole, a part's
  designer making a new structure inside her part and not outside;
  branches' use index through the rights; and **the property that no
  message holds a hidden id or place** extended with branches over a
  working set made, worked on, committed and merged by another user and
  by the user herself.
- **Measured** ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-11-version-control-at-scale-2026-11-20)),
  flat trees (as phase 9's code writes them) against split ones on the
  same model: the country as one model (108 785 objects) — a commit of
  one changed route p50 6.7 s → 100 ms, its status 1.4 s → 107 ms, a
  branch's diff 134 → 9.6 ms, its merge (plan, merge) 24.7 / 33.8 s → 40
  / 117 ms, a merge at a shared tower 10.7 s → 79 ms; a line of 1 590
  objects — the commit 348 → 89 ms, the merge 785 → 43 ms. Phase 9's
  code and phase 11's on fresh databases of the same 147 lines: a move
  applied and broadcast p50 9.2 → 9.1 ms, a replica loaded, its rows and
  joining again after 20 moves (357 ms) the same, Update library pins
  3.2 s both.
- **Found while measuring** (there before phase 11): the first revision
  of a big model in a network whose version store has no rows yet is
  quadratic (the planner's statistics say the table is empty: each
  blob's check reads the rows written so far) — minutes instead of 24 s
  on the country as one model; said in the
  [database's page](postgresql.md#what-is-not-there-yet), a store reading
  many blob hashes at once to come.
- **Not yet**: opening a model reads each branch's base revision whole
  (the country with the bench's branches: 20 s instead of 1.8 s); the
  branch's in-memory line is still a whole line (its
  objects' JSON shared with main's): on a model of a whole country a
  branch costs the line's structure in memory (a branch the size of its
  working set comes with phase 12's offline working set); reverts and
  rollbacks read whole states; history, diffs and reviews are not served
  to a network's clients yet (the server's operations are there);
  OHL-Design has no window for branches over a working set yet.

> **Owner:** (answered 2026-11-20: as recommended — [the owner's entry](#2026-11-20-owner-country-server-phases-7-10-11-and-12--recommendations-approved); the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. Split trees only on a network's models, the desktop's project file
> keeping flat trees? → yes, as built (the format unchanged).
> 2. A model exported with split trees: readable by this build and later
> only; or flattened at export (new revision ids, the bundle round trip
> lost)? → keep them split, as built; say so in the export's report.
> 3. Tags, whole-line branches, rollbacks and reviews' merges still need
> the whole line? → yes for now; tags of a branch over a working set by
> its maker later if wanted.
> 4. A commit decided object by object (it may record other users'
> uncommitted work only if its user may edit it all)? → yes, as built.
> 5. Stale marks written when a branch's changes reach main, not on the
> branch? → yes, as built.
> 6. A merge into a protected main moving another route's tower waits for
> a review even by a line admin? → yes, as built (phase 8's rule).
> 7. A team named by users (and groups); a draft's requester named in it?
> → yes, as built.
> 8. Merges changing library files take the whole way (slower on a very
> big model)? → yes, until a library file's merge is made per entry on
> the trees.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 10)

**Scoped computations: each check's reach, the neighbours within it
pulled in from this and other lines, other lines' wires as targets,
structure loads with other lines' sections on shared towers, hidden
neighbours computed on the server, results saying what was pulled in and
marked stale when it changes** (ROADMAP O17 phase 10; the plan's answers
of 2026-11-16 — a hidden neighbour computed on the server and reported
without its details, shared towers checked under each line's cases, the
worst kept, fields pulling in lines within 500 m, plugin checks declaring
an optional reach; **owner, 2026-11-20: "You can go ahead with
recommendations and the changes to pull nearby lines"** — the engine
change and the optional plugin-interface step approved; built, in active
development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md#computations-on-the-working-set-and-what-touches-it),
[theory](../theory/scoped-checks.md),
[data model](data-model.md#the-servers-messages-protocol-3),
[plugins](plugins.md#a-checks-reach),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#checks-with-their-neighbours-phase-10-in-active-development),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-10-scoped-computations-2026-11-20)).

- **The engine** (`crates/ohl-scope`, no store, no rights): each check's
  reach (`reach_of`: clearances between wires — the wire rules' largest
  reach; the distance between conductors — what the working set holds;
  fields — lines within 500 m; structure loads — twins; a plugin's check —
  its manifest's `[reach]`, else the working set's whole line and every
  line within 2 km). A `Neighbourhood` gives what lies near (the server:
  its models and tile index; each part as `Session::drawing_part` takes
  it — never a whole line or the network copied).
- **Clearances between wires** (`ohl_scope::clearance`): the reach for
  every potential a section near can have (each phase of each system of
  the lines found near) and the highest structure top near plus 2 m,
  grown with the lines found until it holds; the candidates by a bound of
  each span's wire before it is solved; each solved with its own line's
  settings and wires; other lines' wires the targets of the rules to other
  lines (crossings among them), this line's beyond the working set those
  of the rules between its wires. One function runs the rules for the
  scoped run and the whole network's, the wires in one order; the scoped
  run looks for pairs as far as its reach plus the longest piece of a
  checked wire. **Engine change**: `ohl_clearance::CaseTargets::min_reach`
  (0: as before, every caller unchanged).
- **Decided here (conservative)**: a wire is at most 1.5 times the
  straight line between its ends (checked on every candidate solved;
  NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE said when it does not hold); a typed structure's
  points within 50 m of it and 150 m above it before its type is read; a
  bundle 2 m above its structure's top at most.
- **Fields** (`ohl_scope::fields`): the working set's line computed as one
  with its sections within the field distance, the other lines' fields
  **added by size** (their phase angles to this line's not known:
  conservative); the wires beyond the field distance left out — **NOT ON
  THE SAFE SIDE**, said in every result (the owner's 500 m, a setting).
- **Structure loads** (`ohl_scope::loads`): twins (the same type within
  0.5 m) are one tower; under each line's load cases (its own library's,
  else the shipped defaults) every line's sections there solved and the
  loads at its twin's points taken; a point's load from the line whose
  sections hang there, a point holding none its strings from the case's
  line, the body's wind once; the worst per point and component kept with
  its line and case. **Decided here (conservative)**: several lines'
  sections at one point added, each line's strings counted again; the
  other lines' sections solved in every case the case's line's twin takes
  (their own groups set aside). **Not on the safe side, said**: solved
  rigid — a line set to level 3 or 4 says so with the tower.
- **On the server** (`ohl_server`, `network_scoped.rs`; protocol 3,
  messages added: `check`, `check_result`, `check_stale`; nothing stored,
  network schema 5 unchanged): a check on the working set the connection
  follows or one given (refused when it reaches what its user may not
  see, as a pick); computed on the authority between two commands;
  **hidden neighbours computed too** — the numbers are the whole
  network's — and reported only as the rights allow: never named nor
  placed ("a hidden object of another line is within X m", "check result
  limited by an object you may not see" on the user's own span, without
  the point on it), counted in what was pulled in; a line the user sees
  nothing of never named; texts naming what is hidden replaced.
- **Results say what was pulled in** (lines, routes, objects the user may
  see, the hidden count, what was read) and are **watched**: the working
  set's objects, the neighbours read, the tiles the reach covers, the
  lines read; the first change touching any of them sends `check_stale`
  once (naming the change only as its user may see it); OHL-Design marks
  the working set's routes out of date in its replica — phase 8's marks,
  the same key (`Session::mark_stale`, `client::take_check_stale`).
- **A check run without its neighbours says so**: in OHL-Design on a
  working set's replica, the clearances between wires, the structure
  loads and a plugin's check whose reach is not 0 start with "NOT ALL
  CHECKED: … its neighbours not pulled in …" — never a pass because
  nothing is there. A neighbour the server could not read or solve: NOT
  ALL CHECKED.
- **The plugin step** (optional, additive; interface 0.3 unchanged): a
  manifest's `[reach]` — `default` and `check` (id → m), 0 to 10 000 m;
  none: the most conservative default; refused when not a distance
  (`ohl_plugins::CheckReach`, `Manifest::check_reach`). Plugins stay
  independent of the core: they declare a number, the core decides what
  it pulls in.
- **The safe side, proven** on the synthetic country (each route a line,
  towers of two routes twins; `ohl-scope`'s tests): clearances between
  wires on five working sets in still air and wind — the same pairs, the
  same distances to the bit, the same violations as with every line solved
  whole and every wire a target (three working sets: 22 239 pairs and wires, 2 499 violations, 1 022 other lines' objects used); the loads on nine
  shared towers — the same as the whole network's to the bit, and within
  1.7 % of each point's load of the country as one project (not the same
  model: a tower of two routes there takes one route's alignment); the
  field — what 500 m leaves out at most 0.00019 µT where the largest field is 4.2 µT. On the server: the same
  numbers for a user who may see only the route as for an admin; the
  property test of phase 7 now also asks checks each round — no message
  holds a hidden id or place.
- **Measured** (12 000 pylons, 147 lines;
  [performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-10-scoped-computations-2026-11-20)):
  a whole route of 145 structures — clearances 9.6 s (the first 18.9 s;
  2 220 objects read, of 15 lines with its own), the field 8.4 s, the loads on a shared
  tower 0.39 s; main's code against phase 10's on fresh databases: a move
  applied and broadcast p50 9.7–9.8 → 9.2–9.8 ms, joining again after 20
  moves 359 → 354 ms, a replica loaded 0.072 / 0.119 → 0.076 / 0.108 s
  (a third / the whole route), the start 2.8–2.9 → 2.6–2.7 s.
- **Not yet**: OHL-Design's windows asking the network for these checks
  (the protocol and the server are there; the windows still run on the
  file and say what they did not pull in); the checks computed on a
  worker of their own (they run on the authority between two commands
  — a long check holds the edits); clearances to the ground and to points
  on the network (no terrain or point cloud served); rules across weather
  cases on the network; the field's left-out part bounded and added;
  shared towers' flexible solve (level 3/4); plugin checks run on the
  server (they run in OHL-Design).

> **Owner:** (answered 2026-11-20: as recommended — [the owner's entry](#2026-11-20-owner-country-server-phases-7-10-11-and-12--recommendations-approved); the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. Checks computed on the authority between commands (a long check
> holds the edits) → a worker thread of their own next, the parts taken
> on the authority.
> 2. The field's wires beyond 500 m left out, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE →
> keep, and add a bound of what is left out (the lines' currents by
> tile) later.
> 3. A wire at most 1.5 times its ends' distance (the candidates' bound,
> checked on what is solved) → yes.
> 4. Shared towers: several lines' sections at one point added, strings
> counted again; other lines' sections in every case the twin takes → yes.
> 5. A plugin without `[reach]`: the whole line and every line within
> 2 km → yes.
> 6. A result stale when anything changes within its reach's tiles (more
> often than strictly needed) → yes.
> 7. Hidden neighbours: the distance to them said ("within X m") →
> yes, as the plan's answer.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 9)

**Country libraries: each library kind kept once for the network, locks
and maintainers, requests with pending drafts, releases, pins, Update
library pins, withdrawn entries, a use index read through the rights,
the import's mapping** (ROADMAP O17 phase 9; the plan's answer "library
requests as pending drafts", 2026-11-16; built, in active development,
not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md#country-libraries),
[data model](data-model.md#server-database-postgresql),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#country-libraries-phase-9-in-active-development),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-9-country-libraries-2026-11-20)).

- **A line holds the files of the release it is pinned to as its own
  library files** (`library` objects, as a project today). The engine,
  the solves, the packager and the desktop read them unchanged; the
  network keeps the libraries (`lib_file`: each file's text as it is
  now, its *head*; `lib_release`, `lib_release_file`: releases, their
  texts as the version store keeps blobs — compressed, each text once
  for the network, shared with the revisions holding the same text);
  `line.library_pins` names the release of each kind. **Decided here
  (simple, safe)**: copies per line rather than a resolution of every
  library read through the network — the engine and the `.ohl` format
  stay as they are, and an export stands alone. A line's copy costs its
  files' size (the shipped wire file 3 kB; 147 lines: well under 1 MB).
- **An entry** (`ohl_session::country`): a file with a top-level `id` is
  one entry; else each table of a list of tables named by `id`, `name` or
  `label` (`[[cable]]`, `[[case]]`, `[[type]]`); else the file is one
  entry named by its file name. Its **version** is the SHA-256 of its
  values written canonically (a comment or the order of keys makes no
  new version). The kinds objects name by id — wires, structure types,
  insulator assemblies, bodies' types — keep an entry's id once across
  the kind's files (refused otherwise); the others (weather cases, rules,
  …) are picked by file.
- **Locks and maintainers**: a kind (or one file) locked (`lib_kind`,
  `lib_file.locked`) changes only by requests granted and releases; a
  line's own file of a locked kind is refused (the server decides every
  library file a command changes: put, delete, a batch, a merge).
  Maintainers are assignments (*review* and *lock* on the kind: the
  shipped library maintainer role on a library kind, network admins).
  **Decided here (conservative)**: locking needs *lock* on the kind,
  **unlocking a network admin** (a maintainer cannot open a locked kind
  to pass the review); granting, refusing, releasing and withdrawing need
  *review* and *lock*; a network admin may change a locked file directly
  only with `emergency`, in the audit. The network's library is a new
  target of the rights' one function (`Target::CountryLibrary`), covered
  only by scopes naming no line, route, region or object: a line's
  designer does not see or change the network's library, only their
  line's copy.
- **Requests** (`lib_request`): the entry asked for as a file of its own
  (its *draft*, the entry alone with the file's header), for a line and
  the requester's own branch (made by them, never main); draft →
  requested → granted, refused or withdrawn. Asking needs *request* on
  the line's library (a designer of the line) and seeing the line, or on
  the network's library; asking for a change of an entry the network
  has needs *edit* on it (a maintainer). **A grant needs a maintainer who
  is not the requester** (four eyes; the ADR's "another maintainer
  approves"), and lays the entry into the head (a change replaces it) for
  the next release. **Who sees a request**: its requester (drafts too)
  and the maintainers of its entry (not a draft); a maintainer who may
  not see the line it is for sees it without its line, branch, routes or
  reason.
- **A pending draft** is a library file named `request-N.ext` in the
  requester's branch, holding the request's text exactly: put or changed
  only by its requester, in the request's branch, while it is a draft,
  asked or granted. **It blocks the branch**: submitting it for review,
  merging it (or bringing it) into main are refused while it holds a
  draft not granted; a draft reaching main is refused unless granted.
  **"Replaced"** (the roadmap's word) **is the draft taken out of the
  branch** (another entry used); taking a draft out is always allowed. A
  granted draft may be merged into main (the entry is the network's then);
  Update library pins removes it once a release holds its entry.
- **Releases**: a maintainer freezes the kind's head under a tag; refused
  when nothing changed since the last; each entry version noted with the
  release it first came in (`lib_entry`); granted requests marked with
  their release. **A release changes no line** (the task's rule): it says
  how many lines in design follow the latest and how many built lines
  stay pinned.
- **Pins and Update library pins**: built lines (`line.built`, set by
  whoever holds *lock* on the whole line) are pinned; lines in design
  **follow the latest** — **decided here**: following means they are the
  lines `--following` moves and the status shows behind, never that a
  release moves them by itself (the task: "a line never changes silently
  when a library releases; only Update library pins moves a pin"). Update
  library pins plans each kind (the release's files put; a line's file
  not in the release removed when the release holds every entry of it
  the line uses, kept when it is wholly the line's own; files of the
  kinds a line picks by name kept; refused for a kind when the line would
  lose an entry it uses, or a file mixes such an entry with the
  release's) and carries it out as **one log entry** (kind
  `library_pins`) with the pins moved in the same unit of work; **the
  routes using an entry whose version changed are marked out of date**
  (phase 8's stale marks and notices, "library cables → R3: … changed");
  a kind picked by file marks every route. It needs edit (create,
  delete) of each file changed on the line, and **on a built line review
  of the whole line** (decided here: the ADR's "through a review when
  protected" as the reviewer's right; a review flow of its own later).
  **Not undone by Undo** (decided here: the pin is the network's, so
  files and pin never disagree): the pins are updated again to the
  release before. On the server a client asks `UpdateLibraryPins`; the
  server plans it and carries out `LibraryPins` (what the replicas
  replay); a client's `LibraryPins` is refused. On the command line it
  needs the network's writer (no server running).
- **Withdrawn entries** (`lib_withdrawn`): withdrawn by a maintainer,
  kept in the head and in later releases — **a line using one keeps
  working and is shown it** (status, the export's
  `network.library_withdrawn`); **no object may start using one** (the
  server refuses a section, jumper, structure or spacer whose new uses
  hold a withdrawn entry it did not use before; the use index says what
  it used). **Decided here**: results using a withdrawn entry are not
  marked out of date by the withdrawal itself (that changes a model: it
  waits for the server's library notices in the app); the status shows
  it.
- **The use index** (`lib_use`): what each element of a model's main
  branch uses (by id) and the entries of the files of the kinds picked by
  file, written by the import, kept by every command of the server in its
  unit of work, made again when a server starts on a model without one
  (and `ohl network library reindex`); branches other than main are not
  indexed (with phase 11). **Read through the rights' one function**: an
  entry the viewer may not see is "not found" in the same words as one
  that is not there; a use on an object (or a line's file) the viewer may
  not see is left out without a word, no count; of an object's routes
  only those the viewer sees as routes are named.
- **The import's mapping**: each entry of the project's library files the
  same as the network's, **added** to the network's file of the same name
  (a kind not locked: the importer is a network admin), or **asked for**
  (a locked kind; an entry that differs, as a change for a maintainer —
  never replaced silently); in the report. **Decided here**: the model
  keeps its own files and no pin until Update library pins (the import
  keeps the current state, owner 2026-11-16).
- **The export** (decided, as the task asked): the pinned entries must be
  in the file, and are — they are the line's own library files; nothing
  else of the network's library is copied. Its `ols_meta` gains
  `network.library_withdrawn` beside `network.library_pins` (now
  filled). The desktop format is unchanged.
- **Network schema 5**: `lib_kind`; `lib_file` + `text`, `hash`,
  `by_user`, `time` (the draft's `kind_locked` dropped: the kind's lock is
  `lib_kind`'s); `lib_release.n`; `lib_release_file`; `lib_entry`'s
  withdrawn columns moved to `lib_withdrawn`; `lib_use` made again (line,
  object, kind, file, entry; places joined from `object` and `spatial`);
  `lib_request` + `text`, `line_id`, `branch`, `released`; `net_meta`
  `library_rev`. The draft tables were empty: a database of schema 4 is
  brought forward when a program connects (tested).
- **Library changes** (`ohl_store_pg::library::LibraryCommand`, `ohl
  network library …`): each one transaction serialised by an advisory
  lock, decided by the rights read in it, with its audit row (a file's
  text by its hash) and `library_rev` moved on; refusals in the audit
  (a file's text by its size). No writer's lock needed; a running server
  reads the locks, requests and withdrawn entries again before its next
  job.
- **Tests**: entries, versions, uses, drafts' names, an entry laid into a
  file and taken alone; the network's library in the rights' one function
  (a line's designer or a kind on a line not covering it, an entry's
  grant only that entry, an entry's deny its file and kind too, any
  order); Update library pins in the session on both stores' code (one
  entry, stale marks, not undone); on PostgreSQL the whole flow with the
  security cases — **a non-maintainer (a network-wide designer, a line's
  designer, a maintainer without emergency) cannot change a locked
  kind**; **requests and drafts seen only by whoever should** (the
  requester; the maintainers, a draft never, without the line they may
  not see); **the use index leaks no hidden entry nor the lines using
  it** (a viewer of the kind without lines sees no use; a viewer of a
  route only its uses and that route's name; a viewer of a line's
  structures no section; a denied entry not found, in the words of one
  that is not there; neither in the files' list nor the status); schema
  4 brought to 5; on the server: Update library pins planned and refused
  as a client's carried-out form, a locked kind refused (put and batch),
  a draft only in its requester's branch, blocking review and merge until
  granted, then merged, a withdrawn entry kept by who uses it and never
  newly used, the use index kept with each command, a built line moved
  only by who reviews it, the libraries read again while the server
  runs.
- **Measured** on the 12 000-pylon synthetic country's 147 lines
  ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-9-country-libraries-2026-11-20)):
  Update library pins of every line 3.3 s (per line p50 21 ms, planned
  in 2.4 ms); a release 2–7 ms; the use index made again 3.7 s (93 977
  rows); the uses of the wire every span uses 0.31 s for a network admin,
  39 ms for a viewer of one route; moves (p50 9.1–9.7 ms against
  9.1–9.8 ms with phase 7's code) and working sets as before; a command's
  rights a few microseconds more.
- **Not yet**: the OHL-Server admin app's Libraries page (stage D, its
  plan waiting); Update library pins in OHL-Design (the server's
  operation is there); notices to a line's users when a release makes it
  behind (the status shows it); the impact run's engineering figures
  before a pin moves (the plan lists the entries and routes); a file's
  entries filtered per entry in what is sent of a line's library files
  (phase 7 sends a line's file whole to whoever sees it; the network's
  library is filtered per entry); branches' use index (phase 11).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-20; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. A release changes no line; lines in design follow the latest by
> `update-pins --following` (one command for all) and are shown behind:
> or should a release move every line in design by itself (logged, stale
> marks)? → as built, explicit; a setting later if wanted.
> 2. Unlocking a kind by network admins only (maintainers may lock)? →
> yes, as built.
> 3. A request granted only by a maintainer other than its requester? →
> yes, as built.
> 4. A pending draft "replaced" means taken out of the branch (another
> entry used); a request withdrawn still blocks while its draft is in the
> branch? → yes, as built.
> 5. A built line's pins moved by whoever may review the whole line, not
> through a review of its own? → yes for now; a library review flow with
> OHL-Server stage D.
> 6. Update library pins not undone by Undo (moved back by updating to
> the release before)? → yes, as built.
> 7. A withdrawn entry stays in later releases (lines keep working) and
> no object may start using it; results using it not marked out of date
> by the withdrawal itself? → keep it in releases, yes; mark the using
> routes "not on the safe side" when the app shows library notices
> (with OHL-Server stage D).
> 8. The import adds new entries of a kind not locked to the network's
> library and asks for the rest; the model keeps its own files until
> Update library pins? → yes, as built.
> 9. A draft must be in the requester's own branch (made by them)? → yes;
> a team's branch with phase 11.
> 10. A line's library file is sent whole to whoever may see it (an
> entry's deny is enforced on the network's library, not inside a line's
> copy)? → filter a line's file per entry with OHL-Server stage D; until
> then deny the file.

## 2026-11-20 (country server, phase 7)

**Rights and roles on a network: one function deciding for the commands
and for everything the server sends; assignments by scope, denies by
network admins, the audit, "see as user"** (ROADMAP O17 phase 7; the
owner's "rights and roles applied to almost every element and library",
2026-11-18; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md#rights-and-roles-on-almost-every-element-and-library),
[data model](data-model.md#server-database-postgresql),
[user guide](../user-guide/server.md#a-networks-server-in-active-development),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-7-rights-and-roles-2026-11-20)).

- **The one function** (`ohl_session::rights`, no database in it):
  `UserRights::allows(permission, target)`. A role is a set of the nine
  permissions (see, edit, create, delete, review, export, lock, request,
  manage rights); the six shipped roles as in the ADR (the schema's rows
  tested against the session's list). An assignment gives a user or a
  group a role on a **scope**, or — network admins only — denies a role's
  permissions there (every permission when no role is named). A scope is
  a conjunction of constraints (none: the network): a line, a route or
  the part of a route between two of its structures (snapped out to
  whole tension sections, as a working set), a region (a polygon), an
  object kind, an object, a library kind, file or entry; "the costs of
  line B" is a line and a library kind. **Default deny**; the union of a
  user's own and their groups' grants covering the target; edit, create,
  delete, review and export need see on the same target; **a deny
  covering the target wins whatever the order** (tested: assignments
  reversed, a deny added never allows more, a grant added never less); a
  disabled user has no rights. A **target** is the network itself (its
  users, groups, roles, assignments, audit), a line as a whole, an object
  of a line (its plan bounds and routes), or a library file or entry of
  a line.
- **Decided here (conservative)**: a region **grants** what lies wholly
  inside it and **denies** what it touches (an object's plan bounds); a
  target without a place (the line's settings, a library file, a report)
  is in no region or route, but a grant on a route, a region or an object
  lets its user **see** (only see) the settings and library files of the
  lines it lies on — a section is solved with them; **the line as a
  whole** (merges, rollbacks, branches, commits, tags, reviews' merges,
  following a model whole, an export) is granted only by a scope of the
  whole line or the network, and denied by any deny that may touch the
  line; a deny's region may touch every line; a grant naming a role
  removed gives nothing, a deny naming one denies everything.
- **What is seen is seen as drawn**: an object with what it refers to — a
  section with every structure it hangs on, an alignment with its route
  and every point of it, an alignment point with the structure it is
  tied to (its place is the structure's), a jumper or a spacer with its
  sections and structures. Found by the property test: an alignment
  point on a visible route tied to a hidden structure gave the structure's
  place away in the route's bounds.
- **The edit side**: every server operation has a rule (an exhaustive
  match: a new operation cannot be added without one): its objects only
  (commands, undo, redo), these permissions on the line whole (rollbacks,
  merges, bringing in, project lines, commits, branches, tags, reviews:
  edit, create and delete or edit; protecting a branch: lock; deciding a
  review: review), edit of the settings, create, edit or delete of a
  library file; users, roles and the project's edit grants are refused on
  a network (they are the network's). After the operation ran, in the
  **same unit of work** (`ohl_server::execute_checked`, the session's
  `atomically`: the store's savepoint and the line in memory put back
  when refused), every object it changed is decided: **create** for a new
  one (as it is), **delete** for one gone (as it was), **edit** for one
  changed (as it was and as it is: nothing moved out of, or into, what
  one may edit). The places "as it was" are the server's: each model's
  objects' bounds and routes as of its last command (`Places`). The
  session's own role rules take their roles from the rights
  (`RoleSource`, `model_role`: admin with edit, create, delete and manage
  rights on the whole line; designer with a grant to edit something of
  it; viewer otherwise). The project's own edit grants (imported with
  it) are still checked by the session too: both apply.
- **Decided here (conservative)**: on a project line other than main,
  an object's place is main's (a new object there: its own); branches,
  commits and tags need edit on the whole line (a designer of a route
  works on main until branches over working sets, phase 11); a grant on
  a part of a route covers what the part holds (resolved again after
  each change of its model) — **making new objects needs a whole route,
  a region or the line** (a question below).
- **The see side** (the outgoing filter, the same function): the
  network's lines and routes (a line listed when its user may see
  something of it, a route when they may see it; bounds and counts of
  what they see); **tile packages** kept per **rights class** — the exact
  set of a tile's objects its client may not see (none for those who see
  everything: one package shared as before; never a hash, so two classes
  cannot be confused) —, a class's package filtered from the whole one
  (structures, wires, alignments, the names of the routes still drawn,
  notes naming what is hidden); **changes**: a client that may not see
  every object a change touched (as it is now; as it was for what went),
  its routes, its library file or settings, or, for a change at large or
  on a branch, the whole line, gets "read these tiles again" for its own
  tiles (through the filter) and nothing more; **catch-ups**: a change as
  it is only to a client seeing its whole line (its operation may name,
  or have moved, what the client may not see then or now), the others'
  tiles read again; **working sets**: refused when they reach anything
  their user may not see (the refusal names nothing), rows of what came
  in later and may not be seen left out (logged), deletes only of what
  was sent, the users of their structures (`part_users`) filtered; a
  route's structures and alignments by station: those seen; **error
  messages** naming an object the user may not see become one fixed
  refusal, "it touches objects you have no access to"; the users' list
  without their presence (a selection names objects, a camera a place)
  and no soft locks for users who do not see everything.
- **Who joins**: only the network's users (`net_user`, enabled), each
  with their personal invitation — the general one admits nobody, and
  `ohl network serve --newcomers` is refused on a network (default deny,
  owner 2026-11-19: "only users an admin added may join a network").
- **Rights changes** (`ohl_store_pg::rights::RightsCommand`, the command
  line `ohl network rights …`): users, groups, members and roles by
  network admins only (a membership or a role reaches every scope its
  assignments name); an assignment by whoever **manages rights on a scope
  holding it** and **holds every permission of the role there** (no one
  gives more than they hold); a deny by network admins only; the shipped
  roles fixed; a role given cannot be removed; the last network admin
  cannot be taken away or disabled; the first one by `bootstrap`, only
  while there is none. A route or object scope gets its line (ids are
  unique in the network); what it names must exist. Each change is one
  transaction serialised by an advisory lock, with its audit row (what
  it was and is) and the rights' revision moved on. **Decided here**:
  rights changes need no writer's lock (an admin changes them while the
  server runs); the server looks at the revision before each job and
  with each heartbeat, reads the rights again when it moved, and **lets
  go every client whose rights changed** (it holds what it may no longer
  see) — it joins again, filtered anew. Group membership changed while a
  client is connected: tested (let go; the next request on the old
  connection refused; less seen after).
- **"See as user"**: whoever manages rights somewhere may join seeing as
  another user (`see_as` in the join; `ohl network rights see-as` and
  `explain` on the command line): what both may see, nothing changed, in
  the audit.
- **The audit** (append only, as before): every rights change with what
  it was and is; refusals — joins, commands, working sets, rights
  changes, see-as, exports, imports, the audit asked by a non-admin —
  with what was asked in full (the audit is the network admins').
- **Imports and exports**: importing needs a network admin (any user
  while the network has none: it is being set up); exporting a model
  needs export on its whole line (a model exported is every row of it;
  a part of one is the offline working set, phase 12).
- **Network schema 4**: `assignment` gains the library kind, file and
  entry and the region's points as given (JSON as text; `area` the same
  polygon for PostGIS); `stream` gains the objects each change touched
  (`kind/id`) and whether it touched its line at large; `net_meta`
  `rights_rev`; an index of members. A database of schema 3 is brought
  forward when a program connects (tested).
- **Tests**: the function's property over random roles, assignments and
  targets (300 rounds); the store's rights changes on PostgreSQL (who may
  do what, the audit, the revision, a region read back exactly, schema 3
  brought to 4); the server: who joins, commands decided and put back,
  tiles, changes, catch-ups, working sets, route details and refusals
  filtered; grants and denies in any order, a group's member taken out
  and a user disabled while connected; see as user; and **the property
  that no message holds a hidden id or place**: six rounds of random
  assignments (a line, a route, a part of one, a region, a kind on a
  line, with a deny now and then), random moves by another user and the
  user's own, tiles, a catch-up, a route's detail and a pick — every
  string, word and number of every message to the user checked against
  what the user may not see before and after (a structure standing where
  a visible twin of another line stands excepted: its place is the
  visible one's).
- **Measured** on the 12 000-pylon synthetic country with 204 users and
  1 297 assignments ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-7-rights-and-roles-2026-11-20)):
  a command's rights decided p50 15–16 µs, p95 23 µs; who may not see a
  change (20 viewers) p95 under 0.14 ms; a tile's rights class p50
  28–39 µs; a package filtered p50 0.18 ms, p95 0.68 ms (then kept); a
  move applied and broadcast p95 9.8 ms; a view of 12 tiles for a
  region's viewer 83 ms (a network admin's 90 ms); the start 2.8 s
  (phase 5: 2.5 s).
- **Not yet**: the OHL-Server admin app (its plan waits for the owner);
  rights in the desktop's own server of a project file (unchanged: its
  three roles and edit grants); library locks, requests and releases
  (phase 9: the permissions lock and request exist, the scopes too);
  history, diffs and reviews served to a network's clients (not served
  yet; the stream keeps each change's objects for them); OIDC (phase 13).

> **Owner:** (answered 2026-11-20: as recommended — [the owner's entry](#2026-11-20-owner-country-server-phases-7-10-11-and-12--recommendations-approved); the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. A designer of a part of a route may not make new objects there
> (only a whole route, a region or the line allows it): allow them inside
> the part as it is after the command? → yes, with branches over working
> sets (phase 11); until then a whole route.
> 2. Branches, commits and tags need edit on the whole line: keep until
> branches over working sets? → yes.
> 3. Users, groups and memberships by network admins only, line admins
> assigning within their lines: or line admins managing groups too? →
> network admins only, as built.
> 4. An export needs export on the whole line (no export of only what one
> sees)? → yes; a part goes as an offline working set (phase 12).
> 5. A client let go whenever its rights change (even when it gains
> some), joining again: fine, or re-filter in place? → let go, as built.
> 6. The users' presence and the soft locks hidden from users who do not
> see everything: or filtered object by object? → hidden now; filtered
> with OHL-Server's stage B.
> 7. A project's edit grants imported with it stay checked beside the
> assignments: or turned into assignments at import? → turned into
> assignments at import (a later step), both checked until then.
> 8. Who may see as another user: whoever manages rights somewhere,
> within what both may see? → yes (the OHL-Server plan's question 3
> answered the same way).

## 2026-11-20 (joint layout: the bent end's turn, the end running back to its bend L3b)

**O44, L3b** (built 2026-11-20, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-bent-ends-turn-and-the-end-running-back-to-its-bend-l3b),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md), [joint details](joint-details.md);
no format change):

- **The flat end's turn chosen for the bent end — the other leg kept, a
  switch** (`bend_facing`, on): after step 2b's half turns, an equal-leg
  angle the half turn did not help, left at an end at most 20° off with its
  outstanding leg towards the flange, is tried with its other leg bolted —
  the quarter turn that faces that end's leg away from the flange (from the
  geometry) — in one more planning pass, kept as the half turns are (more
  of its ends planned laid out, its joints no fewer). The order of the ends
  (L1 a: bottom up, then out) unchanged. **Left out**: choosing the half
  turn (or the other leg) from the geometry alone wherever it predicts more
  ends flat or bent (measured: fewer ends laid out — the bent end then
  mostly fails the axis limit, the flat end needs the flange's other face).
- **An end running back towards its bend — kept, a switch** (`bend_back`,
  on): bent away from the flange, its steel kept clear of the bend only
  over the flange (to half the gap past its toe), not to half its length;
  beyond, its steel may pass the plane of the flat plate's face (*an
  assumption of the tool*, the clash check after writing checks it). Its
  bolts their edge distance from the bend, its axis within one plate
  thickness — L3's limits unchanged. The flap on the joint's side of the
  bend line is not built (the flat plate would no longer cover the work
  point).
- **The holding bolts over a hole after writing** (131 ends left on the
  real towers): looked into, not fixed — the hole is the end of the very
  member the plate is held to, not laid out at that joint, drawn after
  writing where the plan did not see it (its `onto` named only in the
  planning copy, or its end off its flange); not a simple fix (a question
  to the owner).
- Unchanged: the bend check C12, the plugins, the 2° / 5° tolerances, the
  20° bound and the edge-distance rule (L3's questions 4–6 open), C10 (the
  tilted inner-face ends not laid out).

Measured on the 78 private real towers (the theory page): joints laid out
whole 49.71 % → 49.78 %, ends 64.66 % → 64.85 % ((1) +39 joints whole and
+199 ends alone, (2) +8 and +132), joints not fitting as given 28 → 28, the
L3 bends 4 085 → 4 398 (84 % pass the strict check under one vertical case),
a run again identical 78 of 78, the time per tower 3–6 % more. The owner's
questions are in the roadmap (O44 L3b).

**O44 J7a with the owner's decisions of 2026-11-19** ("a change of
section is a splice; the same section is one part unless marked; a

bolted through the outer splice cover: yes, after the splice places";

  through a joint — a `[[splice]]` with covers outer and inner on each leg
  bolted, as thick as the thicker piece's leg (the program's starting

  two pieces of one section with bolts — one part (J9's proposal, flagged
  `splice_bolts`, listed with the leg splices). Lay out joints' preview:

## 2026-11-19 (joint layout: pieces in line proposed one part, the mutual-host guard)

**O44 J9 with the owner's decisions D15 and D16** (below; built the same
day, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#pieces-in-line-one-part-confirmed-j9),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md),
[joint details](joint-details.md)):

- **Pieces in line proposed one part (D15).** Pieces of one section in
  line through a joint (the core's 1°), the same reference and
  orientation, rolls within 5°, nothing given there of how they are
  joined: proposed `continuous` in Lay out joints' preview; *Confirm* per
  joint or *Confirm all*, one undo step each. Never a silent default:
  until confirmed each piece ends at the joint, in the checks and the

  D16): bolted directly only with every bolt on that member's steel past
  its cut by the end distance, else onto a plate, else a hand detail; of
  two pieces in line, the one on the end's side is named. *Conservative*
  (pieces not confirmed taken to end there).

  directly onto a member as written (laid out, or left as it was — then
  without the `onto` its planning named) whose bolts would misfit by the
  joint checks' rule is left too and the joint planned again.

  No format change.
