## 2026-11-19 (owner: 22 recommendations approved)

**The owner's answers of 2026-11-19 to the open questions of O45, O19
stage 4.5, O44 J2b and O17 phase 6** (owner: "Okay go with
recommendations"; the numbers are this entry's own). Five needed code and
were built the same day, in active development, not approved yet (A1,
B8, C12, D14, E22); the rest are recorded in the roadmap under their items.

**Estimated eccentricities** (O45; [theory](../theory/estimated-eccentricities.md)):

- **A1, built: an offset of unknown sign only in its member's own check.**
  An end offset whose sign is not known — an upper bound, a plate's offset
  out of its face — is never in the solve: the member's own check takes
  its moment N·e whole and sign-free (about each local axis the sizes of
  its parts' moments added, uniform along it), at frame joints as where
  only bars meet. A change of the core's finite-element crate, approved by
  the owner: `Member::free_offsets` ([data model](data-model.md),
  [theory](../theory/structures-fe.md#eccentric-member-ends-rigid-end-offsets)).
  *Conservative*: the member holds the whole moment whatever the sign; the
  joint's other members are relieved of nothing (statically admissible).
  Two solves (without, with) instead of three; the mixed-sign NOT ON THE
  SAFE SIDE note is gone ([safe side](safe-side.md)). No plugin interface
  changed (the moments reach the plugins in the members' end forces, as
  before). Measured on the 78 private real towers, one vertical case:
  towers solving with the option 64 → 72 of 73 (the one left fails
  without the option too), members whose usage rises 86 % → 27 %, the
  towers' largest usage with it median 0.84 → 0.58, the direct solves
  with the estimates a third of the time.
- A2: the upper bound stays the 30 mm shift limit plus the plate's
  offset, until J5.
- A3: towers that fail to solve with the option on are accepted until A1
  — reported as failed (since A1 none but one that fails without it).
- A4: the estimates stay in OHL-Structure only; the core's line
  calculation does not read them.
- A5: the option on by default only after A1, J3 and the bent plate (all
  built now), measured again with wind cases (to do).

**Bolts** (O19 stage 4.5; [joint groups](../theory/joint-groups.md)):

- B6: a gusset plate's prying lever stays measured to the farthest bolt.
- B7: no "web" credit for members bolted across a plate, unless a source
  is cited.
- **B8, done in the private data**: bolt grade 8.8 (f_ub 800, f_yb 640
  N/mm², SIA 263:2013 3.4.2 Table 2, the bolt grade command's values) in
  the current line's bolt library — its own `grade`, `ultimate` and
  `yield` fields — with a step in the private rebuild script; nothing in
  the repository.
- B9: the NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE flag for a moment about the line of a
  plate's holding bolts stays.

**The bent plate** (O44 J2b; [joint layout](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-bend-in-bending-2026-11-19)):

- C10: no bent plate for tilted ends; J5 handles them.
- C11: the inside bend radius stays two plate thicknesses (no shop value
  given).
- **C12, built: a bending check at the bend in both code plugins** —
  the additive plugin interface `joint-check-bends` (interface 0.3
  unchanged; [plugins](plugins.md)). OpenOHL works out what acts on the
  section along the bend line (the force across it, the shear along it,
  the moment about it and in the plate's plane — each member's force
  across the bend at its line's distance out of the flat, by size, plus
  the force across the bend held at the farthest bolt of the flat on the
  leg, taken at the bend: on the safe side); ASCE 10-97 checks it by Eq.
  3.13-1 with the gross elastic section (3.10.1, 3.14.1–3.14.3) and the
  shear by von Mises' criterion (no rule in the standard: on the safe
  side), SIA 263 by 4.3.5.4 formula (6) with elastic stresses (5.2.1,
  5.2.6: no plastic resistance relied on in a cold-bent zone) and the
  radius against 5.7.1.2 Table 14 (where a weld is on the bent plate).
  A plugin without the export: not checked, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE, as
  before. Not on the safe side, said: a frame member's end moments and
  shear at its bolts are not added at the bend.
- C13: on 45–55 mm legs without room for the holding bolts the hand
  detail stays until J8.

**"Does not fit"** (O19 stage 4.5, O44):

- **D14, built: "does not fit as assumed — not detailed".** A joint check
  that does not fit only where the placements were assumed — not given by
  the user, not laid out by the joint layout (no `onto`, gauges, pitch,
  end distance or `cut` given at the end or in the member's design data) —
  reads "DOES NOT FIT as assumed — not detailed": still failing, never a
  usage or a pass, counted apart in the run's summary, the report's joints
  table (its own row word and count) and the 3D view (orange; as given:
  red) ([theory](../theory/joint-groups.md#a-joint-that-does-not-fit)).
  Measured on the 78 private real towers (one case): as imported 23 128
  of 33 544 joints do not fit, 22 993 of them only as assumed, 135 as
  given; after Orient angles and Lay out joints 17 821 of 55 970, 11 057
  as assumed — not detailed, 6 764 as given (mostly the layout's own:
  pieces in line it cuts back, mutual hosts — D15, D16).
- D15: J9 proposes "continuous" for same-section pieces in line through a
  joint; the user confirms, with a "confirm all" button — never a silent
  default.
- D16: the mutual-host guard (two ends bolting onto each other) is built
  together with J9, not before.

**Country server phase 6** (O17; [phase 6](#2026-11-19-country-server-phase-6)):

- E17: other sections on a working set's structures are read-only context.
- E18: one line per working set until phase 11.
- E19: the 64-bit FNV hash for joining again, for now.
- E20: protocol 3.
- E21: 5 × 5 context tiles and a 64 MB cache, with a setting later.
- **E22, built: a replica's import entry with an empty command**, as the
  network's import writes it (`ohl_session::EMPTY_COMMAND`): each object
  stored once, in its row; old replicas read as before; no table, column
  or key added ([data model](data-model.md#a-working-sets-replica-phase-6-2026-11-19)).
  On the synthetic country's first line: the whole route's replica
  3.48 → 1.98 MB, a third of it 1.79 → 1.03 MB
  ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-6-working-sets-and-context-2026-11-19)).

## 2026-11-19 (joint layout: one roll per member, laid out once per kind)

**O44 J3 and J4** (owner 2026-11-19, step 5 of the order; built the same
day, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#one-roll-for-the-whole-member-j3),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md)):

- **The owner's order of the classes** (owner 2026-11-19: "You can do 90
  degrees turn or more if necessary also start with aligning the main
  legs then diagonals and finally secondary braces with redundant members
  being last"): the layout turns the members class by class — the legs
  and chords are never turned to suit what bolts onto them (their roll is
  the tower's shape, Orient angles), then the diagonals, then the
  secondary bracing (horizontals, plan and hip members; a member of no
  class with them, said), the redundants last — each class's turns found
  with the classes before already turned. Any turn where it is needed,
  the smallest that lays the member's ends flat; a roll given by hand
  kept unless *Replace values given by hand*. The same order ranks the
  ends of a plane and the planes in J1's search (before: by class leg,
  bracing, redundant, then the bigger member — the diagonals and the
  horizontals, both `bracing`, by size): the owner's order used, both
  measured (below).
- **One roll for the whole member** (J3): the turn chosen from both ends'
  needs together; an equal-leg angle's leg bolted may change between its
  ends (a quarter turn more lays its other leg flat — as a member running
  from a horizontal flange to an upright one is built; the two legs are
  alike for its check); an unequal angle's never. Never forced: where no
  roll serves both ends, not turned and said. **Tried and left out**: a
  turn leaving every end within the whole 5° flatness allowed (the ends'
  turns up to 10° apart instead of 5°) laid out slightly fewer ends.
- **Orient angles and the layout agree**: Orient angles keeps a plan or
  face member's roll the layout chose for both its ends; the layout starts
  from Orient angles' roll. The estimated eccentricities (O45) plan with
  the same choice.
- **Laid out once per kind** (J4): joints alike by the tower's symmetry
  (the eight rigid maps keeping the vertical) or a repeated panel —
  matched geometrically with the tool's tolerance (a tenth of a degree, 2
  mm) on the members, sections, rolls, classes and what the planner reads
  (bolts, what they bolt onto) — are planned once, the plan mapped onto
  the others, each checked for clashes in its own place and planned on
  its own where it fails there. No format change.
- **Apply this joint's detail to similar joints** (J4): a command in Joint
  details (a tool window: a preview of the joints it changes, one undo
  step) copies a joint's connections and plates — laid out or detailed by
  hand — mirrored or turned onto the joints of its kind, the layout's
  record following; a copy that would run into more than the source in its
  place is left, said; a splice is not copied.
- **The quantities panel's test** (O46): it waits for the panel's and the
  view's background threads before stepping (they ask for a frame when
  done, which under load ran a step past its frames: "max_steps
  exceeded"); what it checks unchanged.

## 2026-11-19 (joint layout: the bent plate)

**O44 J2b, the bent plate** (the owner's example joint of a gusset plate
folded to follow two planes; approved the same day "before J3"; built
the same day, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#a-bent-plate-round-the-other-leg-j2b),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md)):

- **What it takes**: an end on a flange's inner face that leaves the joint
  over the heel, through the angle's other leg — before, "runs towards the
  angle's other leg", a hand detail. One flat where the end lies (its own
  plane, beyond the other leg), folded along the member's line round the
  heel onto the other leg's outer face, bolted there by two provisional
  bolts (`[plate.leg_bolts]`, so that the flat is bolted to the flange as
  asked); the ends of one plane share the flat. The end stays where it
  lay (no farther out than directly on the flange), only pulled back.
- **The order**: the half turn onto the outer face first (checked with
  the bent plates off), then the bent plate, then a hand detail. Step 4's
  welded plate keeps the ends no roll lays flat: a bent version of it is
  not built (with the same offset limit it would lay out about the same
  ends) — a question to the owner.
- **The file**: `[plate.bend]` on the second flat (`to`, `angle`,
  `inner_radius`, `line`), **structure file version 22** written only
  when a plate is bent (21: the bolt grade's of the same day); the two
  flats one part, never welded.
- **Assumptions, said**: the inside bend radius two thicknesses (the
  program's starting value, not a standard's; a radius given is kept); the
  holding bolts' head clear of the bend (the program's rule); the end's
  bolts their edge distance from the bend (on the safe side); the weight
  from the developed area at the middle of the thickness (the heavier
  count); the clash check's flats to the bend line (more steel than the
  bend).
- **Checks**: each flat as a flat plate through the plate checks as they
  are; the holding bolts and the leg's bearing under them by the joints'
  own checks; the bend's own bending **not checked, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE
  where it governs**, said on the plate (a code check in the plugins: a
  question to the owner).
- **Estimated eccentricities**: an end on a bent plate is estimated with
  the plate's offset 0, no longer an upper bound.
- **Measured** on the 78 private real tower files: joints laid out
  whole 44.1 % → 45.8 %, member ends 62.8 % → 64.3 %, joints with a hand
  detail 49.7 % → 47.9 %; the estimated eccentricities' upper bounds
  24.3 % → 22.0 % of the ends ([theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#measured-j2b-the-bent-plate-2026-11-19)).

## 2026-11-19 (country server, phase 6)

**OHL-Design on a network: working sets picked and snapped, a partial
replica fed by rows, context tiles around the camera; the idle solve of
the context case; no whole-line copy in the packager** (the owner's order
of 2026-11-19, item 6; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md),
[user guide](../user-guide/working-set.md),
[data model](data-model.md#a-working-sets-replica-phase-6-2026-11-19),
[running it and its tests](postgresql.md),
[measured](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-6-working-sets-and-context-2026-11-19)).

- **Picking** (owner, 2026-11-16): whole routes (a list or the map), a
  station range along a route's first alignment, from one structure to
  another, or an area drawn on the map (a polygon). **Snapped out to
  whole tension sections**: every section with a span in a pick (or its
  structure in the area, or a span crossing it) comes whole, with the
  structures it hangs on, the jumpers on them or tapped on its spans, its
  spacers and the alignment points tied to its structures; a whole route
  takes every object of the route. Shown before it is confirmed (the
  server's extent: counts, the stations really covered, an outline on
  the map, notes); saved by name.
- **Decided here (conservative)**: other sections on the working set's
  structures with no span in a pick (circuits straining elsewhere) are
  **not in the working set** — taken again and again, they grew a third
  of a route to the whole route on the synthetic country (720 sections
  added) — but **come as context**, read-only: the replica holds what
  solving each of its sections alone reads (the other sections and
  jumpers on its structures, its spacers' sections, the alignments within
  500 m: the tile packager's sub-line), so its sections solve as on the
  whole line (tested, bit for bit) and each of its structures carries all
  its wires. A part of a route also brings its routes' alignments and
  their points (the stations need them), and so the structures tied to
  them, as context.
- **Decided here (conservative)**: **a working set is on one model**
  (line): the desktop holds one project; a route of another line is
  refused, saying to open that line's own working set.
- **Saved working sets** keep the picks only (network schema 3:
  `working_set.line_id`, `working_set.picks`, JSON as text); the extent is
  worked out again when one is opened, on the model as it is then. A row
  of schema 2 (routes, no picks) reads as its routes picked whole.
- **The replica** is a project file of today's format (no table or
  column added): the server's rows as it holds them (the JSON text and
  the place of each), the working set (`part`) and its structures' users
  outside it (`part_users`) as phase 3 and 8 wrote them, and the
  network's keys (`network.name`, `network.line`, `network.position`,
  `network.working_set`). The authority takes the rows between two
  commands (the extent's objects only) and a thread writes the file.
- **Fed by rows, not operations**: an operation may touch objects a part
  does not hold (its validation needs the whole line), so after each
  change that may touch a working set — its routes, an object its replica
  holds, or any change when it picked an area — the authority works the
  extent out again and sends what changed in it, came into it and left
  it, on the client's own queue before the change's broadcast (the rows
  of a user's own edit arrive before its answer). A change that does not
  say which objects it changed (a library file saved or removed, a merge,
  a line rolled back) sends the rows that differ from what the replica
  holds (the server keeps a hash of each object it sent). The replica takes them
  as one entry of kind `network`, without cascade (the server validated
  them on the whole model).
- **Joining again** sends what the replica holds, each object with a
  hash of its JSON (64-bit FNV-1a), and gets only what differs — whatever
  happened meanwhile, with or without a log entry. **Decided here**: a
  64-bit hash (a collision would leave one object unsent: about n²/2⁶⁵
  for n objects); a question for the owner below.
- **Edits** of a working set go to the server on its model (the whole
  model validates them, shared towers' rules included); the part's own
  refusals (no change of the context, no deletion in a part) apply to a
  part edited alone, not to the rows.
- **Context tiles** around the 3D view's target: 5 × 5 tiles of level 2
  (about 5 km across), a cache of 64 MB (least recently used first, never
  a tile in view), asked again when a change touched them; drawn grey in
  3D and the plan on a layer of their own ("Context (network, a
  drawing)"), the replica's own objects not drawn again; labelled a
  drawing in the context case — never a result, never in a table, never
  used by a check (2026-11-19). "Add this route" lists the routes of the
  same line, those in view marked.
- **The idle solve** (2026-11-19: the context case solved ahead when the
  server is idle, low priority, memory bounded): while no client's job
  came for 0.5 s and no tile a client asked for is being made, the next
  tile not kept at its revision is made — one at a time, so a client's
  tile waits for one at most; every tile once after a start, then the
  tiles changes touched. Its packages are kept only while the packages
  take less than half their bound (it never pushes out what clients asked
  for); it stops when the shapes reach nine tenths of theirs.
  `--no-idle-solve` turns it off. Measured: all 26 543 tiles of the
  synthetic country in 60 s, 78 MB of shapes, the server 1 252 →
  1 442 MB.
- **No whole-line copy in the packager**: the authority gives each tile
  the part of each model's line it reads (`Session::drawing_part`: the
  tile's objects and each of its sections' sub-line), the packager
  resolves only that; each section's sub-line is the whole line's, bit
  for bit (tested on the example lines and a 300-pylon country by tile).
  The part files of phase 3 no longer clone the whole line either
  (`Line::settings_only`).
- **Protocol 3**, messages added (additive; nothing of protocol 3 with
  working sets was released): `pick`/`extent`, `set_working_set`,
  `hold`, `save_working_set`/`delete_working_set`/`working_sets`,
  `route_detail`, `rows`; `join` gains `working_set`. Working-set
  requests share the interest pace (4 a second, 8 at once).
- **Not yet**: checks on a working set run on what it holds and pull no
  neighbours in (other lines' wires within a clearance's reach, the field
  distance: phase 10) — said in the Working set window and the user
  guide; rights (phase 7); the extent worked out again per change costs
  the size of the model (10 ms for a line of 145 structures; on the
  country as one model, the country) — an index of objects by route
  next; the replica's import entry holds every object twice (see the
  questions).

> **Owner:** (to answer, 2026-11-19; the recommendation after the arrow)
> 1. Other sections on a working set's structures with no span in it:
> context, read-only (as built), or members of the working set (a part
> of a route then grows, on the synthetic country to the whole route)?
> → context. 2. A working set on one line only, or across lines (several
> replicas side by side in OHL-Design)? → one line until branches over
> working sets (phase 11). 3. Joining again by a 64-bit hash of each
> object, or SHA-256 (a little slower, no practical collision)? →
> SHA-256 if you want certainty; the 64-bit one is kept until you say.
> 4. Protocol 3 with messages added, or protocol 4? → 3 (nothing
> released). 5. The context's reach: 5 × 5 tiles (about 5 km) and a cache
> of 64 MB? → as built, a setting later. 6. A replica's import entry
> holds every object again (3.5 MB for a route whose line's copy is
> 2.6 MB): write it with an empty command, as the network's import does
> (a change of how the session writes an import)? → yes.

Answered the same day — every recommendation, the empty import command
built: [the owner's answers](#2026-11-19-owner-22-recommendations-approved).

## 2026-11-19 (estimated eccentricities at level 3)

**O45 A1–A3, the joints' eccentricities set automatically** (step 4 of
the order of 2026-11-19; the owner's decisions of the same day; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/estimated-eccentricities.md),
[user guide](../user-guide/structure-analysis.md)):

- **A2, in the analysis**: the option **Estimated eccentricities** at

  through), off by default. The ends become rigid end offsets as a

  and compared on the private real towers). An upper bound's sign and a
  plate's side are not known: the cases are solved without the estimates,
  with them and with those the other way, each member and plate taking its

  SAFE SIDE: two or more ends of unknown sign at one frame joint (signs

- **A3, measured** on the 78 private real towers (kept privately): the

## 2026-11-19 (bolt grades by command, a bolt's tension capacity, a gusset plate's prying)

**The owner's decisions of 2026-11-19 on the bolts, built** (O19 stage
4.5; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-groups.md#bolt-strengths-a-grade-set-by-command)):

- **"Use 8.8 as default for bolts in the current line but add a command
  to set it."** A command, not a program default: OHL-Structure's
  **Design › Bolt grade…** (a tool window: the members picked, a member
  group's or the whole tower; one undo step; Escape cancels;
  [user guide](../user-guide/bolt-grade.md)) sets the grade of their
  bolts — their ends', their design data's and a gusset plate's own bolts
  onto them — or takes it away. The grades offered are SIA 263:2013, 3.4.2,
  Table 2's strength classes, read in the standard's text (8.8: f_yb 640,
  f_ub 800 N/mm²; SN EN 20898-2, which the table names, was not at hand).
  The grade is written into the structure file with its values, source and
  `set_by = "command"` (`[[bolt_grade]]`, a member's `bolt_grade`;
  **structure file version 21**, written only when a member has one), and
  every result says it ("bolt grade 8.8 set by command: f_ub 800 MPa, f_yb
  640 MPa (SIA 263:2013, 3.4.2, Table 2)"): the run's notes, the member
  ends' notes, the bolt groups' notes. The grade's f_ub and name go over a
  bolt's library or design data; a capacity given for another grade is
  dropped (the grade's worked out by the code, said); one given without a
  grade is kept. **No silent default**: a bolt without strengths stays
  without them, its tension said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE. There is no
  command-line form (`ohl` has no structure edits; the edit is
  `ohl_structure_edit::set_bolt_grade`). Applied to the current line's
  towers in the private data, not in the repository.
- **A bolt library's `tension_capacity` is the bolt's ultimate tensile
  load, F_u × A_s** (the guide of Kulak, Fisher & Struik, 17.6.1): defined
  so in the data model, the field's documentation and OHL-Structure's help
  beside it — not a design value (ASCE 10-97 4.3.3 takes 0.6 of it, SIA
  263 (77) 0.9 of it over γ_M2).
- **A gusset plate's own prying and bending under bolts in tension** by
  the same T-stub model as an angle's flange (Struik & de Back 1969, as
  Kulak, Fisher & Struik give it): the plate a flange **without a web** —
  the pull reaches it through the members' bolts, which hold it against no
  turning, so no moment is taken there (Eq. 17.8 with no moment at the
  web): Q = T b′/a′, twice a flange's with α = δ = 1, and its bending at
  the bolt line T b′ ≤ δ w t² f_y / 4 (SIA 263: over γ_M1); b to the
  farthest bolt of a member pulling it, a to where the plate stops bearing
  on the leg (its outline, the leg's toe or heel), w as a flange's — each
  on the safe side. Removed from the NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE list
  ([safe side](safe-side.md)); said not worked out only where the plate's
  geometry is not known or a plugin lacks the new additive interface
  `joint-check-groups-prying` (0.3 unchanged; both bundled plugins have
  it).

## 2026-11-19 (the joints' own checks: the follow-ups, bolts in tension with prying)

**The owner's decisions of 2026-11-19 on the joint checks, built**
(step 3 of the order of 2026-11-19, O19 stage 4.5; built, in active
development, not approved yet; [theory](../theory/joint-groups.md)):

- **A gusset plate's own bolts onto the leg** in the file format:
  `[plate.leg_bolts]` (`member`, `leg?`, `bolts`, `bolt_points`; structure
  file version 20, written only when a plate gives them; older files read
  unchanged). A plate on a leg running on through the joint — which has
  no bolts at that end — is held by them: checked as the plate's holding
  bolts and the leg's bearing under them, its outline drawn round them,
  counted in the bill of materials. No window for them yet (typed in the
  file; `connection_edits::set_plate_leg_bolts` writes them).
- **A joint that does not fit** reads "does not fit": a bolt's hole not
  within the flange it bolts onto, a holding bolt outside the plate's
  outline, holes in one ply overlapping, a bolt beyond the end of a
  member's steel where it is known. Coloured as failing in the 3D view,
  said in Joint details and on its own row of the report's *Joints*
  table, counted apart; the group is not sent to the plugin — never an
  infinite usage (`PlateUsage::does_not_fit`, `joints_not_fitting`).
- **Pieces in line not said continuous end at the joint** (on the safe
  side; before, one angle running on, an assumption). Where the piece's
  steel stops is not given: the code's conservative case, as before
  (ASCE 10-97: its end distance said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE; SIA 263:
  Table 17's e₁ at most). The joint layout proposing `continuous` for the
  user to confirm follows the layout's current work (ROADMAP O19).
- **Bolts in tension, with prying.** Each bolt's pull: the forces square
  to the plies and the moments bending them out of their plane, shared
  elastically about the bolts' centroid (`bolt_groups::tension`; no
  contact of the plies taken and each share taken as pulling — on the
  safe side; a moment about a line every bolt lies on said NOT ON THE
  SAFE SIDE). Prying: both codes ask for it without a method (ASCE 10-97
  4.3.3, SIA 263 6.2.2.4): the T-stub model of Struik and de Back (Stevin
  Laboratory report 6-69-13, 1969, as Kulak, Fisher & Struik's guide gives
  it, Eqs. 17.8–17.12, a′ = a + d/2, b′ = b − d/2, a ≤ 1.25 b) with α = δ
  = 1 — its largest bolt force, on the safe side —, the most prying of the
  flanges a bolt pulls governing, each flange's bending by the model's
  mechanism. By the codes, in the plugins (additive interface
  `joint-check-groups-tension`, 0.3 unchanged): ASCE 10-97 4.3.3 (F_t =
  0.6 F_u, case (b): the proof-load stress is not in the data) and 4.3.4
  (Eq. 4.3-2); SIA 263 Table 16 (77) and 6.2.2.6 (78); the stress area
  taken as 0.6 of the gross (on the safe side); a library bolt's
  `tension_capacity` read as its ultimate tensile load. Not worked out,
  said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: a plate's own prying and bending, a member
  that is not an angle, more than two gauge lines, the local prying of a
  bolt's head; not checked, said in the notes: fatigue and preloading
  (SIA 263 6.2.2.3), countersunk bolts and thin nuts (6.2.1.4).
- **The elastic method for the moments stays.**
- Still assumed or not checked, said: a member's own gauge eccentricity
  in its plane as a moment on its bolts, the plies' offsets in the
  levers, the joint's own loads through its plates, the holding bolts of
  a welded plate's several plates.

## 2026-11-19 (O42: the solve after an edit; the writer's lock released)

**Owner decisions of 2026-11-19**, on the questions the in-place work
left:

- The solver's internals in `ohl-line` may change so that a case's
  update reads only what each section and jumper needs; the results stay
  **the same bit for bit** (quality before speed: speed work never
  coarsens a computed result). The change of 03d27083 (the line's routes
  worked out once per update) is kept.
- `ohl-store-pg`: a writer's advisory lock is released explicitly when
  its connection's last user goes, so that a server started again at once
  is not refused; the tests' wait for the locks to go
  (`Cluster::wait_for_locks_gone`) is kept as a safety net.
- The safety-volume test's mesh of 0.5 m is accepted. The views (O42
  item 3) stay as they are.

**A solve's lookups** (roadmap O42; built, in active development, not
approved yet; [performance](performance.md#the-solve-after-an-edit-o42-2026-11-19)):

- **What a solve looked up again and again in the whole line** — for
  every section and jumper it solved: a structure, section or jumper
  searched by id, the sections at a wire point or through a structure,
  the line's route views made again, every jumper's estimated load worked
  out again (for each section solved in a jumper's design case), each
  solved shape searched against every section — is now **worked out once
  while the solve runs** (`ohl_line::lookups`). A case's update, a whole
  solve, `solve_line` and `solve_jumpers` open them; the line's own
  methods (`Line::structure`, `jumper_section`, `wind_factor_at_structure`,
  `alignment_views`, the nearest route segment, …) answer from them: the
  first object of an id and the line's order as a search gives them, the
  same values computed by the same code. They are kept per thread (as the
  solve's thread count already is), handed to the solve's worker threads,
  and only for the line borrowed for the solve (by its address while it
  is borrowed: it cannot change meanwhile); a copy or a part of a line is
  searched as before.
- **Chosen over the server's sub-line way** (each section solved on the
  part of the line it reads): the sub-line holds only the alignments
  within 500 m and the structures of one ring of sections, so the route
  views it makes can differ from the whole line's (a run's structures
  following each other, a structure far from every alignment); right for
  the server's drawing, not provably the same for results. The lookups
  give the same answers by construction.
- **The route views** themselves are worked out through the places of
  the structures and spans (each structure tried only against the
  alignments tied to it, of its routes or with a free point near it;
  each alignment's run on the straight followed only through the
  structures and spans near it), and the **nearest route segment** to a
  point through the routes' segments in cells, ring by ring, while a
  solve's lookups are open — of equally near segments the first, as the
  search keeps it. The jumpers' still-air lengths are kept up to 200 000
  (20 000 made every update on a country work them all out again).
- **A case's update solves its sections over the cores**, as a full solve
  does (each section alone is independent of the others), with the
  jumpers' loads on the clamps given once per update (before: copied for
  each section solved, quadratic in the line's size).
- **Proof**: the solves with the lookups equal the solves with every
  lookup searched (`lookups::searched`) — a whole solve, updates after
  structures moved and moved back, the full solves — on the example
  lines and a synthetic country, in still air and in wind, the jumpers'
  cut lengths cut again each way; every answer of the line's methods
  compared (ids given twice, local winds); the route views compared with
  the old way (`Line::alignment_views_reference`) on the examples (towers
  moved beside and off) and on synthetic countries; the grid's nearest
  segment with the search on 3 000 points. The existing tests unchanged.
- **Still worked out over the whole line once per update** (each a small
  part of an edit, said in performance.md): the route views (an edit may
  move a structure against an alignment), the jumpers' estimated loads,
  the lookups themselves, each jumper's inputs compared, the solved
  shapes listed for the jumpers.

**The writer's lock** (roadmap O46): `ohl_store_pg` releases the
network's writer lock (`pg_advisory_unlock`) when the writer's
connection's last user — the network or one of its models' stores — is
dropped, after rolling back an open step; a connection already broken
loses it with its process as before. Tested: a second writer connects at
once after the first is dropped (also in the middle of a step), not while
a store still uses the first's connection.

## 2026-11-19 (joint layout: a search per joint, the place of a member left kept)

**O44 J1 and J2** (owner, 2026-11-19: "plan ideas to get the automatic
layout working", approved with the recommendations, in the order J1–J8;
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-layout.md#the-search-per-joint-j1),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md)):

- **J1, a search per joint**: each plane's ends placed in every order
  that can matter, the owner's order first (so it wins every tie), the
  most ends then the least eccentricity winning, at most 400 placings per
  joint (said where reached); each end clear of the joint's fixed steel
  (what is not laid out: the clash check's pieces, seen from above in the
  end's layer) and of what the planes on bigger members laid out (boxes
  holding the angle, its bolts' heads and a plate: on the safe side for
  the fit); after writing, an end in a clash pulled back past it up to
  three times before it is left as it was (six clash rounds instead of
  four). Deterministic; values given by hand kept; a run again identical.
  The flange, the side and the leg bolted follow the member's roll (J3);
  direct or on a plate stays per plane.
- **J2**: a member left for its own sake keeps its place as it is (the
  ends laid out keep clear of it, in the plan and in the clash check);
  one left for want of room or for a clash, a plate under a member left
  and the members joined first are said with it, as before — keeping the
  place of every member left cost a quarter to a third of the ends laid
  out on two real towers (measured, left out). An assumption of the
  tool: the place kept is the member as it is, not where its hand detail
  will put it (said in the theory).
- **Measured** on the 78 private real towers: whole joints 27.6 % → 44.1 %,
  ends laid out 48.9 % → 62.8 %, a whole tower 1.5 to 1.9 times as long
  (10–15 s). The order search alone changed nothing there: said, kept.
- **The owner's example joints** (2026-11-19): direct flange connections
  and mid-panel gusset plates are invented test joints now; the bent
  plate at a corner is not built (a new element) and proposed next.
- No format change.

## 2026-11-19 (O42 and O46: edits in OHL-Design in place; the tests' PostgreSQL)

**OHL-Design's line is kept in step with the session in place** (owner,
2026-11-19: "per element modified instead of validating the whole
thing"; roadmap O42, first in the order; built, in active development,
not approved yet; [performance](performance.md#ohl-design-an-edit-taken-in-place-o42-2026-11-19)).

- **What changes**: after a command the session applied in place, the
  desktop takes only the line objects it changed from the session's line
  — a structure resolved with its type alone
  (`ohl_line::library::resolve_structure`, the steps of `resolve_with`
  for one structure), the sections a changed spacer ends on, a structure
  moved by a drag — puts them where the session has them, keeps its own
  reference index, and validates locally (`Line::validate_local`: the
  objects changed and what refers to them). The line's own fields follow
  the session's. The reference state is checked again as before (the
  stored state, never what an earlier check left). On a refusal the line
  is left as it was, as the whole way leaves it.
- **Made whole, as before**, and said in the edit's report ("the line
  made again whole: …"): a change of the line's settings (a `meta` row:
  the creep-stretch, bimetallic and reference-state switches, systems,
  circuits, the solver…), a library (read again whole, as before), the
  session's whole way (`ohl_session::Applied::whole`, new: objects of
  older forms read into others, an import), a line replaced meanwhile
  (another project line, libraries read again), objects that would not
  land in the session's order (a check).
- **Proof**: two copies of a project, the same random commands (moves,
  turned and retyped structures, a type not in the library, stringings,
  wind factors, deletions, renames, copies, alignment points, settings,
  batches), undos, redos and drags (let go or cancelled), one taking them
  in place and one whole: the same answers, the same line, the same
  solved cases (the plain and the typed example, three seeds, 60 steps
  each; most taken in place). Every edit any test of the desktop makes is
  also compared, while testing, with the line made again whole.
- **Kept**: only the cases shown are solved at once, the others after
  the 2 s settle (owner, 2026-11-18); no result is computed coarser, no
  file changes.
- **The solve's routes once per update**: a case's update made the
  line's route views again for each section it solved (its wind's side)
  and searched the line for it; the side now comes from the routes made
  once per update (a few sections) or from the routes' grid (many) — the
  same answer. Outside the in-place work, done because without it the
  app could not open the measured country at all; the jumpers still read
  the whole line each (left, on the roadmap).

**The tests' PostgreSQL: one cluster per test program, the flake
fixed** (owner, 2026-11-19: "the server seems to have very long tests
can they be optimised?"; roadmap O46; built, in active development, not
approved yet; [the scheme](postgresql.md#the-tests),
[timings](performance.md#the-tests-of-the-server-the-store-the-session-and-the-command-line-o46-2026-11-19)).

- **The flake** was not the port: `schema_and_the_writers_lock` dropped
  its first writer and connected the second at once; PostgreSQL lets a
  connection's advisory lock go when its process for it has ended, a
  moment later (1 run in 144 with six programs' tests side by side). The
  tests wait for it (`Cluster::wait_for_locks_gone`, at most 10 s): what
  is tested — one writer, and the lock going with its connection — is
  unchanged.
- **Ports**: a start refused for its port is made again on another, and
  every cluster started or joined is checked by its `data_directory`
  before a test uses it.
- **One cluster per test program**, shared by its tests across nextest's
  processes through file locks the operating system lets go with the
  process (a key lock while joining, making, leaving or stopping; a
  shared lock per test using it); a database and a folder per test,
  dropped at its end; the last test out stops and deletes the cluster; a
  killed test's cluster is stopped and deleted by the next test of any
  program. Chosen over a cluster kept by a process of its own (that
  process could outlive or die before the tests) and over nextest's
  setup scripts (no teardown).
- **The safety-volume test** meshes at 0.5 m instead of 0.2 m: the same
  command, steps, files and assertions; nothing it asserts depends on the
  mesh's fineness.

## 2026-11-19 (lattice towers: weight and quantities)

**A tower's parts counted and weighed; the self-weight from the counted
mass where every joint is defined** (owner, 2026-11-18: "go ahead" on the
lattice-tower open items, queue C item 7 — joint details stage 4.6, and
2026-11-02: "the self-weight factor stays until every joint is defined";
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/structure-weight.md)).

- **What is counted**: the members (section × length), and from the
  connection records only the bolts of each end (the bolt library's mass,
  else weighed from their sizes), the gusset plates and splice covers
  (outline × thickness), the welds between plates; a member end without a
  `[[connection]]`, a joint left for a hand detail, a bolted end without
  bolts or a plate without an outline make the joint not defined, its
  parts not counted. The automatic layout's parts are marked.
- **Two counts**: heavy (holes not deducted, a weld without a size at SIA
  263 6.3.6.3's largest throat both sides, the more open fillet corner, a
  member's steel beyond the work points) and light (holes deducted, the
  members to where their steel stops, a weld without a size left out).
  The steel of a plate: the heaviest member on it; nothing on it, and
  every weld: SIA 261 Table 28's 78.5 kN/m³.
- **The switch, a conservative envelope** (coordinator, 2026-11-19,
  pending the owner's answer to "should the heavy count be at least the
  members × the factor"): the counting is not validated against real
  tower weights and leaves out galvanising, fillers and fittings, so the
  counted mass may only raise a load. Where every joint is defined,
  OHL-Structure's runs take, where the weight loads the tower (a case's
  self-weight factor ≥ 1), the larger of the heavy count and the members ×
  the dead-load factor; where it holds the tower (< 1), the lesser of the
  light count and the members × the factor. The run's note says which
  governed ("… below the dead-load factor 1.3: factor kept (counting not
  validated)"). `self_weight_from` (structure file version 19):
  `"factor"` keeps the factor (said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE where the count is
  above it), `"counted"` takes the counted mass alone (opt-in, off by
  default, marked NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE until validated). An extension with
  its own members keeps the factor.
- **Not counted, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE**: galvanising, fillers and
  packs (no record in the data), fittings, the washers of a bolt without a
  library mass, a worked-out plate outline (the least plate), the welds of
  welded member ends. A case typed with a factor of 1 where the weight is
  favourable takes the heavy count (not on the safe side by the two
  counts' difference, shown).
- **The bill**: Design › Weight & quantities in OHL-Structure (a panel,
  counted in the background), `bill_of_materials.csv` among the CSV tables,
  File › Export › Bill of materials (xlsx), a section of the structure
  report.
- **Measured**: no shipped example has joint details; on 73 real towers
  after Orient angles and Lay out joints none has every joint defined (the
  legs' ends and the hand-detail joints have no records), so no run
  switches; the plates and bolts scaled to all ends give about 1.14 (up to
  1.20) against the typed 1.15 to 2.4 (median 1.3). The line's checks (the core) keep the
  factor.
- **Kept to the brief's limits**: `ohl-structures` gained the one key,
  `ohl-structure-link` the counting and the switch (run.rs, lib.rs), no
  change in `ohl-structures-fe`.
## 2026-11-19 (country server, phase 5)

**The server on the network's database: every model in memory, each
command one transaction with what its clients' interest needs, the
operation stream by interest with heartbeats and catch-up, tile packages
of the context, protocol 3** (owner, 2026-11-18: go ahead with the server
plan, report only; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md), the
[data model](data-model.md#the-servers-messages-protocol-3),
[running it and its tests](postgresql.md)).

- **`ohl network serve`** (`ohl_server::network`, the feature `network`
  of `ohl-server`: the command line enables it, the desktop application
  does not, so it carries no PostgreSQL client): the authority takes the
  network's writer's lock (a second server on the database is refused),
  opens a session on every model (each model's line read once, changed in
  place by each command), and keeps a **tile index** at the package level
  (structures, sections, alignments and alignment points by tile, each
  tile with its revision). The server of a project file is unchanged:
  the same code paths (both authorities now share the users, locks and
  broadcasts, `server::Common`), every earlier server test passing
  unchanged.
- **Each command is one transaction**: the session's rows (its steps
  nested in the unit), then the routes and references of each element of
  the main branch it changed (`object.routes`, `object_ref`), the models
  and tiles its log entries touched (`oplog.lines`, `oplog.tiles`), and
  the change in `stream` at its **position** — committed before it is
  broadcast. A command the session applied but whose rows cannot be kept
  is rolled back and its model read again from the database (said in the
  log and to its sender). **Positions** (decided here): (`seq`, `step`),
  the network's last log entry and, for changes making no log entry (a
  library put, a role, a commit), steps after it — so every change has a
  place, even those the log does not keep, and catch-up can replay them;
  kept in the database, they survive a restart.
- **Schema 2** of the network: `object.routes` (NULL until counted: a
  database imported before is counted when the server first starts),
  `oplog.lines`, `oplog.tiles`, the `stream` table; the import writes the
  routes and references of every element and the tiles of its entry
  (147 line projects: 88.5 s instead of 74.9 s, 369 MB instead of
  208 MB — the reference rows and the GIN indexes).
- **Tile keys** (decided here): one `bigint` per tile (level + 128 in the
  top 8 bits, column and row in 28 bits each); the package level a
  network setting (`net_meta` `tile_level`, 2 by default: 1 024 m — a
  view of a few kilometres takes a dozen tiles; a level-0 tile of 256 m
  would take hundreds).
- **The stream by interest** (plan §5.4): a client follows whole models,
  routes and tiles; each change is encoded once and broadcast; each
  connection passes on what touches its client (`stream::View`). What is
  for one client alone — a tile package, a catch-up, a change of its
  interest — goes on its own queue marked with the broadcast it follows
  (`stream::Feed` merges both in the authority's order): a tile taken at
  its revision is followed by exactly the changes after it, none missed,
  none twice. A **heartbeat** (every 2 s by default) carries the stream's
  position and the last change sent to that client: a client whose last
  is older missed something. **Catch-up** from a position (`catch`, or
  `since` when joining again) reads `stream` (10 000 changes at most,
  else "read again"). A change touching more tiles than a setting (256)
  reaches the clients that only view tiles as `tiles_changed` ("read
  again"). Interest and catch-up requests are paced (4 a second, 8 at
  once), a client views 256 tiles at most, its own queue holds 1 024
  messages (a client further behind is let go and catches up when it
  joins again).
- **Protocol 3**; the messages of 2 unchanged (a file server speaks 3
  with them alone). A client of protocol 2 is refused with "this program
  speaks protocol 2, the server protocol 3: update OpenOHL to join"; a
  desktop's hello to a network's server with what it can do instead
  (joining a network with a working set is phase 6). New messages in the
  data model.
- **A desktop following a model** (`client::join_network` with a model;
  the command line and the tests — OHL-Design's working sets are phase
  6): its copy written by a **reader** (a pool of read-only connections)
  at a snapshot taken between two commands, so the authority goes on
  while it is written; then the model's changes, replayed with the
  server's log numbers (`Session::set_next_seq`: a network numbers the
  entries of all its models in one sequence, a replica of one model sees
  gaps; the project file's statement is unchanged when no number is
  given — the desktop never gives one).
- **Tile packages** (plan §5.2): made by packager threads (2) from a copy
  of each model's line at the model's revision (copied once per revision;
  the database is not read for them): per structure its id, position,
  orientation, type, height and a stick (its drawing, else a mast and
  arms, and its strings); per section its wires solved in the **context
  case** (`net_meta` `context_temperature`, 15 °C, still air) — **each
  section solved alone** (`solve_one`: no jumper loads, no coupled
  assemblies, no flexibility; a drawing, never a result — said in the
  package's case and the web client's notes), on
  **the part of its line it reads** (its structures, the sections and
  jumpers at them, its spacers, the alignments within 500 m, the line's
  settings: the same shape as on the whole line, bit for bit — tested on
  every section of the example lines and every eleventh of a synthetic
  country of 300 pylons — so a solve costs the same in a model of the
  whole country), its sections solved side by side (4 threads); the alignments' segments crossing the tile (so a
  point moved changes the tiles of its segments only); the routes'
  names. **Caches**, each bounded (settings): packages per (tile,
  revision, rights class — 0 until phase 7, the key ready), 128 MB;
  solved shapes, 256 MB, keyed like the solve memo's (a 128-bit
  fingerprint of everything the solve reads: the section, the part of
  the line it is solved on, the line's settings — every field but its
  elements, listed so that a new field must be —, the wire type and the
  weather case); resolved structures per model and library revision
  (`ResolveCache`), the libraries read once.
- **The web client by tile** (plan §5.5): on a network's server it gets
  the network's routes and bounds, asks for the tiles around its view (96
  at most, the nearest first, again when the view moves), draws their
  packages with the scene's drawing code, and reads a tile again when a
  change (or a heartbeat showing a gap) touched it. Still a viewer.
- **Proved** (a throwaway cluster per test, a small synthetic country):
  the property — 24 random edits and undos, every client receives exactly
  the changes of the stream touching its interest, in order; a desktop's
  replica equal to the server's export of its model row by row, log
  numbers included, after edits, a gap and a catch-up; a lost change
  shown by the heartbeat and brought by a catch-up; a desktop gone while
  four changes were made gets exactly those, in order, then the live
  stream; what each command keeps in the database; tiles read again at
  the change's revision, only those touched; one writer per database;
  protocol 2 refused (QUIC, web, a file server); roles and soft locks as
  on a file server; a browser reading tiles.
- **Measured** on the 12 000-pylon synthetic country (147 line models,
  [performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-5-the-server-on-the-database-2026-11-19)):
  the server starts in 2.5 s and holds 1.25 GB idle; a connection costs
  0.08 MB (a viewer on a view of its own 6.2 MB, the shared caches); an
  area query 8 µs in the tile index (0.41 ms in PostGIS) at p95; a tile
  from the cache 7 µs in the server; a tile made p50 10 ms, p95 96 ms
  (each section on its sub-line; on its whole line p95 was 253 ms); a
  move applied and broadcast p95 10.8 ms; a view of 12 new tiles p50
  0.10 s, at most 0.52 s. The country as one model: start 1.9 s, a tile
  p95 68 ms, a move p95 9.8 ms. The machine was shared with two other
  builds (load 12–19).
- **Not yet**: OHL-Design on a network (working set, context tiles,
  partial replica: phase 6); rights (phase 7: until then every user who
  may join sees everything, edits by each model's own roles); point
  clouds, backgrounds and terrain tiles are not in PostgreSQL yet and not
  served (a model's surfaces are, whole, not served by tile); the
  context's wires are drawings (each section alone); a model as large as
  the country works, but the first tile asked after an edit copies its
  whole line (about a second for the 12 000-pylon country) — one model
  per line (as the import of per-route files does) keeps that small.

## 2026-11-19 (country server, phase 4)

**The PostgreSQL store: a model of the network opened as a project; the
same store tests on both stores; project files imported into the
network, one model exported as a project file** (owner, 2026-11-18: "yes
install PostgreSQL and PostGIS", go ahead with the server plan; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md), the
[data model](data-model.md#server-database-postgresql),
[running it and its tests](postgresql.md)).

- **`ohl-store-pg`** (new crate; the `postgres` client, MIT OR
  Apache-2.0; PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3, run as programs of their own):
  `Network` (a connection: the schema made or brought forward, the
  models, the audit), `PgStore` (one model as the session's store),
  `import`, `export`.
- **One model is one store**: the session opens a model as it opens a
  project file (`Session::open_on`); every table it uses has the model's
  code (`line_id`) in its key. The store keeps the file's meaning: steps
  as savepoints in one transaction (a savepoint outside one begins it), a
  new log entry the next `seq` of the network (the one writer: no gaps, as
  SQLite's rowid), grant and review ids the next of their model, times
  as the file writes them, revisions "newest first" in the order kept.
  Point clouds are refused there for now (they stay in the files).
- **The session**: holds its store as `Box<dyn Store>`; the interface
  gained `prepare` (make the store's tables, as the project file did when
  opened) and the rows of a whole copy (`meta_rows`, `blob_hashes`,
  `put_…_row`: rows kept with their ids and times; `store::copy::copy_all`
  copies a whole project between any two stores); `Session::store` reads
  it (the import); `Kind::parse` is public. **The project file is
  unchanged**: the same statements; the session's 128 tests, and files
  written by the build before and after through the example lines (edits,
  undo/redo, renames, a refusal, a setting, a library file, commits, a
  branch, a review merged, a tag, a grant, rollbacks, a deletion, a
  surface, a bundle out and in, a part) and an 800-pylon synthetic country
  edited: the same `sqlite3 .dump`, times masked.
- **The store suite** (`ohl_session::store::suite`, feature
  `store-suite`): 12 tests of every group of the interface (meta, users,
  objects with tombstones and places and their JSON kept as written,
  nested steps with a failed statement rolled back, the log, the spatial
  index, versions, project lines, grants and reviews, surfaces, whole
  copies, a session) run on project files (`ohl-session`) and on
  PostgreSQL (`ohl-store-pg`, a throwaway cluster); one session's
  transcript (import, edits, undo, redo, commit, branch, tag, opened
  again) the same on both. Without PostgreSQL's binaries the PostgreSQL
  tests say so and pass (the CI has none); `OHL_REQUIRE_PG_TESTS=1` makes
  that a failure.
- **Schema** (network schema 1): every table of the draft — network,
  users and groups, roles (the shipped six with their permissions),
  assignments, models, objects, reference index, log, spatial index with
  a PostGIS geometry (GiST) beside the tile key, working sets, versions,
  grants, reviews, country libraries, surfaces and their tiles, stale
  marks, notices, the audit (append only: a trigger refuses changes).
  Tables of later phases are made and stay empty. **Decided beside the
  draft**: the objects' JSON stays **text** (as the session wrote it; a
  `jsonb` column would reorder keys and rewrite numbers, so an export would
  not be the rows imported — queries use `json::jsonb`); `seq` unique per
  model (a copied model keeps its numbers; new entries numbered across the
  network); blobs once for the network with each model's use noted
  (`vc_blob_use`); the spatial bounds as four numbers (exact) beside the
  geometry; `object.routes` and `oplog.lines`/`tiles` come with phase 5,
  when the session keeps them current with every write (written only at
  import they would be wrong after the first edit).
- **Migrations**: numbered, forward only, run when a program connects, in
  one transaction under a lock; a newer database refused. (Refused without
  a recent backup: phase 13.)
- **One writer**: `Network::connect_writer` takes a PostgreSQL advisory
  lock for its connection; a second writer is refused; readers (an export)
  read at one snapshot.
- **Ids unique in the network**: a unique index on the main branch's
  elements (routes, alignments, alignment points, structures, sections,
  jumpers, spacers) of every model; a command making another model's id
  is refused in words ("ids are unique in the network").
- **`ohl network import FILE… --user U`** (plan §3.5): each file a new
  model (code: `--line` or the file's name), read into memory and never
  changed (nothing made beside it); one coordinate system and one grid for
  the network (the first import sets them; another refused with the hint
  to reproject); ids another model has renamed `CODE-id` (`CODE-id-2` …)
  by the session's own rename (everything referring follows); the main
  project line's current state — objects as they are, spatial index, meta
  rows, users (also as network users with the matching shipped role on
  the model), edit grants, surfaces — as one transaction with **one** log
  entry, then a revision "imported from FILE"; **twin towers** (another
  model's structure within 0.5 m in plan, of the same type — an estimate
  for the owner) listed, never merged; the file's history, other project
  lines, tags, point clouds and backgrounds left in it and listed; the
  report as text, HTML and JSON (`--report DIR`); in the audit. A part of
  a line, a file without a line, a code taken: refused, nothing left
  behind.
- **`ohl network export --line CODE OUT.ohl --user U`**: every row of the
  model through the store interface into a new project file (today's
  format), read back as the desktop reads it; `network.name`,
  `network.line`, `network.revision`, `network.library_pins`,
  `network.exported` added to `ols_meta`; in the audit.
- **Round trip**: a project imported and exported back has the same
  object, spatial index, meta (but `network.*`), user, grant and surface
  rows (sorted dumps compared) — the example line (a test), one synthetic
  line and the 12 000-pylon country (108 785 objects); imported again
  under another code, every id renamed and, mapped back, the same line.
- **Synthetic country**: `ohl synth country --per-line` also writes each
  route as a project of its own (`lines/CODE.ohl`; a tower shared by two
  routes in both files under one id: the import's clashes and twins);
  `ohl synth`'s measure works on any opened session
  (`project::measure_session`), so `ohl network measure` times the same
  moves through PostgreSQL.
- **Measured** (12 000 pylons, seed 1;
  [performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-4-the-postgresql-store-2026-11-19)):
  147 line projects imported in 75 s (2 657 ids renamed, 3 584 twin pairs
  listed), 208 MB; the country as one model: import 31 s (7 s without the
  revision), 194 MB, open 1.9 s, a move median 4 ms, an undo or redo 2 ms
  (the file: 2 and 1 ms), export 9.8 s.
- **Open**: the server on the database (phase 5: authority, caches, the
  interest stream, the columns above); rights evaluated (phase 7); library
  mapping at import (phase 9); point clouds, backgrounds and terrain tiles
  in the database; a backup check before migrating, TLS to a database on
  another host (phase 13); the merge of twin towers (an admin's command).
## 2026-11-19 (the joints' own checks: bolt groups and the leg's bearing)

**The bolt groups under the members' forces together and the bearing of
the member they bolt onto, a usage per joint** (queue C item 6 of the
lattice towers' open items, stage 4.5 of the
[joint details](joint-details.md); owner 2026-11-18: "Go ahead"; built,
in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/joint-groups.md)).

- **Two groups per joint**, gathered by the core
  (`ohl_structure_link::joint_groups`): a gusset plate's **bolts onto the
  leg holding it** (the joint's leg bolted onto the plate, with the
  members running on in line with it) carry the resultant of the other
  members' forces on the plate with its moment about those bolts'
  centroid; **the bolts onto a member** at the joint (its bearing) — the
  lapped members' and the holding bolts' — each the vector sum of every
  part it holds. Bolts of different parts within a quarter of a diameter
  are one bolt, checked on one shear plane under the sum (on the safe
  side).
- **The forces**: each member's end force from the analysis in the same
  case only (a frame's end shear with its axial force), at every joint it
  bolts at; a member's own bolts share its force equally (ASCE 10-97
  4.1: its gauge's offset from its axis not taken as a moment on them —
  the member's slenderness takes it; SIA 263 6.2.4.6 gives no rule, said
  not on the safe side in the theory); a frame's end moment and a plate's
  resultant moment shared **elastically** (Kulak, Fisher & Struik, *Guide
  to Design Criteria for Bolted and Riveted Joints*, 1987: the more
  conservative of its two analyses); the plies' offsets through their
  thickness left out of the levers, as in every lapped connection's
  checks. One bolt with a moment adding 1 % or more: a pin, said NOT ON
  THE SAFE SIDE; forces square to the plies: bolts in tension not
  checked, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE (as the plate checks of 2026-11-18).
- **The distances along each bolt's force**: to the ply's edge (a
  plate's outline; an angle's toe and, where its steel stops at the
  joint, its end), square to it, and to the next hole; where the steel
  stops not given, the code's conservative case. Two pieces in line
  through a joint of the same section, not said continuous and without a
  splice there: taken as one angle running on (an assumption, said).
- **The codes' rules in their plugins** (additive export
  `joint-check-groups`, interface 0.3 unchanged): ASCE 10-97 bolt shear
  4.3.2, bearing 4.4, end distance along the force 4.5.1 (not checked
  where the end is not known: said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE), spacing 4.5.2,
  edge 4.5.3; SIA 263 Table 16 (73)–(75), bearing (76) with e₁ along the
  bolt's force (the next hole: p₁ − d₀/2; the end not known: Table 17's
  e₁ at most, on the safe side), Table 17's distances along and square to
  the force (Figure 31). A plugin without the export: every group NOT
  CHECKED.
- **The joint's usage** is the largest of its plates', welds', bolt
  groups' and bearing checks: Joint details ("Usage of the joint", the
  list now "Joint checks"), the 3D view's joint dots and the report's
  new *Joints — usage per joint* table.
- **Not defined, said**: a plate the joint's leg does not bolt onto
  ("NOT CHECKED, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: how plate … is held … is not
  given"): a leg running on through a joint has no bolts there in the file
  (`kind = "continuous"`), so a plate's own bolts onto it cannot be given
  yet — a question to the owner; bolts not placed; a thickness not known.
- No file format changed; `PlatePart` gains `Holding`, `Bearing`,
  `NotChecked`.

## 2026-11-19 (buckling lengths from what braces a member)

**Lattice members' buckling lengths are worked out from what braces
them** (stage 4.3 of the [joint details](joint-details.md); owner "Go
ahead" on the lattice-tower open items, queue B, 2026-11-18; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[ASCE 10-97](../theory/asce10.md#buckling-lengths-from-what-braces-the-member),
[SIA 263](../theory/sia263.md#flexural-buckling)).

- **The geometry in the core, the rules in the code plugins.** The core
  finds each member's run (the members continuing it in line through its
  joints, within 10°) and the bracing points along it: every joint, with
  each other member there (design-checked, not a cable; a tension-only
  one only passing through) and the direction it holds the joint in, a
  support fixed in all three translations, and a `crossing` partner
  where it crosses away from a joint. No code's rule in it
  (`ohl_structures_fe::bracing`).
- **Plugin interface** (additive, interface version stays 0.3): an
  optional export `member-check-bracing` taking `member-check-full`'s
  records and the bracing of each member; called first, a plugin without
  it as before. Both bundled plugins have it.
- **Given lengths win.** A member's `k` (other than 1), `lk` or
  `length_ratios` are taken as before; each result says "from the
  bracing", "given" or "assumed: no bracing found". `k = 1` counts as not
  given (the default; it cannot be told from one not written). Where the
  bracing gives a member its own length between its joints about every
  axis (the lengths the default took), the check and its words are those
  before, the notes saying the lengths were worked out: the shipped
  examples and the typed example line give the same results to the bit
  and the same words. A support fixed along some axes holds the joint
  along each of them.
- **ASCE 10-97**: L between the points holding each axis (3.6, C3.7.4);
  a single angle's v held at any point (Figure 3.2 (a), Appendix B's
  Examples 5 and 7), its geometric axes and every other section's axes
  only where held along them (within 20°) or every way (two directions
  20° apart; assumptions); a leg with staggered bracing × 1.2 on the
  geometric axes (Figure 3.2 (b), (c)), its v between the points held in
  both faces where those are more than four panels apart (a panel the
  figure's L, between the points of one face); a crossing
  holds out of the plane only while the other diagonal pulls at least
  20 % of the compression (Example 7; never for an unequal angle bolted
  by its long leg); a member holding a point inside the run counts only
  while its own KL/r is within its class's limit (C3.7.4); the curves'
  ends per stretch (a point inside the run concentric and not
  restrained, Examples 7–9).
- **The 20 % rule also with lengths given** (ASCE 10-97): a crossing
  diagonal of class `crossing` is held out of its plane only while its
  partner pulls at least 20 % of its compression (before: any tension).
  More members unbraced out of plane: larger usages only.
- **SIA 263**: L between the joints held in the direction of buckling
  (5.4.1.3), read strictly (a joint held across the direction does not
  hold it); Table 13 and a crossing out of its plane not taken (5.4.1.4's
  conditions not judged); a member holding a point inside the run counts
  only while it resists 1 % of the run's largest compression in the case
  (4.2.3.7, its resistance in one pass: an assumption); 5.4.1.6's 0.9 L
  kept.
- **Both**: a run's end at a joint other members frame into is held
  every way, as a member's ends always were (ASCE 10-97 C3.7.4's working
  points; SIA 263 5.4.1.3's nodes the bars' length runs between) — the
  directions count at the joints a member runs on through. Measured
  first with the ends read by direction too: on three towers with every
  joint detailed, redundant members ending on a diagonal became
  cantilevers, dropped out as bracing and took the diagonals' bracing
  with them (SIA 263: members failing by N at N_cr) — not what either
  code means. A stretch to a free end (a run end nothing frames into) is
  a cantilever (twice, an assumption); a run nothing holds in a
  direction: twice, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE. Not taken: ASCE 10-97 3.7.4.4's K', SIA 263's Table 13 —
  the lengths longer.
- **Measured** on the shipped examples and the real towers (local, the
  lengths given removed to see the worked-out ones): see the results
  review (private); usages drop only where a bracing point is found and
  the code allows it.

## 2026-11-18 (a placed structure's Edit window: strings from the library, set by two angles)

**The Edit window of a structure without a type chooses which string
hangs there, not its parameters; a click in its view shows the object's
row; its wire points are set by their string's two angles** (owner,
2026-11-18: "this window should allow the change of string but not of
the strings parameter like weight, strength shape and so on"; "when we
click on something on the small window … the table on the left [should]
be switched to the right one and show the point data … also the wire
point table is unnecessary and it would be better to have the up/down
angle of the string and the compass angle to set it"; built, in active
development, not approved yet;
[user guide](../user-guide/desktop-app.md#the-edit-window-of-a-structure-without-a-type)).

- **Strings**: the library entry is chosen (`insulator`); length, kind,
  weight, wind area, compression and limits are read-only, "from library
  entry X". A value kept on the structure that differs from its entry is
  a warning; nothing is changed. A string without an entry: its values
  read-only, "not from a library entry: choose one, or make one from it",
  and **Make a library entry from this string** (one command; the entry
  holds its values exactly, the string keeps its own and names it, the

  there; **+ String from the library…** adds one.
- **Angles** (conventions to confirm): **from vertical** 0° hanging, 90°
  level, 180° straight up; **compass** in the structure's axes, 0° ahead
  along the line, clockwise seen from above; the **true bearing** beside
  it, read-only (compass − the structure's orientation, from north,
  clockwise). Typed, the string turns about its attachment point as a

  A V's angles are shown, not typed (said). Shown to 4 decimals; a

- **A click in the view** on a point, wire point or string switches to

  row chosen picks its object. Typing an attachment point's position
  follows the drag's rule (what hangs from it moves along) — on the
  structure types' screen too.
- **Positions kept exactly** in that window's document (12 decimals
  where not on a millimetre; before, every Apply put the points and wire
  points of the structure on the millimetre of its axes).
- **The window follows the line** after an Apply, an undo or a redo
  (before, after an undo it kept showing the change undone, and a later
