## 2026-11-18 (dragging keeps the strings' lengths)

**A dragged wire point turns its string about its attachment point; a
dragged attachment point takes its strings along** (owner, 2026-11-18:
"moving the attachement point should move the whole string (translation)
and moving the wire point should only influence the angel of the string
(same length and same attachement point -> rotation centered on the
attachement point)"; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[user guide](../user-guide/desktop-app.md#what-a-drag-does-to-the-strings)).

- **Where**: the structure screen's drags (`type_workspace`), so also a
  placed structure's **Edit** window (`placed_editor`, the structure
  screen on a structure without a type — the owner's report), and the
  line's 3D view handles (`handles`): one rule, `ohl-app`
  `string_drag::drag`, on the points, wire points and strings in any
  axes.
- **Before**: the structure screen wrote a dragged wire point where the
  pointer was (its strings' lengths changed: a placed structure's
  document gives every wire point its position) and moved a dragged
  attachment point alone (its strings' wire points stayed, so their
  lengths changed); the 3D view's handles moved I-strings along but left a
  V's wire point where it was (a length changed) and moved a dragged wire
  point freely.
- **Wire point dragged**: on the sphere of its string's length about its
  top (nearest the pointer, not snapped); a V on the circle both legs
  reach; three strings or more from tops not in one line: refused, said.
  The readout gives the string's length and its angle from the vertical,
  across and along the line.
- **Attachment point dragged**: everything hanging from it moves by the
  same displacement. A V whose other leg hangs from a point not dragged
  turns about that point (every length kept; the wire point nearest to
  where the dragged leg takes it); refused where the legs cannot meet.
- **What hangs below** a wire point that moves (a chain): moved by the
  same displacement (its strings keep their lengths and directions).
- **No drag changes a length** (owner, 2026-11-18: "in this window from
  the edit button the length of the string should not be editable as
  it's only in the string library"): no key frees it; another length is
  another library entry, chosen for the string.
- **Precision**: the line's 3D view and a placed structure's Edit window
  keep a length to 1e-9 m; a structure type's file writes positions to
  the millimetre, so a turned wire point keeps its string's length to the
  millimetre there (a translated one exactly: the point is put on the
  millimetre). No computed result and no file format changes.

## 2026-11-19 (joint layout: welded plates, splices)

**The owner's steps 4 and 1c** (owner 2026-11-18, the method; brief of
2026-11-19, "report only"; built, in active development, not approved
yet; [theory](../theory/joint-layout.md), [user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md)):

- **A welded plate** for an end no roll lays flat: a plate in its own
  plane welded to the flat plate of its face (two plates of the file,
  the weld's throat and length written — the layout's choice of a weld
  from both sides, 0.4 × the plates' thickness each side, at least 3 mm —
  so the existing weld check is made; the checks unchanged). Laid out only
  where the member's axis lies at most one plate thickness farther out of
  the flange than on a flat plate: the analysis keeps every axis through
  the work point, so a larger joint eccentricity would be left out
  silently — **on the safe side**: a hand detail, said. Whether to allow
  more (and take it into the analysis) is a question to the owner.
- **A splice of covers** for two angles in line of other sections that do
  not nest, both with bolts, nothing else bolting onto them at the joint
  (step 1c); the bolts' shear planes from the covers, a count given still
  winning. With bracing on them there the splice is not made (its bolts
  would pass through a cover: by hand) — measured, it cost joints laid out
  before.
- **Leg splices of one section** stay as they were drawn, said: where the
  splice is is not known from the data (the members' design bolts at both
  ends) — never a splice bolt check dropped.
- **No new setting**; two starting values of the program's, not a
  standard's: at most 75° off for a plate in its own plane, and the flat
  plate reaching the flange over half a square of its width.

## 2026-11-18 (joint layout tuned on real towers)

**The automatic joint layout tuned on two real towers** (owner,
2026-11-18: "for the automatic joint layout it doesn't work too much on
real structures … can you please tune it based on 1 or 2 pylons"; built,
in active development, not approved yet; [theory](../theory/joint-layout.md),
[user guide](../user-guide/joint-layout.md)):

- **Orient angles lays face members in their faces** (new record kind
  `face`): bracing, horizontals and redundants of a steep face, one leg
  in the face, the other out of the tower (the bracing on the outer face
  of the legs' flanges), the leg in the face down from the heel where it
  can — an assumption of the tool (no water lying in it), as for plan
  members. An angle running on in line through a joint that lies in a
  face of the legs is no chord any more (a face's diagonal running on
  through its crossing).
- **The layout names what an end bolts onto first**: the member running
  through the joint for an end bolting onto nothing named; for an end
  whose worked-out leg has no flange in whose plane it lies, a member
  running through the joint that has one (a plan diagonal onto the
  horizontal, not the vertical post). Its restraint is then worked out
  from what it is laid out onto (the code's stiffness rule, as for any
  end bolted onto a member).
- **Half a turn** for a member whose end cannot be laid out on an inner
  face, kept only where it lays out more of its ends and spoils none.
- **Plates on an inner face** are laid out (clear of the angle's other
  leg and root).
- **A clash leaves the members in it, not the whole joint**: those
  members as they were, with the clash, the rest of the joint laid out
  and checked again (up to four rounds).
- **The owner's order of steps** (same day: "pull everything back then
  line up the biggest profiles and join them …"; then "i might have been
  too confident in the method with 90% but i'm confident those few rules
  can help"): step 1 built — the biggest pair in line joined as one part
  (same section, turned alike, no bolts at either end: a splice with
  bolts stays a bolted splice, so no bolt check is dropped) or the
  smaller nested in the bigger; steps 2–3 as before (direct where the
  bolts land, else a plate on that flange); on a built-up member the ends
  whose bolts land are bolted to it. Not built: a splice plate for other
  sections in line (1c) and the welded plate for an end no roll lays flat
  (4) — they stay hand details, counted in the results.
- **Faster writing** (`connection_edits::Connections`: the connections by
  member and joint for many edits; the layout's plate ids from a set).
  A run writes the plates, the connections and its record at the end of
  the file (plates, connections, generators, each in its list's order), a
  made plate takes the first free id unless something was given on it by
  hand: the same layout gives the same text (a run again identical on
  the real towers).
- **Settings unchanged** (gap 10 mm, longest pull-back 300 mm, shift
  limit 30 mm, flatness 5°, corners 45°–135°): none was what blocked the
  two towers.

## 2026-11-18 (country server, phase 8)

**Towers shared by several routes: a working set per user, the rules
that keep the other routes connected, stale marks with notices, a
review on protected lines, connection conflicts in merges** (owner,
2026-11-16: the plan's question 5 answered as recommended — changes that
only move the other line allowed, its results stale and its owners told,
a review only on protected or built lines, parts used only by the other
line need rights on it; 2026-11-18: "continue structures + server plans";
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md), the
[data model](data-model.md#towers-shared-by-several-routes-2026-11-18),
the [user guide](../user-guide/shared-towers.md)).

- **Where a working set is**: a user's routes in a project file
  (`Session::set_working_set`, `ols_meta` `working_sets`; OHL-Design's
  View › Editable routes), or a part of a line (its working set, and the
  objects of the whole line using its structures, recorded when it is
  written: `part_users`). Until rights exist (phase 7) the working set
  stands for "the routes I may edit"; on the server it will be the
  user's picked routes.
- **No working set: nothing changes.** The check returns at once; no
  key is written; every existing test passes unchanged; project files
  written by the build before and after through the example lines and
  an 800-pylon synthetic country give the same `sqlite3 .dump`, times
  aside (36 steps: imports, edits, undo, redo, branches, a review merged, grants, a rollback, a deletion, a bundle, a surface, a typed line, an 800-pylon country measured). The one difference without working sets: a merge
  whose merged line would not be valid because one side changed a tower
  and the other strung a wire on it now offers that as a conflict to
  choose (before: refused with nothing to choose) — never a refusal of a
  merge accepted before.
- **What belongs to a route** (`ohl_session::shared`): a structure its
  own `routes`, else the routes of the alignment points tied to it and
  of every alignment within 5 m of it — worked out without a search of
  the whole line, so never fewer than `Line::structure_routes` gives,
  sometimes more (safe side); a section the routes all its structures on
  a route share, else (from one route into another) all of theirs; a
  jumper its sections' (else its structures'); a spacer its sections'.
  An object is the other routes' when one of its routes is outside the
  working set; a structure is *theirs* (not to be changed at all) when it
  names only outside routes, else when everything using it is on
  outside routes only, else when its place puts it on outside routes
  only — an alignment drawn near another route's tower does not make it
  one's own, nor tying one's alignment point to it.
- **The rules and their tests** (`shared_tests.rs`, the example's two
  routes sharing the Y pylon T3, a jumper between them with a support
  clamp, a spare set, a structure group naming both routes' towers):

  | # | Refused | Test |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 | changing, making or deleting the other routes' sections, jumpers, spacers, alignments, alignment points, routes; changing a structure that is theirs | `rule_0_the_other_routes_objects_are_not_changed` |
  | 1 | deleting or renaming a structure they use | `rule_1_a_used_structure_is_not_deleted_or_renamed` |
  | 2 | their wire point removed, left out, renumbered | `rule_2_a_used_wire_point_stays` |
  | 3 | what it hangs on changed (strings, tops, the points above) | `rule_3_what_it_hangs_on_stays` |
  | 4 | suspension ↔ strain, hanging ↔ fixed | `rule_4_suspension_stays_suspension` |
  | 5 | a support clamp's strings or assembly changed | `rule_5_a_support_clamp_keeps_its_strings` |
  | 6 | their route taken off the structure, their point untied, the structure moved off their alignment | `rule_6_the_other_route_stays_on_it` |
  | 7 | a structure named by their circuit start or a group naming their structures deleted or renamed | `rule_7_a_group_naming_the_other_routes_structures` |
  | 8 | anything else leaving them not valid (the validation's refusal names the outside routes) | `rule_8_the_other_route_stays_valid` |
  | §7.4 | their hardware (a wire point only they use, what only it hangs on) changed | `hardware_only_the_other_route_uses_is_its_own` |

  A typed structure with other routes' wires on it may move (whole, or a
  point or string of its own) but not change the make-up of its own
  hardware, its omissions, type or extension: the session does not read
  the structure library, so whether such a change keeps their wire
  points cannot be shown — refused (safe side; open: reading the
  project's type files). A wire point strings reach is placed by them:
  only a fixed one's own place counts as a change of it.
- **Allowed, marked stale** (`moving_a_shared_tower_marks_the_other_route_stale`):
  moving, turning, the height, foundations, local factors, a shared
  string or point moved (its topology kept), an insulator changed; undo
  and redo too. Each outside route gets a stale mark with a notice
  ("T3 moved 0.80 m" by ana, log entry N) in `ols_meta` `stale_routes`,
  written in the command's own step (the latest 20 notices kept per
  route, the others counted: a busy corridor does not grow it without
  end); the log entry's note and `Applied::notice` say it; a change of
  the settings or library files marks every outside route. A user with
  the route in their working set (or with none) marks it up to date
  (`Session::clear_stale`).
- **Protected (built) lines** (`a_protected_line_needs_a_review`): on a
  protected project line such a change is refused, even for an admin
  with a working set: "needs a review by its owners — make the change on
  a project line of your own and submit it for review". The existing
  review flow; an approved review's merge is not a user's edit. The
  desktop has no per-route "built" mark: the protected project line
  stands for it (a question for the owner).
- **Parts** (`a_part_checks_the_users_it_recorded`): the rules 1–7
  against the recorded users and the context it holds; rule 8 for
  objects it does not hold is the whole line's (the part's check stays a
  preview).
- **Merges** (`a_merge_breaking_a_connection_is_a_conflict`;
  `shared::connection_conflicts`, also in project lines brought in,
  reverts and OHL-Design's merge window): a structure changed on one side
  only, a section or jumper made or changed on the other on it, the
  change breaking it (rules 1–5) — a conflict on the structure: keep the
  change (the other side's wire not taken) or the structure as it was.
  Without working sets only where the merged line would not be valid
  (a set removed under a new section: before refused, now a choice; a
  string turned to strain under it: a valid line, merged as before);
  with working sets always.
- **Property tests**: random commands (the phase-3 generator plus
  hardware changes at the shared tower: strain toggled, strings removed
  or re-hung, points moved, sets left out, routes given, moves) by a user
  working on one route, on the example (12 seeds × 60 steps in the
  suite; 1 500 seeds run once: 46 864 accepted, 27 001 refused by the
  rules) and on a 400-pylon synthetic country (half its routes in the
  working set, 250 steps at towers shared with the other half, undos
  and redos among them): every
  command accepted with the working set is accepted the same without
  it, the other routes' own objects are as they were (an alignment
  point's place aside, following a shared tower), the line is valid.
- **Measured** (12 000 pylons, seed 1; `ohl synth measure --working-set`:
  74 of 147 routes in the working set, 50 moves of the 176 towers shared
  with the others, against `--shared-towers`, the same towers without
  it; [performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-8-towers-shared-by-several-routes-2026-11-18)):
  a move median 4 → 5 ms (95 % ≤ 8 ms), an undo and a redo 3 → 4 ms;
  every move marked the outside routes stale; memory unchanged.
- **Open**: rights (phase 7) to replace the working set as "what I may
  edit" and to tell owners (the server's notices, phase 5); typed
  towers checked with the project's type files; a per-route built mark
  on the desktop; stale marks for merges (a merge marks nothing stale
  yet); the routes of structures by their place are counted generously
  (5 m), so a tower beside another route counts as on it.

## 2026-11-18 (country server, phase 3)

**An edit costs what it touches: commands applied in place, a reference
index, the local validation; the whole validation, the index and the wind
sides worked out without searches; a session over a part of a line;
longer sections in the synthetic country** (owner, 2026-11-18: phases 0–3
approved; "it could be nice to compartimentalise the validation per
route", then "which validation need the whole system? Mostly just edit
and validate whatever is modified. Your option is also valid"; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md), the
[data model](data-model.md#what-the-session-keeps-in-memory-and-how-a-command-changes-it-2026-11-18-country-server-phase-3)).

- **Reference index** (`ohl_line::index::LineIndex`): per kind, id →
  place in the line; per target (an object, or a structure's wire point)
  the objects referring to it; the sections with a span point by
  station. Made when the file opens, kept up to date by the commands.
- **Commands applied in place** (`ohl_session::in_place`): the objects
  map, the line and the spatial index change where the command changes
  them; nothing is copied, nothing read again from every object's JSON.
  **The same result as before**, to the byte: the same line (it is the
  line read again from the objects), refusals and their words, log
  entries with their dirty sections, index rows. The **whole way** stays
  for the import, a change of the line's settings, objects in a form of
  older files that reading changes others for (routes of version 2,
  alignments of version 3, own load case sets, circuit names given
  circuits when read), and commands changing more than 2 000 line objects
  plus an eighth of the line (faster whole; the same result). A refusal,
  and a unit of work failing half-way, is put back from a journal.
- **Local validation** (`Line::validate_local`): what an edit changed and
  what refers to it, by the reference index — the same checks in the same
  order as the whole validation, so the same first problem. Every check
  and its reach:

  | Check | Reach when an edit is validated |
  |---|---|
  | Every number finite | the objects changed |
  | Ids given and unique (every kind) | the objects changed (a lookup in the id index) |
  | Structure: resistances, load cases, foot movements, place, strings, points | the structures changed |
  | Structure: its routes there | the structures changed and those giving a route changed |
  | Alignment point: finite, its structure there and within 1 mm | the points changed and those tied to a structure changed |
  | Alignment: its route and points there, no point twice | the alignments changed, through a point changed, of a route changed |
  | Section: structures and wire points there, stringing, local wind and ice, span points inside their spans, spreads, colour, bundle | the sections changed and through a structure changed; with a structure, alignment, point or route changed, every section with a span point placed by station (its station reads the routes and every structure) |
  | Jumper: ends there, bundle (from the first section at its end or the tap's), taps, points, length/sag/tension, support clamps | the jumpers changed, at a structure changed, at a wire point of a section changed, tapping a section or jumper changed, and those tapping them, all the way |
  | Spacer: its sections, spacer clamps, finite elements, one span, values | the spacers changed and on a section changed |
  | One system phase per conductor path (paths join sections across routes: shared wire points, jumpers) | every path through a section changed, a section at its wire points or a changed jumper's end section — each path whole |
  | Circuit starts: section points, each once | every start, when a section changed |
  | No ring of jumpers on taps | whole, when a changed jumper taps a jumper |
  | Settings: bimetallic, creep-stretch, electrical, structure groups, format, heights' datum, display, defaults, circuits, systems | whole: a change of the settings goes the whole way |

  Clearances, crossings and loads are engineering checks, not part of the
  validation: scoped in phase 10. **Per-route blocks of findings are not
  kept** (the owner's refinement: optional): a valid line has none, and
  the reach above is finer than a route (an edit on one route re-checks
  the objects of other routes that refer to it — a shared tower's
  sections, a jumper or spacer between routes, a conductor path through
  both — never skipped because the edit stayed on one route).
- **The whole validation** looks objects up in the index instead of
  searching the lists (a jumper's section, a tap's, a spacer's, a
  structure, the circuit starts): 16.2 s → 0.56 s on the 12 000-pylon
  country, the same answers (the validation as it was kept as the tests'
  reference). **The wind sides** of the sections (which routes give the
  wind from which side, `sections_against_the_line`) through a grid of
  the routes' segments, the same nearest segment, and kept by the
  session (`ohl_line::solve::Sides`): an edit moving a route's point (a
  tower with its tied point) works out again only the sections as near
  to a segment that changed as to their own nearest one, and those whose
  ends moved — exactly the sections whose side can turn. **The spatial
  index's entries** by the index.
- **A session over a part of a line** (`Session::write_part`, `ols_meta`
  `part`): a working set and what it refers to written into a file of its
  own, worked on in place; no change to the context, no deletion or
  rename there (what they take may be outside); what refers to the
  working set from outside is not seen there — the whole line's session
  (the server) has the last word. The single-file desktop and the server
  keep loading everything.
- **Synthetic country**: `--section-spans` above 2 now makes angle
  suspension towers until a section has about the spans asked (5 asked:
  4.94 on average at 12 000 pylons, seed 1); the default country is the
  same, bit for bit (its hashes tested). `ohl synth measure` also times
  redos, says the dirty sections per move and with `--whole` sends every
  command the whole way.
- **Proof**: random command sequences (moves, puts valid and not,
  deletions with what they take, renames, alignment points, spacers,
  taps, undo, redo, rollbacks, project lines, units of work failing
  half-way) on two project files, one in place and one the whole way:
  the same answers, objects, lines (also the line read again), spatial
  and reference indexes after every step, the same rows in both files at
  the end; the same on two small synthetic countries (towers of two
  routes, 2 and 5 spans per section); random edits of a line with every
  kind of reference, valid and not: the whole validation by the index,
  the local one and the dirty sections equal the reference. Files written
  by the build before and after through the example lines and an
  800-pylon synthetic country: the same `sqlite3 .dump`, times aside.
- **Measured** (12 000 pylons, seed 1; before → after;
  [performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-phase-3-an-edit-costs-what-it-touches-2026-11-18)):
  sections of ≈ 2 spans — a move 29–59 s → median 2 ms (at most 4 ms
  over 50 moves), an undo 27–54 s → < 1 ms (at most 9 ms), a redo → < 1
  ms, opening 24.6 s → 1.8 s, the whole validation 16.2 s → 0.44 s, peak
  memory 1.32 → 1.19 GB, a command the whole way (a settings change) →
  1.0–1.5 s; sections of ≈ 5 spans — a move 10–12 s → 1 ms, opening 9.5 s
  → 1.0 s. An edit touches 4 to 26 sections to solve again, whatever the
  network's size.
- **Also faster, the same results**: the dirty sections of two whole lines
  (`sections_to_solve_again`, the whole way and OHL-Design's other project
  lines) look the jumpers and spacers up instead of searching them
  (quadratic before: half a minute per settings change on the country).
- **Open**: opening still reads and checks everything once (seconds); a
  partial replica fed by the server (phase 5–6); per-route blocks of
  findings not kept (above).

## 2026-11-18 (lattice towers: the safe-side items)

**Queue A of the lattice towers' open items** (owner, 2026-11-18: "Go
ahead", queue A first; built, in active development, not approved yet).
Every change makes a usage equal or larger; the results say where
something is still not on the safe side.

- **A weld's moments** ([theory](../theory/joint-plates.md#the-force-a-weld-carries)).
  Before, the force a weld carries was spread evenly along it and the
  moment of that force about the weld was not taken (not on the safe
  side, said). Now each member's force acts along its line through its
  bolts; about the weld's middle the moment bending the weld along its
  length (M) and the moment about the seam's line (T), the larger of the
  two sides' (a ring: the sums); a weld shorter than the seam where along
  it its moment is largest. The SIA 263 plugin checks (87) and (88) on the
  force per unit length at the weld's most loaded end, F/L + 6M/L² +
  6T/(L w) (6.3.1.7: a simplified distribution; 6.3.2.1: the resultant
  per unit length) — without moments the force alone, as before. T > 0
  is said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE (6.3.6.5: a one-sided fillet bent across
  should be avoided; one side or both is not in the data). ASCE 10-97 has
  no weld rule, with or without moments: not checked, said.
- **A shift where only bars meet** ([theory](../theory/structures-fe.md#eccentric-member-ends-rigid-end-offsets)).
  Before, the moment of a connection's shift at a joint only bars meet
  was left out (said, not on the safe side). Chosen of the two ways the
  plan named: the moment N·e into the shifted member's own check, not a
  rigid link making the end a frame end (that would change the solve and
  add rotations nothing else holds at such a joint; frame towers' results
  are untouched either way). The solve is unchanged; the check takes the
  moment about the member's local axes as a uniform moment (the larger
  end's), the member alone taking it (on the safe side for it,
  statically admissible for the joint); the plugins check a truss whose
  forces carry end moments as a frame (ASCE 10-97: the linear sum;
  SIA 263: its stability check). A cable cannot bend: left out, said NOT
  ON THE SAFE SIDE. The end shears N e / L are not put into the solve
  (about e/L of the force, said in the theory). Found on the way, in the
  SIA 263 plugin: the stability check took a frame angle's moments only
  about axes named y and z — an angle's axes are u and v, so they were
  dropped (with `single_angle_moments`); and an eccentric angle's (50)
  replaced the frame moments by N·e. Both fixed on the safe side: about u
  and v the bound |M_y| + |M_z| (uniform), added to N·e.
- **A gusset plate in compression** ([theory](../theory/joint-plates.md#a-plate-in-compression-an-assumption)).
  Neither standard has a rule; before, "plate buckling not checked" was a
  note and the part's usage left it out. Now a strut, an assumption said
  as such: Whitmore's width (the primary source, Whitmore 1952; Thornton
  1984 for the strut), at most the width the plate's sections take; the
  free length from the bolts nearest the joint to the nearest bolt of a
  leg on the plate within that spread, else to the plate's edge (other
  members' bolts not taken as holding it); K = 2, the largest classic
  case (no tests of these plates: the conservative value, a question to
  the owner); the code's own column curve (ASCE 10-97 3.6 with E =
  200 000 MPa of its Appendix A; SIA 263 4.5.1 on curve c, Figure 7's for
  solid sections, E = 210 kN/mm² of 3.2.2.1). One bolt (no Whitmore
  width) or no free length: not checked, said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE.
- **A frame member's end shear and moments in the plate checks**
  ([theory](../theory/joint-plates.md#a-frame-members-end-shear-and-moments)).
  Before, the axial force only (said). Now the analysis' end forces at the
  member's bolt group, split by the plate's plane, go with the part; the
  plugins add their sizes: bearing by the most loaded bolt of the group
  elastic about its centroid, at the nearer of the end and edge
  distances; the other checks under N + V + 6M/w + 6M_o/t in tension and
  compression. The force square to the plate and the out-of-plane moment
  pull on the bolts: bolts in tension are not checked, said NOT ON THE
  SAFE SIDE where they add 1 % or more. One bolt is a pin: no moment
  through it (its bearing under N + V); a moment adding 1 % or more said
  NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE (the analysis' frame end is not what the joint
  does). Measured first without the 1 % rule and with an infinite bearing
  for one bolt: nearly every part of the real towers' plates said or
  failed for moments of a few N m (numerical) — hence the rule, as for
  members' moments. The tearing path towards a plate's side edge (the other half
  of this item) was already built on 2026-11-08 under both codes: kept.
- **Plugin interface** (additive, interface version stays 0.3): a new
  optional export `joint-check-moments` — `joint-check-full`'s records
  with, per part and case, what acts on it beside its force
  (`part-moments`) and a bolt group's plate's free length in compression.
  OpenOHL calls it first; a plugin without it gets `joint-check-full` and
  each part concerned is said NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE (what was not sent).
  Both bundled plugins have it.

## 2026-11-18 (third round)

**The bolt tools' force basis into the code plugins; default minimum bolt
distances; Member details follow the parameter file; provisional bolts
keep a tower at level 3 everywhere** (owner, 2026-11-18, on round 2's
open points: "1 yes go ahead, 2 ok but put a default minimum, 3 yes fix
it"; the core change for provisional bolts approved the same day; built,
in active development, not approved yet).

- **The force basis is the plugin's own.** Without an analysis the bolt
  tools' minimum distances take the force one bolt transmits as the
  bolt's design shear capacity; before, the core worked it out by ASCE
  10-97 4.3.2 for every code (`member_ends::bolt_shear_per_bolt`). Now
  each design-code plugin works out its own through an additive export
  `bolt-distances-full` (`bolt-distances`' records with the end's merged
  bolts, the analysis' force per bolt and the parameter file; back the
  force taken and where it comes from). **ASCE 10-97** (`asce10`): the
  same formula moved — compared before the core's use was removed on the
  shipped examples and two conversions of a real line's towers plus three
  level-4 towers (146 + 3 structure files and the 2 examples), every
  member end in the leg and in two plates, with and without an analysis
  force: 4 013 640 rows, every distance, force and clause identical to
  the last bit. **SIA 263** (`sia263`): its own Table 16 resistance over
  γ_M2 (the parameter file's), smaller than ASCE 10-97's (0.80 of it for a
  given capacity, 0.65 for f_ub alone with the factor 0.5); Table 17's
  minimums take no force, so **no distance changed** (the same 4 013 640
  rows: 2 113 356 show the smaller force, 0 a changed distance). A plugin
  built without the new export is asked as before (the analysis' force,
  else ASCE 10-97 4.3.2's bolt shear — `bolt_shear_per_bolt` kept for
  that alone, `bolt_rules::shear_without_plugin`). Interface version
  stays 0.3 (additive).
- **Default minimum bolt distances** where no code gives any (the simple
  check, a plugin without `bolt-distances`, one that returns none): end
  and edge 1.5, spacing 3 bolt diameters to start with (what the plate
  outlines and the joints' drawing already assumed), editable in
  OHL-Structure's Design › Analysis (`[default_bolt_minimums]`, structure
  file version 18, raised only when given). The bolt tools, the bolt
  layout form, the plate outlines and the joint layout use them, said
  everywhere as "default minimum, assumed, not a code's" with why; never
  in place of a code's own minimums. They take no force: NOT ON THE SAFE
  SIDE where a code's force-dependent minimum would be larger (said with
  a plugin that gives none; theory: joint plates). The joint layout's
  provisional bolts take the default spacing and end distance for a pitch
  and end distance not given, and the default edge distance where no code
  gives one — before, a given edge distance of the end was taken first
  in the simple check.
- **Member details and the bolt tools** in OHL-Structure are worked out
  again when only `Plugins/<plugin>.toml` changes (their caches keyed on
  the file's content; tested with SIA 263's factors).
- **Provisional bolts keep a tower at level 3 in the core**
  (`StructureType::provisional_bolts`, reading only the joint layout
  record's `provisional` list; `detail()`, `level_note()`): OHL-Design's
  structure picker, properties and type workspace, `ohl structures fe` and
  the line's calculation level 4 give level 3 and say why;
  OHL-Structure's own workaround (its run reading the file without
  `joint_details`) is gone. No file format change; older files unchanged.

## 2026-11-18 (country server, phases 0–2)

**A country server with PostgreSQL started: the decisions written down
(ADR-0013), a synthetic country to measure on, the session's SQL moving
behind a store interface** (owner, 2026-11-16: "PostgreSQL is good", the
plan's recommendations accepted, "Just reduce the synthetic test"; owner,
2026-11-18: "the rights and roles should be applied to almost every
element and library", "the single user model should still be saved under
the current format but the server could use the postgresql as a place to
store all the models and models element then each model could be exported
individually in the OHL format from the server"; in active development,
not approved yet; [ADR-0013](../adr/0013-country-server.md), amendments
to ADR-0004, 0005, 0008 and 0010, the draft
[server database](data-model.md#server-database-postgresql)).

- **Two modes, one session**: the desktop keeps the single-file `.ohl`
  (schema 6, unchanged — files written before and after the store
  interface are compared dump against dump); a server keeps every model
  and model element in PostgreSQL; any one model exports as a standalone
  `.ohl` (rights-filtered, the *export* permission, audited).
- **One writer**, each command one transaction; the line model of the
  network whole in the server's memory, the heavy parts (LiDAR, terrain,
  structure types' models, results) streamed and cached within bounds.
- **Working set and context**: whole routes, a part of a route (station
  range or structure A to B) or an area on the map, always snapped out to
  whole tension sections; the rest streamed as light, read-only tiles.
- **Computations** on the working set plus what touches it, each check by
  its own distance; a neighbour not pulled in makes a check *not all
  checked*, never a pass.
- **Rights and roles on almost every element and library**: roles are
  named sets of permissions (see, edit, create, delete, review, export,
  lock, request, manage rights); assignments give a role to a user or
  group on a scope (network, region, line, route or part, element kind,
  object, library kind, file or entry); default deny, union of grants,
  *see* needed for the rest, an explicit deny by a network admin
  overrides. Derived data (tiles, caches, indexes) follows its sources.
  The desktop file keeps today's three roles.
- **Country libraries**: locks per kind or file, maintainers (role
  assignments), library reviews, requests that may be refused, releases;
  built lines pinned, designs in progress following the latest.
- **Measured first** (phase 1): `ohl synth country` (`crates/ohl-synth`)
  makes a synthetic country of the owner's size — 12 000 pylons, 2.47
  systems per pylon, 10.5 % of them shared by two routes, 147 routes,
  4 195 km, 50 936 sections, 43 041 jumpers — deterministically (its
  SHA-256 tested per seed); LiDAR only on four sample tiles, the
  country's **extrapolated** from them (≈ 90 GB), said so. Today's code
  on it as one project: open 25 s, ≈ 0.9 GB, **every edit ≈ 32 s** (the
  whole line rebuilt and validated per command) — what phase 3 must
  remove ([performance](performance.md#synthetic-country-todays-session-on-a-whole-country-2026-11-18)).
- **Store interface** (phase 2): the session writes no SQL any more
  (a test keeps it so); `ohl_session::store::Store` offers what it needs
  in its own words (objects, log, spatial index, versions, grants and
  reviews, surfaces, settings, nested steps) and `SqliteStore` holds every
  statement and the upgrades of older files, moved unchanged. **No change
  of behaviour or file**: every existing test passes unchanged, and files
  written before and after through the example lines (import, edits,
  undo, redo, branches, tags, a review merged, grants, a rollback, a
  deletion, a bundle, a surface) and through a synthetic country (an
  800-pylon one written whole; the 12 000-pylon one edited and undone)
  give the same `sqlite3 .dump`, times aside. The point-cloud and
  background stores still open the file themselves (for later).

## 2026-11-18 (second round)

**ASCE 10-97, the default member check, moved out of the core into a
bundled plugin; a plugin's settings reach its joint checks and Member
details; a longer time limit for the bundled plugins** (owner,
2026-11-18, on round 1's open points: settings to the joints and Member
details, the file name kept; the time limit raised for bundled plugins
only; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/asce10.md), [plugins](plugins.md#the-full-records-parameters-foot-movements-bundled-codes)).

- **ASCE 10-97 moved, not rewritten** (`plugins/codes/asce10`, AGPL like
  `sia263`): the members' check (the core's `asce10.rs` and its part of
  `check.rs`: the usage, the clauses not covered, the redundant-force
  check), the plates (`plates.rs`' ASCE part) through `joint-check`, the
  bolt distances of 4.5 through `bolt-distances`. It takes no parameters
  (a parameter file with a value is refused, named). **The same numbers
  bit for bit**: before the core's copy was removed, the shipped example
  towers, the lattice towers of two conversions of a real line (144
  structure files, 579 to 3 030 members) and three of them made level 4
  with a joint detail at every member end were checked by both in four
  load cases and up to five variants — 4 487 212 member results, every
  usage identical to the last bit and every "what governs" word for
  word; the three level-4 towers' plate checks (9 452 part results) and
  the validation report's values likewise. The examples' 2 256 results
  stay a test against the plugin (the hash recorded before the first
  round). Then the core's copy was removed.
- **What the core keeps**: the simple check; `CapacityMethod::Code` (any
  design code: a plugin's method, `Model::capacity_plugin`) instead of
  `Asce10`; the joints' data merged (`member_ends::end_bolts`,
  `onto_leg`) and the bolt tools' force basis without an analysis
  (`member_ends::bolt_shear_per_bolt`: a bolt's shear capacity as ASCE
  10-97 4.3.2 gives it, 0.62 f_ub on the root area, whatever the code —
  kept so that the distances asked of a plugin stay what they were;
  listed for the owner); a model of a design code solved and checked
  without its plugin (tests, a library caller) reports every member not
  checked and caps its tension-only members by their Euler load only — the
  runners (OHL-Structure, `ohl structures fe`, the line, the validation)
  find the plugin first, as since round 1. In the line, a structure whose
  code's plugin is not found is refused (its check, named) and, at levels
  3 and 4, taken rigid with that reason — not solved as flexible with
  another cap (`Analyses::plugin_error_of`).
- **Old files unchanged**: no `capacity`, or `capacity = "asce10-97"`, is
  the plugin's method (an alias, written back as it was: none stays
  none); nothing rewritten, no version raised. ("none" read as *no name
  given*: a file saying `capacity = "none"` is still refused — a literal
  "none" could be meant as *no check*.)
- **Settings reach the joints and Member details**: an additive interface
  `joint-check-full` (`joint-check`'s records with the parameter file's
  text), called before `joint-check`; OHL-Structure passes the structure's
  folder to Member details, the plate checks and the bolt tools
  (`member_capacity_in`, `plate_plans_in`, `bolt_rules_in`), so
  `Plugins/<plugin>.toml` is read there as a run reads it. Round 1's "NOT
  ON THE SAFE SIDE where the file's factors are larger" is gone with its
  cause (test: a γ_M2 of 1.5 raises a plate part's usage by 1.5/1.25 and
  lowers Member details' tension). The bolt tools' minimum distances get

  out every profile's properties again for every member of a call (9.9 s

## 2026-11-17

**Calculation level 4 faster, no digit changed** (owner: *"go ahead with
the level 4 speed-up"*, with the standing rule *quality before speed*:
speed work may only coarsen the display, never computed precision;
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[performance](performance.md#calculation-level-4-how-it-is-made-fast-2026-11-17)).

- **Proof of no change**: every step compared bit for bit
  (`format!("{:?}")` of the results, durations left out) with the
  solver before it — the example line's level-4 structure loads (five
  load cases) and a real line's five-case structure loads (read-only,
  local) — and pinned by tests: the skyline kernels against the textbook
  loops (`kernels_are_the_textbook_loops_bit_for_bit`: 400 profiles,
  definite, indefinite, singular, signed zeros), a full model's solves
  with and without its memo (`the_memo_changes_no_digit`), the interface
  matrix from the columns a block reaches against the whole width
  (`the_block_product_is_the_whole_one`).
- **The skyline solver** (`ohl_structures_fe::skyline`): each sum formed as
  the textbook loop forms it (the same terms, the same order, the same
  start; Rust does no fast-math), eight independent ones side by side in
  the vector units — the rows of eight columns in the factorisation (their
  factors kept interleaved row by row), eight right-hand sides of a
  condensation's unit loads, y_j's own sum of the product in a register;
  the held-to-ground check of a condensation reads only the rows of K·u
  it needs (the whole product per column before).
- **What a structure's solves have in common** (`ohl_structures_fe::solve::Memo`,
  kept in each `FullModel`): a first iteration that failed before the
  joints were held (a mechanism, or unstable) — keyed by what its matrix
  is made of (the members left out, their forces, P-Delta), never by the
  loads — is not factorised again; the first-order factors that the
  P-Delta solve's first iteration takes again (the same matrix when no
  member carries a force yet) are reused when the matrix assembled is
  the same bit for bit, kept only within one solve (a few MB a tower).
  `FullModel`'s fields are read through methods since, so its memo stays
  its own.
- **The passes' order**: the structures of a pass are started the longest
  first (their last solve's time), so none is left alone at the end; each
  answer its own, back in their order.
- **The interface Newton step**: each structure's flexibility multiplies
  only the columns of the wires' stiffness that reach its points (the
  others give zero, which adds nothing); the elimination runs down
  contiguous columns.
- **Not built (approximations, for the owner)**: see the performance page
  — the tangent only when the Newton step needs it, P-Delta started from
  the last pass's state, the first-order check of a warm-started
  active set skipped, the last P-Delta factorisation as the tangent, a
  frozen tangent across passes; and, exact but costing memory, the
  first-order factors kept across passes.

**Stiff jumpers along the falling wind, their second shape in still air,
those swapping between the band's pressures; a spacer section that did
not converge** (owner, on the open questions of the jumper review: *"Go
ahead with recommendations"*; built, in active development, not approved
yet; [theory](../theory/jumpers.md#as-the-wind-falls-again)).

- **The falling wind** (`jumper::WindPath::falling_from`,
  `JumperShape::falling`): in the clearance runs (danger trees, safety
  volumes, `ohl analysis`, the clearance windows, `ohl zones`) a stiff
  jumper solved below its case's pressure (a band level, a wind step,
  still air from each side) is also solved as the wind falls from the
  case's pressure: its rising path walked on to the case's pressure, and
  where that jumped walked back down; where it ran without a jump the
  falling shape is the rising one (a stable branch followed back —
  marked an assumption in the theory). The band and the positions take
  both shapes; still air reached falling from each side is a band level
  (a state or job of its own, `fallen_only`, sharing the still air's line
  solve: without wind the side and direction are out of the solve's key).
  The NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE note for a jumper that snapped goes where every
  solve below the snap held its falling wind (said instead: checked in
  both shapes); it stays where not (a failed falling path, no band or
  wind steps). Cost (measured, real line, 526 jumpers): a band's jumpers
  about 1.9 times as long (a 500 Pa case: a side's 4.1 s → 7.8 s, a busy
  computer); the whole band with the swaps' solves below: a 300 Pa case
  4.7 s → 18.0 s, a 500 Pa case 364 s → 388 s (a quiet computer); the
  snapped jumpers of the real line's 300 and 500 Pa cases
  are now held (said as checked in both shapes).
- **Two still-air shapes** (`WindPath::still_shapes`,
  `JumperShape::other_still`): the still air of every clearance run solves
  each stiff jumper also from its still-air shape mirrored about the
  vertical plane through its ends; a second stable shape (more than
  0.05 m away) is said with its distance — only the shape found from the
  hinged catenary (as hung, as installed) is checked; NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE
  unless the still air after a wind from a side is that shape (then
  checked with the band). Real line, 10 °C: 6 of 526 jumpers (1.2–5.5 m
  apart).
- **Swaps between the band's pressures** (`ohl_clearance::jumper_swaps`):
  a jump on a jumper's path (`JumperShape::jumps`; on the clearance runs'
  paths a step taken thanks to the allowance for its predicted move walked
  again without it), or its shapes
  at two neighbouring solved pressures of a side not leading to each other
  (`cross_swaps`, `jumper::solve_jumper_from`) — the real line's case: each
  path smooth, its ends held at the pressure solved, but to the one shape
  at 100, 110, 140 Pa and to the other at 120, 130 Pa: that jumper alone
  solved every 10 Pa over that interval (with the sections at its
  structures), its band holding those shapes; said in the results.
  Measured (10 Pa steps against the band of the default spacing): the
  jumpers' worst excess 0.62 m → 0.13 m at 300 Pa, 0.19 m → 0.089 m at
  500 Pa (56 and 94 more solves of the sections at the swapping jumpers'
  structures).
- **The section that did not converge** (a real line: the section and the
  one its spacer joins, solved at every 10 Pa of each of its 55 windy
  cases from both sides, failed at 194 of them — always from one side,
  between 160 and 230 Pa by temperature and ice, in 39 cases; band levels
  among them: 170 Pa at 500 Pa, 160 Pa at 650 Pa, 190 Pa at 1300 Pa, 200
  Pa at 1000 Pa iced): a spacer
  of 3 m given length between two phases about 1.1 m apart, solved by the
  spacers' passes; in the second pass the section holding the spacer (a
  strut: it takes compression) to the other section's moved point did not
  converge — Newton stalled at 617 N unbalanced where no step lowered it
  (the strut's compression makes the tangent indefinite), the load steps
  too, and the dynamic relaxation was tried for chained strings only. A
  solver problem: **the relaxation now also for models with struts**
  (`ohl-wirefe`, `Model::solve_by_relaxation`; models Newton solves never
  get there: bit for bit as before). With it none of the 194 fails, and no
  section of the real line fails at the band's pressures (and full
  pressures) of any of its windy cases.
- **A test changed** (`ohl-electrical`, `a_jumper_carries_its_phase_current`):
  its jumper's clamps face each other 0.4 m apart; since 2026-11-16 the
  stiff jumper takes its stable shape there — a loop crossing itself
  below the clamps (energy 2.2 kJ) instead of an S-shape of 4.7 kN that
  was a saddle (6.4 kJ) — whose circulating current lowers the field 2 m
  below it by 7 %. The test is about the current a jumper carries: its
  jumper is now a plain wire (EI 0), the U the comparison means.

keeps as the wind rises from still air** (owner: *"Yes investigate the

  between 140 and 170 Pa): each a loop held at two clamps on V strings,
  with **two stable shapes** at every pressure up to 1500 Pa (the loop to
  either side). Solved from the hinged catenary at each pressure, the
  shape found depended on that start: between 116 and 148 Pa it changed
  from one to the other — through **saddles of the energy** (unstable
  equilibria Newton converged to, 1.4–2.8 kN against 0.2–0.5 kN in the
  stable shapes) and a third stable shape. A solver problem (saddles; a

  stable shapes; one of them ends at about 1480 Pa from one side, where
  the jumper snaps over).

  equilibrium whose energy curves down in a direction the constraints
  allow is left along it, down the energy, to a stable shape. Two tests

  under an I-string, and under a V: both buckle sideways); corrected.

  solved in still air, then at every 100 Pa up to the case's pressure,

  shape, not held below that pressure. Every jumper's results can change

  in the last digits.

  jumpers' worst excess over their bands 0.62 m at 300 Pa (one jumper
  with two shapes 0.2 m apart, open) and 0.19 m at 500 Pa, against
