  already present at stringing left out" in the level-2 results.
- **Not taken** (said): level 3 (each case its own deflection), the
  **structure loads** and the loads sent to OHL-Structure (kept as drawn,
  rigid: on the safe side — the coordinator's choice, for the owner to
  confirm), internal clearances (the body is not deflected in the check).
- **LiDAR**: the As-built wires window compares with the reference state
  by default when it is current (coordinator's default; the owner may
  change it), a **Structures** switch for as drawn; `ohl lidar
  fit-wires --structure-reference ignore` likewise.
- **Command line**: `--structure-reference use|ignore` (default use) on
  every command reading a line; `ohl line --solve-reference CASE
  [--save-reference FILE]`.

**Structure flexibility, phase 5: the line's calculation level, the
checks taking it** (owner: "Go ahead with the next steps"; built, in
active development, not approved yet;
[user guide](../user-guide/calculation-level.md),
[theory](../theory/structure-flexibility.md#checks-at-level-3)).

- **The setting**: Line › Criteria › Calculation options › *Structures in
  the wire solve* — rigid (default, calculation level 2), linear
  stiffness (level 3), full structures (level 4). The line file's
  `solver.structures` (**version 21**, written only when not rigid; an
  older file reads rigid), OHL XML `<solver structures>`, the session's
  solver command (one logged, undoable command), the app's revision
  (every result out of date when it changes). **Full structures are not
  built yet**: the choice is in the format (so phase 6 needs no new
  version) and shown greyed in the window, not offered; a file that asks
  for it is read, and every run taking the level refuses it with why
  (`--structures-as full` too). Beside each choice the window shows the
  last run at that level on this computer (its time, the setup's, how
  many times its rigid solves, the largest change against rigid and the
  largest move), else an estimate from the last rigid run; its (?) lists
  the structures that stay rigid and why (from the files, and from the
  last level-3 run).
- **The command line**: `--structures-as rigid|linear` overrides the
  line's choice for one run (every command reading a line through the
  common model arguments, and `ohl line`); `ohl line --calculation-level
  2|3` kept as the same by number (`--structures` was taken: the
  structure type folder). `ohl line` at level 3 prints the level-3 solve
  of each weather case after the rigid tables (which stay rigid, said).
- **The checks taking it**: the structure loads and usage (phase 4), the
  **wire tensions** and the **string checks** (both in the window and
  `ohl tensions` / `ohl strings`), and the **loads sent to
  OHL-Structure** (each case from the rigid and the level-3 solve, the
  line-values file's `levels`; OHL-Structure says "Line forces from a
  level 3 solve"). The weather-case checks set the structures up once
  per run with each section by its own method (a rule asking another
  method than a section's is solved rigid, said) and each structure's own
  wind and ice of the weather case on its own; **never less safe than
  rigid**: both solves checked, per row the worse kept with both values.
  The string swing at level 3 is measured from the moved top, the
  structure's tilt left out (said).
- **The Structure loads window's switch follows the line's choice**;
  ticked or unticked there it sets that window's runs (and the loads sent
  to OHL-Structure) only, kept with the project's setup, its hover saying
  the line's choice; ticked back, it follows the line again. A setup kept
  before (ticked) still reads as ticked.
- **Not yet taking the level** (rigid, said where cheap — "calculation
  level 2 (structures rigid): this check does not take the line's level
  yet"): the clearances (vertical, radial, wire clearances, vegetation,
  safety volumes, LiDAR; their adoption waits for the swing-arc band work
  on the clearance positions), galloping, ice shedding, lightning, the
  distance between conductors; internal clearances stay rigid until the
  structure body is drawn deflected. The views, tables, sagging tables and
  drawings are the rigid solve's.

**The swing band takes intermediate solved pressures (levels); cases
differing by their pressure alone share their solves; a span the band
does not hold is checked at its steps** (owner: *"try the correction
with a bit more cases for the band and for the calculations going
through multiple windy cases, we should find a way to simplify the
number of computation needed based on the different wind cases. For
example if you have 500/600 and 800 only computing 800 should suffice to
have the result of the others"*, and on directions: *"if we have wind
along the line, the conductors might sway differently and necessitate a
new solve"*). Built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/clearances.md#wind-positions).

- **Why: the band was not on the safe side.** Measured on a real line of
  930 spans with 10 Pa steps from both sides, the wire at intermediate
  pressures lay outside the band of still air and the two blowouts by up
  to 0.23 m at 500 Pa across the line, 0.49 m at 1000 Pa, 0.69 m at
  1300 Pa, 0.82 m at 30° (1450 Pa); the default margin of 0.15 m held
  only up to about 390 Pa. The theory's label "Conservative" for the
  band (and the statement below, in the entry "Both wind sides always
  drawn…", that "the band stays conservative for a wind at an angle")
  rested on the example lines alone (0.091 m) — **wrong on a real
  line**; corrected in the theory, which now gives the real-line
  amounts.
- **The levels.** The band also holds the wire solved at n intermediate
  pressures from each side, k·P/(n + 1) rounded to a whole 10 Pa, and at
  least one every 200 Pa (`positions::band_levels`), n = 4 by default
  (`BAND_LEVELS`; the
  **band levels** field beside the band margin in the clearance windows,
  the vegetation panel and the safety volumes; `[wind] band_levels`;
  `--band-levels` of `ohl zones`, `ohl safety-volume`, `ohl analysis`;
  saved runs record it, older ones read as 0). With the wind steps, every
  step is a level. Measured on the real line with 10 Pa steps: at most 0.063 m outside the
  band with the default levels (across the line up to 1300 Pa, 30° and
  60° at 1000 Pa, along the line, ice and wind), 0.69 m without; the
  excess grows with the spacing of the solved pressures (about 0.3 mm
  per pascal), hence at least one level every 200 Pa; example lines
  0.009 m (0.091 m without). Cost: 2n more solves
  per windy case (8 by default; 3 before), the band's checks unchanged.
  Without levels (0): the results say NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE.
- **Where the band does not apply.** A wind along an inclined span lifts
  the wire towards and through the line between its clamps (on the real
  line at 1450 Pa from ahead; 8.7 m outside the band). A span whose
  solved positions or levels lie more than 0.1 m above their own chord,
  or are pulled towards it to less than half of still air's sag (along
  the line at 1000 Pa a steep span pulled so lay 0.30 m outside its band
  with any number of levels), or that has no band, is said; the danger trees, safety volumes and
  `ohl analysis` also check it at its 10 Pa steps from both sides (solved
  for that case only); the clearance windows and `ohl zones` say NOT ON
  THE SAFE SIDE for it unless the steps are ticked.
- **Shared solves.** Every run solves each distinct case once
  (`positions::solve_key`: the case without its name, description and
  tags, and across the line without its direction, which the solve does
  not read there): cases differing by their pressure alone
  (`family_key`) share their solves at the same pressures — the steps
  of the 800 Pa case are the 500 and 600 Pa cases' steps and blowouts —
  bit for bit what solving each alone gives (tested), and the two copies
  of one wind across the line (from 90° and from 270°) share every blown
  solve. A wind from another direction (along the line, at an angle) is
  its own family, never derived from another (owner, same day). On the
  real line's 76 windy cases stepped by 10 Pa with the band: 11,266
  solves asked, 3,541 made (−69 %); its 150 windy cases (each wind from
  90° and 270°): 22,340 asked, 3,557 made (−84 %); one family (10 °C,
  200–650 Pa) 118 s together against 200 s one at a time (a shared
  computer), the positions bit for bit the same. A band is still made
  about each span's axis as the run's first solve gives it (as before).
- **Changed results.** With the swing arc on, every band is at least as
  wide as before (more positions held): results can only get worse; a
  span the band does not hold gets its steps (more positions). Without
  the arc, nothing changes (the shared solves are the same solves).
- **Also:** the structure condensation's note "offset … taken as the
  joint's translation only" is no longer said for offsets of 1 cm or less
  (imported positions rounded to whole centimetres; nothing computed
  changes).

**A joint is an attach joint only while attachment points are on it;
OHL-Design's Structure types page asks onto the joint or an offset**
(owner: *"if no attach points are left on the joint then no it shouldn't
be attach anymore"* and, for the question, *"also in OHL design"*).
Built, in active development, not approved yet.

- **The joint left.** Before, a point moved off a joint wrote
  `kind = "attach"` on the joint it left (so a point could be moved
  back), and an explicit `attach` stayed after unlinking or deleting its
  last point. Now, in the same edit (one undo step brings back both),
  the joint whose last point leaves goes back to its plain kind — its
  `kind = "attach"` and an `attachment` naming a point no longer there
  taken off, worked out again as none, or support with a `support`
  (`ohl_structure_edit::links::release_joints`). Every path that takes a
  point off a joint goes through it: OHL-Structure's list, Link and
  Move attachment point (`link_point` / `relink_point`), Unlink,
  Delete (`Removal::left`), a point written before 2026-10-21 moved
  off the joint at its place, a generator putting a point on a tip;
  OHL-Design's Move attachment point on the type and its Structure types
  page (the same edits); the line's links in OHL-Structure's run of a
  placed structure (`with_placed_links`, the file itself unchanged). The
  joint a point arrives at must already be an attach joint, as before.
  A point and a joint stay separate objects (`links::joint_of` finds a
  point's joint among the `[[node]]`s only). *This structure only* in
  OHL-Design changes no structure file: the type's joints keep their
  kinds there (left as it is). Files written before with an attach joint
  carrying no point read the same.
- **The question on the Structure types page.** Its Link tool and the
  joint chosen in its Attachment points table linked a point that was
  not on the joint at an offset without asking. Now they ask as
  everywhere else (`type_workspace::LinkAsk`): onto the joint (the
  default) or its position kept; within 1 mm onto it without asking.
  The question's two choices and its sentence are one shared copy for
  both applications (`ohl_ui::link_question`), used by OHL-Structure's
  window, OHL-Design's Link / Move attachment point window and the
  Structure types page. A point dropped onto a joint by dragging still
  goes onto it (the drop is the answer).
- **A point deleted takes its allowable load.** Deleting a point that
  had an allowable load (`[[capacity.attachment]] point = …`) left the
  entry behind, naming a point no longer there, and the structure file
  no longer read (found by the tests above). The entry now goes with
  the point, listed in the Delete confirmation (`Removal::capacities`).

**Both wind sides always drawn; the danger trees, safety volumes and
unequal wind check a wind at an angle with its mirror** (owner: *"Display
weather case should indeed not have 'both, left or right' for wind. We
should just display both sides at once."* and *"Please also check how
this impacts the wind arc in the clearances and danger tree... maybe it
needs a slight rework."*). Built, in active development:

- **The display.** View › Display weather cases has no wind choice any
  more (`WindDisplay` removed). Every case with wind is drawn as it is —
  without a direction from the right (90°), with its own direction as
  given — and mirrored about the line (θ → 360° − θ; across: the other
  side). Once only when the mirror is the same wind (along the line, 0°
  or 180°) or when another case drawn with it, wherever it is drawn, is
  its mirror (the two directed copies of one source wind, from 90° and
  from 270°, shown together: each drawn once; where a section shows only
  one, it is drawn with its mirror). The mirror is solved only when it
  is drawn; a mirror solved before and no longer needed is hidden, not
  thrown away. The checks of the case shown (fields, distance between
  conductors, galloping, buildings) take the case as it is only — the
  same as before for the default; under the old "from the left" choice
  they took a case without a direction from the left, now always from the
  right. The choice remembered in a user's view (`right`, `left`, `both`)
  is read and ignored, not written. Cost: a displayed case with wind takes
  two solves (it and its mirror) where the default took one.
- **What the arcs did** (the investigation). None of the arcs depended
  on the display's choice: the clearance windows, `ohl zones` and the wire
  to wire swing take the sides of their own `[wind] sides`, and the
  danger trees, grow-in, safety volumes and `ohl analysis` always both.
  The swing arc itself (`SwingArc`) is built from the solved blowouts
  whatever their wind and takes the smallest to the largest angle and
  radius, so it is right for any direction once the blowouts are. The
  vertical and radial clearance windows already took a wind at an angle
  and its mirror (2026-11-15). **Wrong:** the positions of the danger
  trees, grow-in, safety volumes, `ohl analysis` and the unequal-wind
  distance between conductors set only the side (`wind_from`) for each
  blowout, which a wind at an angle does not read — so for a case with
  its own direction at an angle both "sides" were the case as it is and
  its mirror was **never checked** (not on the safe side against the
  views, which drew it). Now (`ohl_clearance::positions::from_side`): from
  the right the wind from θ when it comes from the right half (0°–180°),
  else its mirror; from the left the other — each blowout blowing the
  wires to the side named, said with its angle ("left (from 30°)"). A
  wind along the line (0°, 180°) is one blowout (its arc from still air to
  it); the clearance windows' positions take it once too (before: the same
  position twice). The wire to wire swing's labels say a wind at an angle
  by its angle (before "from the left/right").
- **Changed results.** Cases without a direction and cases with their own
  direction across the line: identical, bit for bit (the tests of before
  pass unchanged). Cases with their own direction at an angle (new since
  2026-11-15): the danger trees, safety volumes, `ohl analysis` and the
  unequal wind now also check the mirror — results can only get worse
  (more positions); along the line the duplicate position is gone (the
  same lowest result, counted once).
- **The band at an angle, measured:** both windy example cases from 30°,
  60° and 0° against their 10 Pa steps from both sides: the steps lie up
  to 0.082 m outside the band without its margin (across: 0.091 m), held
  by the default margin of 0.15 m — the band stays conservative for a
  wind at an angle on the example line (**corrected the same day**: not
  on a real line, across the line nor at an angle — see the entry on the
  swing band's levels above) ([Wind on the
  line](../theory/wind.md#clearances-and-the-views)). A case with its own
  direction checks that wind and its mirror only, not the across
  envelope (said there as an assumption).
- **The project lines shown next to the line** (owner, same day:
  "yes"): both sides too, by the same rule and code
  (`Model::want_others` asks `Model::mirror_wanted` for each case, the
  other line's `Solved::mirror` and `mirror_hidden` as the line's): the
  mirror solved in the background only while drawn, from the line worked
  on's mirror with only the sections that differ solved again (waiting
  for it as the case waits for the line's case), hidden when no longer
  wanted (`mirrors_changed`); the plan draws their `Solved::drawn` as the
  3D view did already. Cost: one more such solve per windy case and line
  shown. The lines on the ground take the mirror they hold instead of
  solving it again. Nothing in the files changes. The
  drawings' other versions (Sheets) draw a project line's both sides
  too, as the line itself (`Solved::with_mirror` when not yet solved).

**Structure flexibility, phase 4: calculation level 3 in the structure
loads** (owner: "Yes"; built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/structure-flexibility.md#structure-loads-at-level-3)).
The Structure loads window's **Structures flexible (level 3)** (kept with
the project's setup, off by default) and `ohl line … --load-cases …
--calculation-level 3` compute the structure loads and usage with the
line solved by the interface loop: the structures set up once per run
(the stringing state solved with every section by finite elements in its
initial condition, the structures condensed there over the cores, a
progress stage of its own), each structure's **own wind and ice of the
case in its deflection** (the check's member wind, ice and snow, or the
pole's shaft wind and ice, unfactored, on the same tangent), a **broken
wire as a whole-line solve** (with `"every"`, one per span), at
unfactored loads with the case's factors on the resulting forces. As the
owner decided, **never below rigid**: each load at a point is per
component the larger of the rigid and the flexible solve's; the model and
pole checks take both solves each on its own and keep the worse (the
envelope of components is no upper bound of a member force), the member
checks once per structure and case after the loop. A case whose loop
does not converge keeps the rigid loads, said. Every level-3 case says
what it assumed, the structures taken rigid and why, the passes, the time
and the largest move. OHL-Structure keeps getting the rigid loads until
the line's own level setting (phase 5); the line-values file can carry
each case's level (**version 10**, `levels`, written only when a case is
not rigid). Measured on the example line: the lattice towers' points move
up to 19 mm leeward in high wind, the pole's 0.3 m, the transverse loads
change by 0.1 % (1.4 % at the pole); with a broken conductor the other
circuit's point on the next tower takes up to 40 % more longitudinal
load than rigid gives it (kept); vertical loads change by at most
0.05 %; the level-3 solve governs a member check by less than 0.01 %.

**Every wire solve about a local origin** (owner: "fix the rounding";
built, in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/wirefe.md#newtonraphson)). The wire solver
(`ohl_wirefe::Model::solve`, and the wires' stiffness at their supports)
takes whole kilometres off a model whose first node is more than 10 km
from the origin and adds them back to its results — so every line solve
does, rigid included (each section, the shared assemblies, the broken
wires, the jumpers, the posts, the final stringing, the coupled solve of
calculation level 3, whose own translation of the line is gone: pass 0
and the moved passes now round alike). Exact for the given points (the
fixed nodes come back bit for bit). **Changed results** on lines in
projected coordinates (a line near the origin is not moved: the
examples change only within the solver's tolerance, 10⁻⁴ N and 10⁻⁷ m,
from the stretch passes below): before, a position was resolved to only about 5·10⁻¹⁰ m and
the solver's floating-point floor grew with the coordinates, so a
section with a stiff string stopped up to about 100 N out of balance.
On a real line (99 weather cases, 554 sections) the tensions changed by
up to 293 N (6 % in a short span; 99 % of the spans within 13 N), the
clamps by up to 9 mm, the sags by up to 6 cm; the new results agree with
the same line moved near the origin to 0.4 N and 0.01 mm. The price:
about a third more Newton iterations on such lines (the line solve
about 15 % longer on that line). Two changes keep the time and the
robustness: a load step short of the whole loads (the solver's fallback)
is solved to 10⁻³ of the loads (it is only the next step's start: one
section of the real line failed one more weather case without it), and
a pass on the stretches (ice and wind per stretched metre) whose
stretches will still change is solved to a share of that change, the
pass returned to the full tolerance.

## 2026-11-15

**A weather case's own wind direction is kept and never turned by the
display** (owner's report: "the duplicate detection doesnt recognise the
angle for the winds and offers to merge 2 winds coming from different
directions"). Cause: a weather case written with `wind_direction` 90 /
270 ("right" / "left") was read as the across rule with its side and
**no** direction; in the desktop application every case without a
direction takes the side View › Display weather cases shows, so the two
copies of one source wind (*— from the right (90°)*, *— from the left
(270°)*) became the same case: Merge duplicate weather cases offered
them, and — worse — the left copy was solved, checked and handed to the
structure loads from the display's side, not from the left. Now: the
direction given is kept in memory (its side in `wind_from`, the across
rule from it bit for bit); a case with its own direction (across or at an
angle) is never turned by the display — as it is, its mirror drawn with
*both* — and the display's choice applies to the cases without a
direction exactly as before (owner's rule: "the current cases need to be
identical"; `wind_direction_identical` unchanged). `same_physics`: 90°
and 270° never the same; a case without a direction and one with its own
direction across from the same side not the same either (one follows the
display, the other does not); the merge window lists the cases only the
direction keeps apart, with why. The clearance positions: both sides =
the direction and its mirror, one side = the direction alone (never
turned). **Changed for existing projects:** nothing for cases without a
direction. A case with an angle under the display's left (until today
"mirrored") is now shown as it is, not mirrored — its mirror is drawn
with *both*, and the clearance checks' both sides take it (before, they
took the same angle twice). The Weather cases table now shows a 90° /
270° case's direction (before: empty). Load cases naming such a case:
their own `wind_from` / `wind_direction` still win, as before. Built, not
approved yet.

**Attachment points moved from joint to joint; the two applications tell
each other** (owner: *"on OHL-Structure, the attachment points on point
and strings can not be moved from a joint to another in the list where
it should and i would like to have a tool to move attachment points
where i can click on a joint with an attachment point and move it to
another. also a joint can have multiple attachment points on it and
moving one would require to choose one from the listed attachment points
on the joint. in OHL design in addition to the link attachment point
tool when we add a 3d structure where there was none before, a move
attachment point should also be available. 2 two apps should communicate
with each other when attachment points are linked to a joint or
moved."*; then *"in the table when adding a new attachment point in
OHL-Structure it creates its own joint where it should be created as an
attachment point by itself then linked."* and *"if the attachment point
is not exactly on the joint, linking it should ask if we want to move it
on the joint or create an offset."*; and the rules: an attachment point
and a joint are separate objects even of the same name; a string never
hangs from a joint; an attachment point must be linked to a joint to
load the 3D structure — an unlinked one belongs to the level-1
description, allowed with a warning; a linked point's offset gives the
moment at the joint as before. Built, in active development, not
approved yet.)

- **OHL-Structure, the list**: a point's joint is chosen in the Points &
  strings list (the attach joints, a search, or an id typed); the point
  moves there, its strings follow; one edit, one undo step.
- **OHL-Structure, Move attachment point** (a new tool): a joint
  carrying points clicked (several: a chooser lists them with the
  strings and sets hanging from each), then the target joint; Escape
  cancels at any step; one undo step.
- **The question** (every link: the list, both OHL-Structure tools,
  OHL-Design's Link and Move attachment point): a point farther than
  **1 mm** from the joint (`ohl_structures::ON_JOINT`) asks *Move the
  point onto the joint* (the default, so a moved point lands on its new
  joint with no offset) or *Keep its position* (an offset); within 1 mm
  it goes onto the joint without asking. Part of the same edit.
- **A point standing alone**: `[[point]] unlinked = true` with its
  `point` (structure file **version 17**, `UNLINKED_POINT_VERSION`,
  written only when used). Add a point and Unlink write it; it never
  takes the joint at its position nor a joint of its own; linking
  removes it. Files written before read the same (a free point on the
  joint at its place, said in the Advice; a stick figure's point its own
  place) — but another point's own place is no joint to link to any
  more.
- **Unlinked points on a 3D structure** (safe side): allowed; their
  strings' loads are left out of the 3D check (OHL-Structure's results,
  OHL-Design's structure check) with *NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: attachment
  point X linked to no joint: the strings hanging from it are not
  attached to the 3D structure* naming them (`unlinked_words`), and in
  OHL-Structure's Advice. Before, OHL-Design refused the whole check of
  a structure with an unlinked point; the owner's rule makes it a
  warning. A linked point's offset moment is unchanged.
- **Points and joints apart**: a string whose top names a joint is
  refused with the fix; the separate model's fallback from a joint id to
  the point's own node (`Model::linked_load`) now says so in its note.
- **OHL-Design, Move attachment point** (a new tool beside Link
  attachment point): a point of a structure with a 3D type (a chooser
  when several share its place), then a joint of its type; **this
  structure only** (the default: the line's relink, `link_point`, one
  command, one undo) or **the type** (its `.ohls` edited with
  `ohl_structure_edit::links::relink_point`, saved into the project and
  read again: every structure of the type follows; not an Edit › Undo
  step — said in the window; refused while the type is open in
  OHL-Structure).
- **The two applications** (no network, the files they share): OHL-Design
  writes a placed structure's own links (where they differ from the
  type) into its line-values file — **version 9**, `links` — written
  again when the line changes; OHL-Structure says what changed (*T2:
  point A1 linked to joint A2 (from OHL-Design)*), marks the point
  **line differs** and solves the placed structure with the line's link over
  the type's, refusing the run when it cannot be applied (never leaving
  the loads on the old joint). OHL-Structure's change reaches OHL-Design
  when the type is saved there (the existing file watch); OHL-Design's
  status says *T2, T4: point A11 linked to joint A1 (from
  OHL-Structure)*.

**Structure flexibility, phase 3: the interface loop and calculation
level 3** (owner: "go ahead with phase 3 of the flexibility plan"; built,
in active development, not approved yet;
[theory](../theory/structure-flexibility.md#the-interface-loop)). As the
owner's answers to the plan decided: the wires and the structures meet
only at the attachment points, the whole line coupled at once; pass 0 is
the rigid solve (bit for bit); the structures answer u = C (F − F_ref),
C condensed at the stringing state (the tangent there), three
translations per point with every coupling between a structure's
points, displacements from the structures as strung, F_ref the wires'
forces in still air at each section's stringing temperature; a Newton
step in the flexibility form (I + C K_w) Δu = −r, a halved step when the
mismatch grows; converged at 0.1 mm and 1 N (or 10⁻⁶ of the force) at
every point; exit clauses 20 passes, a 10-minute guard per case, the
cancel token, each section's budget; **a case that does not converge
fails** with its worst point, direction and trend — never the last pass
returned — the rigid results kept, said rigid. Structures without a
model, or refused, rigid and listed with why; ruling-span sections
rigid; at unfactored loads. **No check takes it yet**: an internal entry
point (`ohl_loads::solve_line_flexible`) and, for testing, `ohl line …
--calculation-level 3`, which prints the displacements and the change
against rigid after the rigid results and says that every check, the
structure checks included, still uses the rigid solve (the larger of
rigid and flexible, the owner's rule for the structure checks, comes
with phase 4, as do the structures' own wind and ice in their
deflection — until then **not on the safe side** for leeward clearances,
said). Hand cases: a span on a spring and on a pole against the elastic
catenary in closed form (to 10⁻¹³), two spans on a flexible string top
with one span iced against the same wire model solved at once with the
spring as long bars (0.001 N), the stringing state (u = 0 exactly), the
rigid limit, the exit clauses, the example line. Measured on them: the
hot-case sag of rigid larger (conservative, slightly), the longitudinal
load next to an unbalance lower when flexible.

**The Load cases library shows the values a case does not give, and
"as the wires" says the wires' actual direction** (owner: "on the load
case library, the default should show what the value is even if greyed
out for example the ice and snow on the structure or the wind factor";
and "the default cases for the wind ahead and back said 'as for the
wires right' which isn't accurate anymore if we have the wind on an
angle defined in the weather case. this should be removed"). Built, in
active development, not approved yet:

- Where a case gives no value (an unticked *own …* box, a *default*
  choice, a factor at 1) the form shows the value that applies, greyed,
  with its source: the bodies' pressure and factor
  (`LoadCase::structure_wind`), the ice on the structures — per
  structure for the local ice, the thickness after the factor for the
  wires' ice and a thickness (`LoadCase::structure_ice_at`,
  `LoadCase::takes_local_ice`) —, its density (`LoadCase::ice_density`,
  glaze ice for the wires' ice as `structure_ice_at` takes it), the snow's
  μ C_e C_T and each structure's snow load
  (`StructureOptions::snow_factor`, `LoadCase::structure_snow_at`), the
  factors at 1 and the condition *as strung*. Each value comes from the
  function the loads use — no copy of a rule in the form. A greyed field
  is not editable; ticking *own …* starts from the value shown.
- The structures' wind direction *as the wires* names the direction the
  wires take in the case: the case's `wind_direction`, else the weather
  case's at an angle, else across from the side (the bodies' default of
  `LoadCase::structure_wind`): *as the wires: from ahead (0°)* for the
  default case with the wind from ahead. Before, the form showed the side
  only (`wind_from`), "from the right" for the cases along the line.
  The same in the case notes of the structure loads (a `wind_from` given
  says the direction taken, and that it has no effect beside the case's
  own `wind_direction`) and in the doc comments of `ohl-loads`.

**The Structure loads window: Run to compute, the library followed, the
groups run** (owner reports: "i added the default structure loads in the
library and it does not appear in the compute structure loads"; "when
the load cases in the library are edited and saved, the compute load
case doesn't update the load case library"; "if i restart the project
it's good"; "the compute structure loads starts immediately when the
window is opened. i would like to have to click on run to start it";
"the load cases on the structure should respect the groups defined in
the load case per group if there are some … it should have a list of
groups that are to be run and then the loadcases for the structures not
in these groups under"; "put the structures outside of the alignment by
default out of the calculations and all at the bottom of the list";
"i would like to have the structures be computed in parallel with a
progressbar indicating where we are at. first solve the lines then the
structures … the code on the structure side should be checked only once
at the end and not through every step of the calculations"). Built, in
active development, not approved yet:

1. **The cause**: the window kept the load case library's case names
   read the first time it was drawn, read again only when the library's
   *file path* changed — a save in the library page writes the same
   file, so the list (and the ticks) stayed as they were until the
   project was opened again. Further, a run failed whole when one case
   could not be computed (the default load cases name the default
   weather cases, which a project may lack): one error, no case shown.
   Now the window reads the library again whenever the libraries'
   revision (counted up by every library save) or the file's time
   changes; each case is listed with its state (computed on Run, not
   computable — its weather case missing —, taken by no structure); a
   case that fails fails only itself, said with why and the structures
   not checked in it (never a pass in the governing usage).
2. **Run computes; opening does not.** Checks › Compute structure loads
   only opens the window; the results of an earlier run stay, marked out
   of date when the line or a library changed.
3. **The setup follows the groups**: *3 Structure groups* — each group
   run or not (ticked by default), its structures and cases, the cases'
   own lists shown; *4 Structures in no group* — the load cases run for
   them (a choice of the window, kept in the project; the line's groups
   unchanged; *Make these a group…* optional); *5 Before Run* — what is
   computed and what is left out, with why. A structure in a group run
   and one not run: the cases of the groups run only (said). Results say
   which groups gave each case. Structures on no alignment are left out
   unless ticked, at the bottom of each list.
4. **Two stages, in parallel, with progress**: the line solved in each
   load case (the cases in parallel), then the structures checked (in
   parallel), the bar saying the stage and where it is; the answer
   identical to one after the other (tested bit for bit); Stop ends it
   between cases or structures. The member checks are made once per
   structure and case on the converged forces (they already were:
   `analyse` checks after `solve`; now tested).
   **Profiled first** (a real line, 8 load cases, 78 structures with
   lattice models of about 1000 joints and 2500 members): the line solves
   took a few seconds; the structures took nearly all the time, and of
   that most went into the member checks, which worked out each
   profile's cross-section properties (outline moments, shear centre,
   warping) again for every member, every solve and every load case.
   They are now worked out once per profile and thread
   (`ohl_structures_fe::check::properties`, found by the whole profile:
   a changed profile is worked out again) — the same numbers. With the
   structures in parallel, the run there went from minutes to well under
   half a minute on a 10-core computer; the factorisations of the
   structures' solves are now most of the rest (their first, unstabilised
   try of a model that needs holding is a further saving left open: it
   must give the same answer).
5. **Add the default cases… with their weather cases**: the load case
   form's Add the default cases… adds, with a tick on by default, the
   default weather cases the new load cases name that the project lacks
   — to the weather case file, at once, as its own change (one undo
   step; the load cases are kept by Save, their own step). Chosen over
   one combined command because the two files are saved by different
   paths (the weather table's write and the library page's Save); the
   two steps undo in order.

**Member wind on inclined members: SIA 261 inclination factors and
force coefficients** (owner: "go ahead with your recommendations"). A
review found the member wind of the structures **not on the safe side**:
the force on a member at an angle θ to the wind was reduced with sin²θ,
where SIA 261:2014 Tableau 74 (p. 112, "Coefficients pour treillis
spatiaux") reduces it with ≈ sin θ for round bars and far less for
sharp-edged profiles (0.88 at 45° against 0.5). The owner decided five
points; built, in active development, not approved yet:

1. **Default inclination factor** k(β), β = 90° − θ the angle between the
   wind and the member's normal (θ in 3D, the force normal to the member in
   the plane of the member and the wind): Tableau 74's sharp-edged factors
   c_red 1.0, 0.98, 0.93, 0.88, 0.8 at β = 0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, 60° for every
   shape that is not round, linear between (at least cos β, the projected
   area: the straight line lies up to 0.3 % below it under 9°); sin θ for
   round bars and tubes, raised to Tableau 74's own ratios c_β/c_β(0) where
   larger (up to 2 %, at 30°).
2. **Below θ = 30°** (β > 60°, no value in the standard): first decided
   as the 30° factor held (0.8, round 0.5); the same day, on the
   recheck, the owner chose instead (again "go ahead with your
   recommendations") to **taper** it with the projected area,
   k(θ) = k(60°) · sin θ / sin 30° — 1.6 sin θ sharp-edged, sin θ round —
   continuous at 30°, 0 along the wind, never below sin θ; a curve given as
   data tapered the same way beyond its last angle. An assumption,
   conservative against the projected-area law. The hold was rejected
   because the force normal to a member nearly along the wind is mostly
   across it: on a reviewed real tower with unsymmetric crossarms it gave a
   resultant of 17 kN across a wind of 220 kN (0.2 kN with the taper), and
   it made a reviewed tension tower's model unstable at a crossarm joint —
   that model stays refused with the taper (the joint, held only in the
   crossarm's face, now takes its chord's standard force: 0.41 of the
   broadside force at about 15° to the wind against 0.07 under sin²θ; it
   moves 0.29 m in a first-order run; solved under sin²θ), a weakness of
   the model to fix there. The note counting held members is gone.
3. **Inclination data per shape** in the cross-section library's `[wind]`
   (`[wind.inclination.<shape>]`: `angle`, `factor`) so that a code plugin
   gives its own curve; the built-in one applies without. The section
   library format goes to version 2, written only when the new keys are
   used. The plugin interface is unchanged: a plugin's `structure-wind`
   returns a library text, which may now carry them.
4. **sin²θ kept as an option** for comparison, off by default: `[wind]
   member_law = "sin2"`, or `ohl structures fe --member-wind-law sin2`;
   with `[analysis] drag = 1` it reproduces the former member wind bit for
   bit (tested); every result under it says *NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE*.
5. **Drag default** (decided by the safe-side rule): a member whose shape
   is known and for which no drag is given anywhere (face drag, shape drag,
   `[analysis] drag`) takes the force coefficient of its shape from SIA
   261:2014 Tableau 71 (p. 109) or, for bars and tubes, Tableau 72 (p. 110)
   instead of 1 — the largest over what the program does not look up (the
   wind's angle to the profile, the slenderness, the Reynolds number), on
   the table's reference width: angles 2.1 on the longer leg, channels and
   I sections 2.05, boxes 2.1, two channels back to back 2.2, polygonal
   tubes 2.1 (an assumption), double angles 1.6 (2.4 when the back legs
   are longer than half the width), star and cross angles 1.75, bars and
   tubes 1.2; overridable as before. The notes say which coefficient was
   taken and from where; the former *NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE: … take the drag
   factor 1* note stays only for `general` sections (no shape). A gusset
   plate among such members takes at least the flat plate's 2.0.

**Results rise.** The member wind of every structure with members at an
angle to the wind goes up: on the reviewed real towers about +16–24 % with
the inclination law alone (about +10 % for a wind along the line), and
about twice that again with the drag default where no drag was given (the
default was 1 on the projected width, now 2.1 on an angle's longer leg). The synthetic example's
type-02 model with invented angle profiles: +12.4 % (wind across the
faces) and +9.5 % (the other direction) by the law alone, with its drag
1.8; +10.9 % more with the built-in 2.1 on the leg. Benchmarks
`structwind-001` 2910.915 → 3009.235 N (the side diagonals' factor 0.902
for round bars in place of sin²θ = 0.8) and `structwind-002` 2534.427 →
3139.632 N (no factors: drag 1 → 1.2 of Tableau 72, and the law);
`structwind-003` new, the comparison law with drag 1, 2534.427 N (the
former value). Unit tests with sin²θ expectations moved to the new law
(the cantilever at 45°: 0.85/1.2 of the normal force in place of 0.5).
Code: `ohl_structures_fe::wind_law` (one function for every caller: the
line's structure check, `ohl structures fe`, OHL-Structure's wind on the
body, validation); theory [Inclination
factor](../theory/structure-wind.md#inclination-factor) and [Force
coefficient](../theory/structure-wind.md#force-coefficient-when-no-drag-is-given).

**Redundant members, climbing, local displacements, tension-only notes,
read-only CLI, the 60 N/m ice above 1000 m** (owner, after a review of a
real line's redundant members: "go ahead with your recommendations", then
"for the 60 it should only be applied above 1000m"). Built (not approved
yet):

- **The unexplained gap on a cross-arm's plan bracing** (a review on a
  private line, proposal (d)): found, nothing changed. The candidates were
  tried one by one on the whole tower — the angle frames' bending axes
  (principal u/v with the principal angle added to the roll, instead of the
  geometric y/z OpenOHL uses), tension-only beams as frames, every truss a
  frame, no roll: each changes the bracing's force by at most 0.1 kN. The
  cause is an interior joint lying in the plane of its members (the
  crossing of two redundant lines): the other program puts a share of the
  section's weight on it and its pinned members carry it by sagging (29
  mm), the tension pulls the chord joints together and compresses the plan
  bracing; OpenOHL holds that joint's out-of-plane direction by its joint
  stabilisation. With the joint lowered by the other program's sag
  OpenOHL gives nearly its force; with the members as frames (bending, the
  real continuous angles) the bracing stays nearly unstressed (−1.6 kN
  against OpenOHL's −1.25 and the other program's −5.05). No clear
  modelling error and no primary source to change anything: the member
  results stay; the residual (the membrane share OpenOHL's stabilisation
  leaves out, about 2 % of usage there) is said in the private review.
- **Optional redundant-member force**, off by default: `[analysis]
  redundant_force` (percent): each redundant member also checked for that
  share of the compression in the member it braces — the member passing
  straight through its end joint (within 10°), found from the model; its
  usage the larger, what governs says which; not found: said, not on the
  safe side. ASCE 10-97 commentary C3.7.4 (PDF p. 45): "Common design
  practice is to design redundant members for 1 to 2.5% of the load in the
  supported member" — practice, not a requirement, so the percentage is
  the user's. Model file 7, structure file 16.
- **Optional climbing load**, off by default: `[analysis] climbing_load`:
  members within 30° of the horizontal, the load at mid-length alone,
  simply supported, own weight added, against first yield (ASCE 10-97
  commentary C2.2, PDF p. 38: 1100 N "applied independently of all other
  loads without permanent distortion"); a list of its own, not in the load
  cases' usage. Steeper members not checked (said).
- **A joint moving far against its own members**: a warning (not a
  refusal) when a joint moves more than 10 % of its members' mean length
  relative to the mean of their other ends — the sagging grillage the
  structure-wide limit (half its size) did not see. The mean, not the
  shortest member: on the real towers the shortest (a 0.25 m link to an
  attachment point) flagged a joint that moves with the tower.
- **Tension-only notes**: the default law names itself ("tension-only
  members (compression up to their buckling load): …"); a joint held by the
  stabilisation where its shortened tension-only members would hold it is
  named in a warning (within the limits, not refused, no longer quiet).
- **The command line opens project files read-only** for every command
  that only reads or computes (`Session::open_read_only`: no journal mode,
  no table, nothing written; immutable when no program has the file open,
  so no `-wal`/`-shm`; an older file upgraded in memory only). The review
  had found `ohl line` changing a real project's modification time.
- **"0 °C + 60 N/m ice"** added to the default load cases (vertical 1.3, as
  the 20 N/m case) and given **only to structures at or above 1000 m**: a
  new structure-group rule, the ground elevation (the structure's position
  height; unknown: matches, the safe side), and a load case's own list may
  now have rules (its case only where they hold). A group "above 1000 m"
  ticking only that case was not used: a structure in a group takes only
  its groups' cases, so those structures would have lost every other case;
  the own list restricts that one case and nothing else. New projects with
  the defaults and Add the default cases… put the own list in the line; a
  line without it gives the case to every structure (more load). Line file
  still version 18 (groups and own lists are unreleased).

**Default weather and load cases** (owner): "can you have in the software
by default a few weather cases like -20° 0° 10° 20° 40° 80° 10° + 300Pa
wind and 0° + 20N/m Ice and 0° + 60 N/m ice then also have some default
load cases for pylons like -20°, 10°, 40°, 10° + 300 Pa wind left, and
right and 0° + 20N/m ice with a factor 1.5 on wind for the pylons and 1.3
on the ice. these values are arbitrary but needed to check the codes. also
i would like to have the option to have wind along the line forward and
backward to test the pylons." Built (not approved yet):

- Shipped as `libraries/weather/default-weather-cases.ohlwc` (nine cases)
  and `libraries/loadcases/default-load-cases.ohllc` (eight, file version
  4), embedded in `ohl_weather::default_cases` and
  `ohl_loads::default_load_cases`. Every description says "default case,
  arbitrary values for checking (not from a design code)": the values are
  the owner's, not a standard's.
- The ice cases give no density (the owner gave none): glaze ice, the
  smallest iced diameter for the weight — NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for the
  clearances to the iced surface, said in their descriptions (they have
  no wind, so the table's note does not show for them).
- "1.5 on wind for the pylons": `transverse = 1.5` and `[case.structure]
  wind_factor = 1.5`; "1.3 on the ice": `vertical = 1.3`. The factors act
  on components, not actions, so each is above a factor on the action
  alone (the pull at a line angle, the wires' own weight): on the safe
  side. Every case `condition = "initial"` (none given; needs no
  creep-stretch criteria), strength 1. The ice case puts no ice on the
  structure bodies (an ice load per metre is no thickness for a
  structure).
- **Wind along the line**: the cases `… wind ahead` and `… wind back`
  put 300 Pa × 1.5 on the structure bodies from ahead / from behind
  (`[case.structure] direction`, the case's own `wind_pressure`) and **no
  wind on the wires**: they name the still weather case `10 °C`. The
  program models the wind on the wires across the line only; giving the
  wires the cross wind in a wind-along-the-line case would be a wind they
  do not get. No format change was needed (a `wires_wind = false` field
  was considered and not made: the existing format says it). Left out,
  NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE and said in the case's notes (a new note for a
  body-only wind case): the spans' share at a line angle, the strings',
  jumpers' and posts' wind along the line; the wind bands' one area (the
  one across) is taken, as before. The body pressure is written twice
  (the weather case and the load case): change both together. A weather
  case with wind at any angle is being planned separately.
- **Where**: File › New project… has the tick "Start with the default
  weather and load cases (arbitrary values for checking)", on by default,
  for the empty project (the two files) and the starter template (the
  default cases added to its own two files, so every load case names a
  weather case of the project). Existing projects: **Add the default
  cases…** in Line › Criteria › Weather cases (new rows, Apply keeps them:
  one change) and in the Load cases library (after a look at what it adds
  and at the weather cases the project lacks; Save keeps them: one
  change); by name, never replacing a case. The command line is unchanged
  (no weather file: its one case of `--temperature`); the files are given
  with `--weather` / `--load-cases`.
- The tutorial unticks the defaults (it works with the starter's five
  weather cases and its screenshots).

**Wind at any direction** (owner). Asked: *"it would be nice to be able
to have in the weather cases the possibility to have any angle with 0°
being along the alignment and 90° right of the alignment and a given value
of wind"*; on the drafted plan: *"yes go ahead and the current cases need
to be identical. (please add an option for the friction on the wire."*;
then *"On the display weather cases in view, the wind will not have left
or right anymore but the angles and the name should be written to
correspond to the old weather cases."* and *"Also don't forget the theory
page about the wind"*. Decided, all of the plan's 15 questions as
recommended: the angle names where the wind comes **from**, 0° from
ahead, 90° from the right, clockwise, relative to the line at each place
(the bisector at an angle point); no direction, `right`/90° and
`left`/270° keep today's across rule bit for bit; a wind at an angle loads
each span with its normal part by the projected area (q·D·sin θ, the
default) or the cross-flow principle (q·D·sin² θ, the option), with the
vertical part on inclined spans; a **friction along the wire** as an
option, off by default, with the user's coefficient (no value given by
the program); the direction in the weather case (weather file version 2)
and per load case with sets of directions (load case file version 7, the
worst kept); the bodies take the wires' direction, in a turned
structure's axes; old body angles (load case files up to 6, 0° from the
right) kept as read, θ = 90° − θ_old, the same forces bit for bit;
OHL-Structure keeps its convention, the link converts; the display shows
each case as it is or mirrored (across: from the right, 90°, from the
left, 270°) or both. Built (not approved yet): phases P1–P3 of the plan
and the display; P4 (the clearance checks with a direction and its
mirror) and the rest of P5 (arrows, the load case form's wind direction,
the command line) to come. Every existing case gives identical results:
proved on the example lines against the program before the change (a
test with digests of every number written). The single theory page:
[Wind on the line](../theory/wind.md). The default cases'
*wind ahead* and *wind back* (below) became real winds along the line on
the wires too (see the entry for the defaults).

**Tension-only members: a per-model setting for their compression**
(owner). The owner first asked that "the tension only members should be
assumed to hold no compression, not even until buckling". Made the rule
for every model and measured on a real line, it broke 31 of 73 towers
(attachment joints held only by tension-only members), so the owner
chose: "Add a per-model analysis setting… compression up to buckling
(today, the default) or no compression. You can switch a model to no
compression and see the towers that then lose a support, named. Nothing
changes for existing models until you switch." Built (not approved yet):
`[analysis] tension_compression = "buckling"` (the default, the decision
of 2026-10-19 with the design-resistance cap of 2026-11-08) or `"none"`
(slack as soon as shortened) in structure models (version 6) and
structure types (version 14), each written at that version only when the
key is given; OHL-Structure's Analysis row *tension-only: no
compression* (one undoable edit); `ohl structures fe
--tension-compression`; OHL-Design's structure usage takes the type's
setting through its model. "none" is on the safe side for the members
the tension-only ones relieved (they take the compression), not a bound
for every member of an indeterminate structure (said in the theory); a joint held only by shortened
tension-only members is then held by nothing — held within the
stabilisation's limits and listed, refused beyond them naming the joints,
the refusal adding that the tension-only members carry no compression.
The notes and a slack member's usage say the law used ("tension-only
members (no compression): …", "slack (no compression)"). Benchmark
structfe-016 (the X panel set to none); structfe-011 and every test of
the default unchanged ([theory](../theory/structures-fe.md#tension-only-members-compression-up-to-their-buckling-load-or-none),
[user guide](../user-guide/structure-analysis.md#tension-only-members)).

**Galloping ellipses made safe** (owner, answering the review's open
points: "make it safe"). Built, in active development, not approved
yet:

- **Every loop's middle is a station**: the ellipses are compared at
  the `stations − 1` even stations and at the middle of each of the
  method's loops (`galloping::stations_of`), so the largest ellipse is
  always compared. Before, the middles of 3, 4 and 6 to 9 loops fell
  between the 20 default stations (98.8 % of the ellipse for 3 loops,
  95.1 % for 4), said not on the safe side; that note is gone.
- **The larger sag**: each span's sag is the larger of the solve's
  vertical sag and the sag in the swung wire's plane
  (`galloping::swung_sag`: the largest distance from the chord square to
  the span, across and vertically together). Without wind they are the
  same; with wind the swung plane's is the larger. The note about the
  vertical sag of swung wires is gone.
- **Not checked rather than guessed**: a pair whose voltage is above a
  requirement table by voltage is not checked (no row, never a pass), as
  the internal clearances check does for a voltage beyond its table —
  before, the table's last row was taken; a wire whose type is not in the
  library (no diameter) is not checked by a method whose axes use the
  diameter — before, computed with d = 0. Both said: *NOT CHECKED: …*
  (`galloping::unchecked`, `galloping::notes`); the window's verdict is
  red while any pair is not checked.
- On the example line (`ohl clearance galloping` on
  `examples/synthetic-line`, 1 and 2 loops at 20 stations, glaze ice
  without wind) the results are unchanged. With the same coefficients for
  3 and 4 loops the smallest gaps fall (glaze ice, S1–S2 in their
  second span: 5.28 → 5.20 m for 3 loops, 5.50 → 5.22 m for 4); in the
  case *rime ice + wind* the ellipses grow with the swung plane's sag
  (S1's major axis there 11.43 → 12.39 m) and the gaps fall (4 loops
  6.61 → 5.95 m); a table ending at 60 kV leaves the four 220 kV pairs
  not checked (before: checked at the last row's 0.3 m).
- Validation: `galloping-005…007` (a whole span of 3 and 4 loops
  compared at the loops' middles, a swung wire sized from the sag in its
  plane), new calculation `galloping.span`.

**Lightning shielding: a cross-section at each structure** (owner: "yes
if fast else only as today"). Each span is now cut at its two structures
too, beside the middle of each step; at a structure a wire whose clamp
lies within half a step of the plane (a suspension string swung along
the line, a short strain string) is taken at its clamp
(`cross_section::cross_section_at_structure`); the cut stands for the
quarter step next to the structure. Measured on the example
(`examples/lightning`, both rules, a release build, 20 runs each
alternating): 2.5 % more computing time (0.28 s against 0.29 s), under
0.02 s more — kept. On the 5 m step the lengths exposed are unchanged
(144.4 m), the worst places move onto the structures and r_max grows a
little (46.5 → 47.1 m); at a 100 m step, where the cuts in the spans lie
38.75 m to 50 m from the structures, the 8 kA sphere found no phase
exposed before and finds 6 now. The *NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE* note on the
step now says what is still missed: an exposure shorter than a step
between two cross-sections away from the structures. The cuts at the
structures are marked (`Cut::at_structure`, in `ohl lightning --json`;
the window's cross-section title says *at structure …*).

**Which structures take a case: manual, where the case is defined, per
position** (owner: "Okay for automatic grouping but manual should always
be available where load cases rules are defined and on which pylon they
apply with a list of them. Not per type but per position: if 2 pylons are
the same type they can still get different load cases based on the
location." Accepted as built: old sets read with the union; the angle
rule the largest over the alignments; dead end = a section ends there;
no height or elevation rule for now). Built, in active development, not
approved yet:

- **The Load cases form's section 8 Applies to**: every structure of the
  line in the line's order (id, station on its alignment, type) with how
  it gets the case — through a group, picked or by a rule (the rule in
  words), in no group (every case), picked here, excluded here — ticked
  when it takes it; a tick list as elsewhere (search, All / None / Invert
  on the rows shown, press-and-drag, shift for a range) and *Add / Remove
  the N selected* from the Structures table or a view. A case taken by no
  structure is said in the warning colour.
- **One model, no second concept: a load case's own list** — a structure
  group with `load_case` set (no name, no rules, no other case; one per
  case), shown in Load cases per group as *wind (own list)*. Its picked
  structures take the case **on top of** their groups' cases; its
  **excluded** structures do not take it, whatever their groups give. It
  does not count as a group for "in no group: every case", so it only
  ever adds its case or takes away exactly that case (the safe side: a
  structure never loses another case through it). Ticking writes it
  (`Line::give_case`): tick → picked (an exclusion taken away); untick →
  taken out of the picks, and **excluded** when a group (by rule or by
  pick) or being in no group still gives the case — the status line names
  the rule and says "change the rule in Load cases per group, or keep the
  exclusion". The groups and their rules are never changed from the form.
  Each change (a click, a drag, a button) is one command, one undo, in
  both windows (the groups window's own-list view uses the same command).
- **An exclusion is never hidden**: the case's list, the groups window
  (the own list's row and lists; *Who is in* in the warning colour), the
  Structures table (*— wind excluded in the own list*, *no group: every
  case but wind …*), the Properties (warning colour) and OHL-Structure's
  status block. Excluded from every case it had: *takes no load case*,
  listed as not checked. A case renamed in the library renames its own
  list in the same command (joined to an own list the new name had: picks
  kept); a deleted case's own list stays, in the error colour, its picked
  structures said not checked in it.
- **Per position, not per type**: picking (in a group or in a case's own
  list) is the first way in both windows; the groups window's rules are
  titled *5 Rules (optional)*, an automatic helper. No UI path assigns
  cases per type only.
- **Formats**: a structure group's `load_case` and `excluded`, its `name`
  optional on an own list — in the line file, the project's
  `structure_groups` row and OHL XML (`<structure_group load_case>` with
  `<excluded id/>`, the XSD) — in the same, unreleased line file version
  18 (a line with any group is written at 18 already). `CaseSet::EveryBut`
  (in no group, excluded from some cases), `CaseSets::why` / `takers` /
  `picked_for` / `excluded_from` / `excluded` / `own_list`.
- **Fault fixed:** renaming a structure picked in a structure group was
  refused in a project with an internal error (the groups' settings row
  was sent as a nested batch); now the group follows the new name, as do
  an own list's picks and exclusions (tested).

**Structure flexibility in the line solve: plan approved, phases 0–2
built** (owner, on the plan for calculation levels 3 and 4: "keep the
larger of rigid and flexible, otherwise your recommendations"). Decided:
calculation level 3
first, level 4 on the same loop; wires and structures coupled by an
iteration on the attachment points' displacements (each keeps its own
solver), not one combined model; the drawn geometry is the structure as
strung; level 3's matrix is the tangent at the stringing state; three
translations per attachment point with every coupling between points;
the structure's own wind and ice included; the interaction at unfactored
loads, the load case's factors on the resulting forces; one line setting
with a per-run override (later per check and per structure group);
structures without a computable model rigid and listed; internal
clearances rigid until the structure body is drawn deflected; a case
whose iteration does not converge fails; a structure failing at level 4
is reported failing and taken linear; the whole line coupled; ruling-span
sections rigid; a pole fixed at the ground line, said not on the safe
side; the default stays rigid. **Structure loads and usage are never
below rigid**: the structure check keeps, per structure, point and case,
the larger of the rigid and the flexible result, the change shown; the
other results take the flexible solve where it is less favourable, or
check both. Calculation level (1–4: rigid … full coupled) is kept apart
from a structure's detail level. Built (internal, no setting, no result
changed): the theory page [Structure flexibility in the line
solve](../theory/structure-flexibility.md) (phase 0); a structure, a pole
and a placed structure condensed to their attachment points by static
condensation of the tangent at a reference state, with the reasons a
structure stays rigid and a memo key (phase 1,
`ohl_structures_fe::condense`, `ohl-loads` `flexibility`; the structure
check's point mapping now one function shared with it,
`Model::attachment_load`); a section solved with its structure points
moved and its stiffness there (phase 2, `ohl_wirefe::Model::support_stiffness`,
`Coupling::moved`, `SectionShape::support_stiffness`; without a move,
bit for bit as before). Found on the way: the condensed stiffness does
not exist when two points sit on one rigid link (their flexibility is
singular), so the loop is planned in its flexibility form; a real tower
of some 2300 members with frames takes 0.5–1.2 s to condense (its
reference solve about half), not the tens of milliseconds first
estimated — once per type, extension and reference, kept by its key.

**A jumper-held pivoting post is solved together with its jumper; the
hinge stays frictionless, with an optional friction** (owner's answers to
the two questions left by the pivoting post below: *"No friction moment"*;
*"Should the jumper be solved together with the post? — yes"*; then, on the
hinge, *"keep that written for the pylon but keep it frictionless for now
with an option to add it if needed"*).

- **Solved together** (`post::jumper_pivots`, `post::settle_turn`,
  `jumper::couple_pivots`): a pivoting post holding jumpers' ends only has
  one degree of freedom, its turn about its free line; for each turn every
  jumper ending at its top is solved again by the jumper solver with that
  end on the turned clamp (`jumper::TapContext::moved`), the clamp's fixed
  exit direction turned with the post, and the post settles where its hinge
  holds the moment about the axis of the jumpers' pull and moment, half its
  members' weight and wind and a counterweight — found from where it is
  given, stepping out the way that moment drives it and then the Illinois
  method: the first (stable) balance on its way. Posts sharing a jumper are
  settled in turn, pass after pass. Exit clauses: a whole turn without a
  balance, 120 evaluations, 20 passes — then not solved, said, loads not
  computed. The jumpers' shapes are those with the post settled
  (`JumperShape::pivots`); the post's and brace's forces the statics at
  that top (`post::hinged_post_loads`), the jumper's own pull taken there
  whatever the jumper loads option (one state with the balance). The
  decoupled model and its note (NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for the forces'
  directions in plan) are gone. Hand check and benchmark tbins-007
  (against an independent quadrature catenary and bisection): a jumper
  without bending stiffness to a point fixed at (3, −2.5, 9) m turns the
  post to \( \arctan(3/2.5) = 50.194° \) (the top, the axis and that point
  in one vertical plane), to 10⁻⁶ degrees; the decoupled model gave
  71.57°. A pull towards a point inside the post's circle, which the
  decoupled model refused, now settles (the jumper's length holds it). In
  the loads test (wind 500 Pa, the jumper across the line) the post
  settles about 107° round — the structure's body in the way of so large a
  turn is not modelled (said in the theory).
- **The jumper's wind with the post turned** keeps the direction and size
  it has on the jumper as given: the full pressure square to the jumper in
  plan, turned with it, drives the post round without end (found: no
  balance within a whole turn) — no real wind does that; the full pressure
  kept is on the safe side for the jumper's swing.
- **Rigid jumpers** (tubes) ending at a pivoting post: a rigid jumper holds
  the post as a brace would, with a force along it its model does not
  carry: not solved, said. A jumper's support clamp on a pivoting post's
  strings is solved within that jumper (the hinged post now pushes there as
  well as pulls; before it hung as a tension-only string — not on the safe
  side).
- **A cable jumper's end forces are exact** (`ElementState::force_i`,
  `force_j`): before, its tension along the first and last of its 64
  pieces, off by up to half a piece's turn (~0.5° on a slack jumper) —
  found while checking the coupled balance against the reference.
- **Hinge friction** (`hinge_friction_nm`, N·m, a hinged post's; line file
  version **19**, `.ohls` **15** — each written only when a string gives
  one): frictionless by default (the owner's choice: safe for the post and
  for its swing); with a value, **stick and slip** about the free line from
  where the post is given in every solve — the hinge holds the post there
  while the moment needed is at most the friction, else the post turns
  until the moment is the friction. In a section (`solve::with_hinge_friction`):
  a stiff bar across the post holds a sticking one, a force
  \( M_f/\rho \) across it a slipping one, at most 12 solves. The hinge's
  force and moment reach the structure at the post's base
  (`solve::Support::moment`, `SectionShape::hinges`; with jumpers
  `PivotTurn::hinge_moment`); the string check compares the hinge's moment
  with the post's cantilever rating (\( M/h \)). The note for the pylon
  stays — frictionless: NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for the longitudinal load (a
  hinge that sticks passes part of the pull difference into the
  structure); with a friction: the longitudinal load includes the hinge's
  moment up to that value, NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE where the real hinge holds
  more. Not modelled: a friction moment depending on the pin's load, and
  the order of the cases. UI: Add post / string form (**hinge friction**)
  and OHL-Structure's post column (**friction**), each with a hover saying
  its effect.
- **Unchanged** (the tests above, bit for bit where they ran before):
  fixed posts, posts a section holds without a friction, posts held by two
  braces off the line.

**A pivoting post is held by what is attached to it** (owner: "Pivoting
should simply be tied to the jumper or piece it's attached to. And while
nothing is attached to it it should just move freely. It's not the best
solution but it should represent the truth. If braced then some degrees
of freedom are locked."; the question found earlier today below). A
hinged post turns about its hinge freely in every direction its braces
leave free; with one brace (or braces in line with its base) it turns
about the line through their bases.

- **Cause of the failure found**: in a section in the blocks (strung by
  tension, rolled over sheaves in every weather case) each clamp's
  assembly was solved alone under the sheave's pull; a post and one brace
  taken as a V there have nothing holding them along the line about a
  vertical axis (no weight to swing them back, as a hanging V has), so
  that solve turned the post without end and the rolling never settled.
- **Model chosen**: the section's solve already holds the post's top as
  the owner decided — a free node held by the post and brace as bars and
  by the wire clamped there: it swings along the line until the spans'
  pulls balance, as a suspension string swings (`solve::Shape::Pivot`,
  `pivot_axis`). Only the sharing in the blocks changes: there the post
  is taken where it is given to point (`pivot_back`), the swing comes in
  the solve that follows. Hand check (`ohl-line` `pivot_tests`): two
  level spans clipped in with 0.3 m more wire in the first, a 1.5 m level
  post braced from straight above its base — 5.70° of swing (14.9 cm
  along the line), the bisection on two elastic catenaries and the solve
  agree to 1 µm, the post's and brace's forces to 10⁻⁶. The example line
  with the braced shape on type-02 (T2, T4) now solves in every weather
  case (swings of up to 5 mm there: the spans' pulls nearly balance).
- **A jumper only on its top**: the post and brace solved alone under the
  jumper's pull (`post::hinged_alone`), turned first to the stable balance
  (the pull's part across the free line pointing away from it; along the
  line only: as given); before, the jumper's load was shared equally
  between their two bases as for plain strings — not the statics of a
  post and brace (the brace carries some 1.4 times the load at 45°): not
  on the safe side. The jumper is not solved again with the post swung:
  said with every case (NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for the forces' directions in
  plan where it swings far). Where the pull points back towards the hinge
  nothing near its position holds it: its loads not computed, said.
- **Nothing on its top**: free; its loads are not computed and every case
  and the string checks say so (`post::free_hinged_posts`) — before,
  nothing was said (its and its brace's weight silently missing).
- **The hinge is frictionless**: NOT ON THE SAFE SIDE for the structure's
  longitudinal load (a hinge that sticks passes part of the spans'
  difference into it), said with every case for each pivoting post a
  section ends at (`post::pivoting_notes`).
- **Unchanged**: fixed posts, hinged posts held by two braces off the
  line (their holder is not a pivot), every other string; in the
  simplified sharing (equal H) and the stringing reference a pivoting post
  was turned back across the line as a V and is now turned back to where
  it is given to point (the same for a post given across the line). No
  file changes.

**"Unstable" says where**: a finite-element solve failing as unstable
(compression above the elastic buckling load) now names the joints its
buckling mode moves most and the members in compression at the first —
before, it said nowhere where. Found on a real tower model whose plan
bracing (all its members in one horizontal plane, held across it only by
the bending of thin angles modelled as frames) buckled under a few kN;
how to treat such joints is to be decided.

**A moment only where a member that is always a frame meets the joint**:
an attachment's offset moment (or a post's) at a joint only tension-only
members that bend (or trusses) meet is left out and said NOT ON THE SAFE
SIDE; before, it was put there and the solve refused the case once those
members were bowed or slack.
